## Amendment 369 (2026-09-18 02:00) - THE BULK CONDITION SOLVED AT TWO ORDERS, AND THEY BRACKET THE MEASUREMENT:
## second order gives X* = 1.122, fourth order gives 1.88-1.98, and the certified profiles sit at 1.7004
## (Gaussian) / 1.6507 (binomial). The series is not converged at the working point - which is the
## non-perturbative character of 345, now with numbers on both sides.
(1) THE MACHINERY, VALIDATED (q270). The deficit density L = P(rho) F with P = exp(-b rho^2) and F the measured
gradient expansion is autonomous, so the fourth-order Beltrami invariant H = sum_k sum_j (-1)^j rho_{k-j} D^j
(dL/drho_k) - L obeys H + mu rho = E with the count constrained. P varies by exp(24) along the bulk while E and
mu rho are of that same tiny order, so the BRACKET must vanish: H/P = 0 is the bulk condition, and it is the
E = 0 branch that 359 identified. Evaluated on the first-integral profile (rho_1 = c/rho^2, rho_2 = -2c^2/rho^5,
rho_3 = 10c^3/rho^8, rho_4 = -80c^4/rho^11, rho_5 = 880c^5/rho^14, c = sqrt(X/kappa_AM)), H/P is a function of
rho and X and its root is X*. AT SECOND ORDER the solver returns
        X* = 1.2076, 1.1807, 1.1542, 1.1332, 1.1216, 1.1106, 1.1026  at rho = 0.66 ... 0.90,
and 1.1216 at rho = 0.8333 is exactly 1/c_1 = 1/0.89156 = 1.12163, the analytic second-order answer of 364. The
machinery is therefore correct.
(2) AT FOURTH ORDER, with all five fourth-order coefficients measured at ten densities (368(1)) and fitted to
degree five (rms of the fits 1e-6 to 1 against spreads of 1e2 to 2e5):
        rho = 0.66: X* = 1.8804     rho = 0.70: X* = 1.9827     rho >= 0.75: no root in [0.15, 8]
(the bracket stays negative at the higher densities). So the fourth-order truncation overshoots where it has a
root and loses it where it does not.
(3) THE READING. Consecutive truncations give 1.12 and 1.88-1.98; the measurement is 1.7004 +- 0.0097 (Gaussian)
and 1.6507 +- 0.0154 (binomial). The measured value lies BETWEEN consecutive truncations, which is the signature
of an asymptotic series whose terms at the working point are of order one - exactly what 345 established by a
different route (kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 = 1.7 means the gradient term EQUALS the local term) and what 362(4)
quantified (3 c_2 X^2 = -0.58 against c_1 X = 1.58). The expansion is doing what it should; it is simply being
evaluated where it has no small parameter.
(4) THE WAY ROUND IT, pre-registered. Every term of H is a partial derivative of L with respect to some rho_k,
and L is computable EXACTLY by quadrature (|J|^2, 364(1)) for any set of derivative values. So H can be evaluated
numerically WITHOUT any expansion: take the first-integral profile at a given (rho, X), compute dL/drho_k by
central differences of the quadrature, compute their total x-derivatives by evaluating at neighbouring points
along the profile (where every rho_k is a known function of rho), assemble H, and solve H/P = 0 for X. The only
approximation left is the finite-difference accuracy, which is controllable. Readings fixed beforehand: the exact
H gives X* within 3 % of 1.70 at every density in 0.66-0.90 => the project's central number is DERIVED, with the
kernel offset the only remaining structure; it gives a value far from 1.70, or one that drifts strongly with
rho => either the deficit of the bulk is not int |J|^2 alone (the wall enters, as 368(3) showed it does for the
total) or the first-integral profile is not the exact solution of the exact bulk equation, and the next question
is which.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) is a seven-digit validation of the machinery against an independently derived
number; (2) and (3) are an honest negative about the expansion's convergence, not about the framework.

(1) THE EVALUATION (q271, the instrument pre-registered in 369(4)). Every term of the fourth-order Beltrami

computable exactly by quadrature, so H needs no expansion: the partials come from central differences in each
rho_k, their total x-derivatives from a degree-six polynomial fit to the partials evaluated at nine points along
the first-integral profile. Result, as H/P:
   rho      X = 1.0    1.4      1.7      2.0      2.4      root
   0.70    -0.3228  -0.1452  -0.0458  +0.0253  +0.0767   1.8933
   0.8333  -0.3326  -0.1432  -0.1022  -0.0584  -0.0700   none (the bracket turns back before crossing)
   0.90    -0.2203  -0.1205  -0.0658  -0.2490  -0.2340   none, and NON-MONOTONE: the stencil for the third
                                                          x-derivative is noisy at this density
(2) WHAT IT MEANS, and what it does not. The exact bracket's root (1.893 at rho = 0.70) sits with the
fourth-order expansion's (1.88-1.98, 369(2)) and NOT with the measurement (1.7004 +- 0.0097 Gaussian, 1.6507 +-
0.0154 binomial). So the 11 % gap is not the expansion's truncation error - the exact evaluation reproduces the
truncation, which incidentally validates the expansion at fourth order. The gap is between the ripple functional's
own stationary profile and the certified comb's profile.
(3) THE TWO BRANCHES, and which survives. 369(4) fixed them: the wall enters the bulk equation, or the
first-integral profile is not the exact bulk solution. The second is excluded by measurement: the certified
states' rho^2 rho' is constant to 1.5 % (Gaussian) and 0.4 % (binomial) over a 1.75-fold range of density (351),
so the profile IS the first-integral one. For the first, the constrained form H = E - mu rho can be tested
directly: at X = 1.7 the measured bracket is -0.046 at rho = 0.70 and -0.102 at rho = 0.8333, so
H = P x bracket = -1.8e-10 and -1.2e-13 - a ratio of 1500 where E - mu rho is affine in rho and rho changes by
19 %. So the multipliers CANNOT absorb it either. Both stated branches fail, which leaves a third that 369 did
not consider: the deficit density of the bulk is int |J|^2 (verified exactly on a ring, 364(1)) but the bulk of a
WALLED comb is not a free slice of that functional - the wall fixes not only the count but the profile's
endpoint, and a fixed-endpoint variation has no Beltrami invariant at all, only the Euler-Lagrange equation with
its multiplier.
(4) WHAT IS SOLID AFTER THIS NIGHT, stated plainly because the derivation line has now produced one clean result
and one clean failure. SOLID: the deficit is exactly the ripple's mean square (364(1), ratio 1.00000 over six
orders); the saddle expansion and its coefficients, the second-order pair to seven digits and the fourth-order
set at ten densities (364, 368(1)); the first-order gradient coefficient kappa_eff/kappa_AM = 1 - 3/(4 pi^2
rho^2) + 3/(64 pi^4 rho^4) = 0.8915, matching the ring's independent energy measurement of 0.887-0.912; the comb's
advantage is at the WALL, worth 0.0194 nats against its own envelope (368(3)). NOT SOLID: any derivation of X*,
which is what the project's central number is. Two independent routes (the expansion and the exact bracket) agree
with each other at 1.89 and disagree with the measurement at 1.70.
(5) NEXT, PRE-REGISTERED. Test (3)'s third branch on the object where it can be tested: the certified profile
itself. The Euler-Lagrange equation with a multiplier, delta D/delta rho(x) = mu, can be evaluated exactly on the
certified K = 70 state's own density (not on an idealised first-integral profile) using the same |J|^2 quadrature
and a localised bump, at several bulk points. Readings fixed beforehand: delta D/delta rho is constant to a few
percent along the certified bulk => the ripple functional IS the bulk's variational principle, the multiplier is
the wall's imprint, and X* follows from it with no Beltrami identity needed; it varies strongly => the bulk
deficit of a walled comb is not int |J|^2 over the bulk, and the next object is the wall's contribution to the
bulk equation, which is a genuinely new question.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) and (3) are a negative result with both of its pre-registered branches excluded by

## Amendment 371 (2026-09-18 04:00) - THE KERNEL OFFSET IS THE WALL'S FINGERPRINT: two states with IDENTICAL

(1) THE COMPARISON. X* measured directly from the bulk gaps, beside the first four gaps from the wall:
   Gaussian K = 70        X* = 1.7004 +- 0.0097    chain 2.7188, 2.1696, 1.9352, 1.7901
   binomial K = 68 n = 865 X* = 1.6507 +- 0.0154   chain 3.1260, 2.2616, 1.9838, 1.8231
   binomial K = 58 n = 666 X* = 1.6318 +- 0.0250   chain 3.1261, 2.2620, 1.9843, 1.8237
The two binomial states have the same chain to five digits - the chain is a wall property (statement 293) - and
their X* agree within their scatter: 1.64 +- 0.02. The Gaussian's chain differs in its first gap by 15 % and its
X* differs by 3.4 %. So X* tracks the WALL, not the bulk: two states of the same channel at different K and
different amplitude share it, and a channel with a different wall does not.
(2) WHY THAT MATTERS NOW. 370 left one surviving explanation for the 11 % gap between the ripple functional's own
stationary profile (X = 1.89, by two independent routes) and the certified combs (1.70): a walled comb's bulk is
not a free slice of that functional, because the wall fixes the profile's endpoint and the total's stationarity
carries a term from the wall's response to the bulk's shape. (1) is that hypothesis's signature, and it was
sitting in the record since 329 as the unexplained "kernel offset" of +0.021 in kappa_eff/kappa_AM. It is not a
kernel effect at all: it is the wall's.
(3) WHAT IT PREDICTS, and how to test it. If X* is set by matching the bulk to the wall, then (a) any two states
with the same wall chain have the same X* regardless of K and A - true for the two binomial states here, and
consistent with the Gaussian's own K-independence (351: eleven Gaussian states, X* constant to 1.3 %); (b) the
Poisson channel, whose wall chain differs again, should have its own X*, measurable from the certified Poisson
states already in the record; (c) a comb with an ARTIFICIAL wall - the same bulk law terminated by a chain of
imposed gaps - should shift X* by an amount computable from the chain. (b) is free: the Poisson states exist.
Pre-registered reading: the Poisson X* differs from both and correlates with its chain's first gap => the wall
fingerprint is established across three channels; it equals one of them without matching the chain => the
correlation in (1) is a coincidence of two channels and the explanation fails.
(4) THE BINOMIAL'S NUMBER. With the two binomial states averaged, X* = 1.64 +- 0.02, against zeta(2) =
pi^2/6 = 1.64493. That remains a candidate closed form for THAT channel's wall, now with a reason why a channel
could have its own constant rather than sharing a universal one.

WORTH DERIVING - the wall's contribution to the bulk equation is now the single named object between the derived

## Amendment 372 (2026-09-18 05:30) - 370's EXACT BELTRAMI BRACKET IS WITHDRAWN: it was numerical noise. The
## third total derivative of a numerically differentiated quantity is beyond reach by every route tried, and the
## bracket's own SIGN is unresolved.
(1) THE EVIDENCE. q271 computed the total x-derivatives of the partials dL/drho_k from a nine-point stencil in x.
Varying the stencil step: at rho = 0.75, X = 2.0 the bracket reads -0.0083, -0.0070, +0.0288 at steps 0.3, 0.6,
1.0, and at rho = 0.8333, X = 1.7 it reads -0.0857, -0.1022, -0.0670 - a fifty percent spread and, at the first
point, a sign change. q272 replaced the x-stencil with the analytically cleaner route (every partial is a smooth
function of rho along the profile, and d/dx = rho' d/drho with rho' known exactly, so the derivatives come from
polynomial fits in rho and the chain rule). It is worse: at rho = 0.8333, X = 1.7 the bracket reads +11.99,
+4.74, -1.86 at fit degrees 5, 6, 7. Three successive differentiations amplify the fit's error without bound.
(2) WHAT IS WITHDRAWN. 370's statement that "the exact Beltrami bracket agrees with the fourth-order expansion at
X = 1.89 and disagrees with the certified 1.7004" is withdrawn in full: the exact bracket has not been computed.
With it goes 370(3)'s conclusion that both pre-registered branches were excluded - that argument used the
bracket's values at three densities, and those values are noise.
(3) WHAT SURVIVES. The fourth-order EXPANSION's root (1.88-1.98 where it has one, 369(2)) stands: it is symbolic
in the measured coefficients, with no numerical differentiation. So the record is: second-order truncation 1.122
(validated to seven digits against the analytic 1/c_1), fourth-order truncation 1.88-1.98, measurement 1.7004
(Gaussian) / 1.6507 (binomial) - the measurement between consecutive truncations, which remains 369(3)'s reading
and remains the honest state of the derivation. Also surviving, because it is a correlation in measured data and
not a calculation: 371's wall fingerprint (two binomial states with identical chains share X* = 1.64 +- 0.02; the
Gaussian, whose chain differs by 15 % in its first gap, has 1.7004).
(4) WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK. The obstruction is differentiating a quadrature three times. The way round it is to
never differentiate numerically: extend the SYMBOLIC saddle expansion (q265's route, which stalled on sympy's
series but is mechanical) to sixth order, so that the Beltrami bracket is a polynomial in the derivatives with
analytic coefficients, and use the measured coefficients only as a check at fourth order - where they already
agree to seven digits for the two second-order terms. That is the next computation, and its kill
condition is 369(3)'s: if the sixth-order truncation does not move the root toward 1.70 from 1.88-1.98, the
series is not the route and the wall matching of 371 is.

convergence test we should have run before writing it.

X and the gap; within a single profile X has no systematic drift with g, only scatter. That retires the reading
of 329 as "the coefficient is a function of the local gap" and leaves it as what it measurably is: a correlation
between states' MEAN coefficients and their MEAN gaps.
(2) THE HONEST STRENGTH OF 371. Mean X per state: Gaussian 1.7031, 1.7329, 1.7228 (spread 1.7 %); binomial
1.6544, 1.6377 (spread 1.0 %). Between the channels the separation is 3.4 %. So the wall fingerprint rests on a
separation about twice the within-channel scatter - real, but two sigma, not overwhelming. Anyone reading 371,
374, 375 should read this line with them.
(3) WHY THE POISSON TEST MATTERS MORE AFTER THIS. A single Poisson state carries both chains (376), so its two
sides are compared at the same K, the same amplitude, the same kernel and the same solver tolerance - every
source of the 1.7 % within-channel scatter is removed at once. If the two sides differ by 2-4 % there, the
separation is established on one state instead of on a between-channel average.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) retires a reading of Amendment 329 that has been carried since 8:30 on 17 Sep;
(2) states the evidence's strength in the terms a sceptical reader would use.

## Amendment 378 (2026-09-18 12:30) - WALL ANATOMY: WHY NO POISSON STATE HAS EVER BEEN CERTIFIED, and the port
## that should fix it. The Poisson solver is a plain damped Newton - it never received the soft-mode machinery
## that the Gaussian problem needed from K = 50 onward.
(1) THE WALL. Every Poisson state in the record stops far above the certification bar: results_q193b_poisson_K40
at 1.36e-6, results_q193_poisson_K40 at 4.5e-3, and the tightened rerun (dps 45, tolerance 1e-24, 200 steps)
ended "stuck" at 4.5e-3 with the history 0.8626, 0.216, 0.0691, 0.01348, 0.01215, 0.01185, 0.00573, 0.004514.
Since 307 established that a state above about 1e-20 carries no profile information, the decisive two-sided test
of 376 has never been runnable.
(2) THE MATERIAL. support_mp3.solve takes a plain LU Newton step with a feasibility line search - it has no
singular-value cap, no soft-mode line search and no nested quadratic cycle. Those were built for the GAUSSIAN
problem in Amendments 302-312 precisely because a plain Newton stalls once the Jacobian's smallest singular value
falls below about 1e-9, which the measured ladder (1.40e-6, 4.27e-9, 2.17e-10, 1.85e-11 at K = 26, 40, 50, 60)
puts at K = 40 - exactly the Poisson state being attempted. So the Poisson problem is being solved with the
machinery the Gaussian problem outgrew two hundred amendments ago, and it stalls at the same place for the same
reason. NOT the material: the seed (the same seed converges to 1e-6 in one run and sticks at 4.5e-3 in another,
which is a solver-path difference), and not the precision (dps 45 made no difference).
(3) THE METHOD. Port the cap: support_mp3b.py is support_mp3.py with the SVD-capped step of q206 spliced into the
one line that took the LU step (the coefficient along each right-singular vector is clipped to SVDCAP, and the
exact LU step is used when nothing is clipped), and q193d_poisson_svd.py is the Poisson driver using it. Running
now at SVDCAP = 0.05, 150 steps, tolerance 1e-22. Reading fixed beforehand: residual below 1e-18 => the test of
376 runs and the wall fingerprint is decided on one state; it sticks again above 1e-6 => the cap alone is not
enough and the next port is the nested quadratic cycle, which is the piece that broke the Gaussian's 1e-9 wall.
(4) WHAT IS BEHIND IT. The Poisson channel's X* on both sides of one profile (376), the third chain for the ratio
test of 375b, and - because the Poisson problem is the project's original object - the first certified Poisson
state in the record.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) is the wall anatomy the protocol requires, with the material identified from the
solver's source and the measured singular-value ladder rather than from the symptom.

## Amendment 380 (2026-09-18 14:00) - THE MEASUREMENT WINDOW WAS WRONG, AND FIXING IT CHANGES THE CENTRAL
## NUMBERS: X* = 1.7132 +- 0.0007 (Gaussian) and 1.6662 +- 0.0022 (binomial). The channels separate at TWENTY

(1) THE ERROR. Every X* in this record used the bulk window d in [12, A-8] or [10, A-8], excluding eight units
before the centre. That is not enough: the centre is a symmetry point where rho' vanishes, and its influence

   window        A = 46.3837        46.4487        46.5137        46.5787
   [10, A-8]   1.7022 +- 0.0023  1.6564 +- 0.0210  1.6081 +- 0.0391  1.5579 +- 0.0559
   [10, A-15]  1.7068 +- 0.0020  1.7051 +- 0.0026  1.7024 +- 0.0037  1.6984 +- 0.0055
   [10, A-22]  1.7117 +- 0.0019  1.7107 +- 0.0020  1.7105 +- 0.0020  1.7103 +- 0.0021
At [10, A-8] X* appears to fall by 8 % across the plateau; at [10, A-22] it is CONSTANT to 0.08 %. The whole
apparent amplitude dependence - and 379(3)'s "real 1.2 % within-channel drift", and 377(2)'s "1.7 % scatter" -
was the centre distortion leaking into the window. Only the mid-plateau states were ever clean, which is why

(2) THE CORRECTED NUMBERS (window d in [10, A-22], every certified state with at least five atoms in it):
   Gaussian: 1.7158, 1.7158, 1.7146 (K = 60, three amplitudes); 1.7117, 1.7107, 1.7105, 1.7103 (K = 70, four)
             -> X* = 1.7132 +- 0.0007 over seven states, reduced chi-square 1.98

             -> X* = 1.6662 +- 0.0022 over four states, reduced chi-square 0.05
The binomial's four states, spanning K = 58 to 68 and n = 666 to 865, agree to a reduced chi-square of 0.05: X*
IS one number per channel. The Gaussian's 1.98 reflects a residual 0.3 % difference between K = 60 and K = 70,
which is the only within-channel structure that survives.
(3) THE SEPARATION: 1.7132 - 1.6662 = 0.0470 +- 0.0023, i.e. TWENTY sigma. 377(2)'s "about two sigma" and
379(3)'s "eleven sigma" are both superseded; the wall fingerprint is not a marginal correlation.
(4) TWO CLOSED FORMS EXCLUDED. zeta(2) = pi^2/6 = 1.64493 against the binomial's 1.6662 +- 0.0022 is 9.7 sigma
away; equivalently 6/pi^2 = 0.60793 against 1/X* = 0.6002 +- 0.0008 is 9.6 sigma. The candidate carried since

(5) WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT MUST BE REDONE. Surviving: everything that used the SHAPE of the profile rather than

369, 370 and 373 (which compared 1.88-1.98 and 1.89 against 1.7004 - now against 1.7132, a shift that does not
change their conclusions), and 374's crossing-density arithmetic. The prediction for the Poisson test (376) is

        X*(n) = X_inf + b/n   with   X_inf = 1.6853 +- 0.0059,  b = -14.57 +- 3.67,  reduced chi-square 0.19

## Amendment 383 (2026-09-18 18:15) - WITH AN OBJECTIVE WINDOW AND A COMBINED FIT: the two channels are
## CONSISTENT WITH ONE asymptotic constant, X_inf = 1.6962 +- 0.0031, and the evidence for splitting it sits

(1) THE WINDOW, CHOSEN BY THE DATA (q280). 382(6) left everything limited by our choice of centre exclusion, so
the choice is now made by a criterion: extend the window inward one atom at a time and stop at the last atom for
which the running mean stays within a fixed number of standard errors of the first third's value. Applied to all
nine certified states in both channels at three tolerances (1.0, 1.5, 2.5 sigma), the criterion picks windows
covering 0.50 to 0.72 of the profile and gives
        tolerance   Gaussian X_inf        binomial X_inf        their difference
        1.0 sigma   1.7016 +- 0.0036      1.6904 +- 0.0058      1.6 sigma
        1.5 sigma   1.7003 +- 0.0037      1.6865 +- 0.0059      2.0 sigma
        2.5 sigma   1.6957 +- 0.0049      1.6718 +- 0.0103      2.1 sigma
So the extrapolated constants are stable to 0.3 % against the window rule, and the channel difference is
marginal at every setting - never the 20 sigma of 380, which was a finite-size artefact.
(2) THE FINITE-SIZE LAW IS ROBUST. At every tolerance and in both channels, a CONSTANT fit is rejected: reduced
chi-squares of 7.5 to 8.6 against 0.01 to 0.5 for the 1/size fit. The slopes are +0.7 to +1.1 in 1/K (Gaussian)
and -18 to -23 in 1/n (binomial). That X* depends on the state's size, and in opposite directions in the two
channels, is the firm result of this line.
(3) THE COMBINED FIT, which is the right test of universality. Fitting all nine states with a SHARED X_inf and
separate slopes (three parameters):
        X_inf = 1.6962 +- 0.0031,  a = +0.97 (Gaussian, in 1/K),  b = -22.99 (binomial, in 1/n),
        reduced chi-square 0.82, residuals -0.5, +1.1, +0.8, +0.4, +1.1, -0.4, -0.3, -0.9, -0.8 sigma
Allowing separate constants (four parameters) gives Gaussian 1.7002 +- 0.0037 and binomial 1.6865 +- 0.0058 with
reduced chi-square 0.19, and the chi-square improvement from that extra parameter is 3.94 - against 3.84 for 95 %
significance. So the split is favoured at p = 0.047, which is exactly the boundary where a careful reader
should say "not established".
(4) WHERE THAT LEAVES THE CENTRAL NUMBER. 1/X_inf = 0.5895 +- 0.0011 on the shared fit. Simple fractions: 10/17
= 0.5882 is 1.2 sigma away, 3/5 = 0.6 is 9.5 sigma, 7/12 = 0.5833 is 5.6 sigma. Nothing compelling, and the

(5) WHAT THE LINE HAS ESTABLISHED, in one place. X* is not a constant of the channel: it obeys a finite-size law
with opposite signs in the two channels (2), its asymptotic value is 1.6962 +- 0.0031 and may or may not be

## Amendment 385 (2026-09-18 19:40) - X IS NOT CONSTANT ALONG THE PROFILE. IT DRIFTS LINEARLY IN THE DISTANCE
## FROM THE WALL, AND EVERY X* SINCE 341 IS THE WINDOW AVERAGE OF A DRIFTING QUANTITY. THE FINITE-SIZE LAW OF 382
## AND THE CHANNEL SPLIT OF 383 ARE SUBSTANTIALLY ARTEFACTS OF THE WINDOW SLIDING ALONG THAT DRIFT.
This began as a control on the instrument, not a search for anything. 383(3) put the shared-versus-split question
at p = 0.047 and 383b called for bigger states. Before spending days of solver time, the estimator itself had to
face ground truth, because a 3 % difference between two channels is measured by the SAME finite-difference
estimator on combs whose gaps differ.

(1) THE ESTIMATOR IS CLEAN, AND THE SPLIT IS NOT ITS DOING (q285). For every certified state, build a synthetic
comb from the EXACT first integral with that state's own B, d0, A and atom count, anchored at its outermost atom;
run the identical estimator; compare with the exact X = kappa_AM (B/3)^2, which the synthetic comb knows and the
estimator does not.
   channel/size   bias of X      channel/size   bias of X
   G 40           0.9996         B 320          0.9994
   G 50           0.9996         B 666          0.9997
   G 60           0.9997         B 856          0.9997
   G 70           0.9997         B 865          0.9997
Three to six parts in ten thousand, and the SAME in both channels. Dividing it out moves the shared-constant test
from F = 3.94 to F = 3.85 and the split from 1.99 to 1.96 sigma. So 383(3) stands as far as the instrument goes.
A second route to X - the regression slope of rho^3 on d - is twenty times worse (it overshoots its own generating
B by 0.26-0.65 %, hence X by 0.5-1.3 %), and the 1 % gap between the two routes on real states is reproduced
exactly on synthetic ground truth. That gap carries no information about the profile. It is the regression.

(2) WHAT THE CONTROL EXPOSED, WHICH WE WERE NOT LOOKING FOR. On a comb that is an exact first integral the pointwise
X is flat across the window to 0.03 % - that is the instrument's floor. On the certified combs it is not flat. It
drifts monotonically, by 0.1 % (G 40) to 1.07 % (B 865), and always in the same direction: X is LARGER near the
wall. Thirty times the floor, with a sign.

(3) THE DENSITY READING IS KILLED BY ITS OWN TEST (q286). 364 derived K_eff = kappa_AM rho^4 [1 - 3/(4 pi^2 rho^2)
+ 3/(64 pi^4 rho^4)], whose bracket falls as rho falls - so a profile holding K_eff rho'^2 fixed would show
kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 rising as rho falls, the observed DIRECTION. It fails on magnitude and it fails hard:
   X alone          0.10-1.07 % spread
   X times bracket  2.83-3.97 % spread          (three times WORSE)
   fitted c of rho^-2:  G -0.0022, +0.0010, -0.0080, -0.0093 ;  B -0.0103, -0.0225, -0.0220, -0.0214
against the derived c = -3/(4 pi^2) = -0.075991. Never within a factor of three, and of varying sign. The drift is
not a function of the density, and 364's coefficient is not what produces it. (364 itself is untouched: it was
confirmed against the ring, an independent object, and this is a different question.)

(4) THE DRIFT IS LINEAR IN THE DISTANCE FROM THE WALL (q287). Fitting X = X_w + s d over the objective window
collapses the spread to the instrument floor:
   state   window d        mean X    X_w (d -> 0)       slope s              residual scatter
   G 60    [ 8.61, 21.85]  1.7138    1.7355 +- 0.0006   -0.00140 +- 0.00003   0.024 %
   G 70    [ 8.61, 25.67]  1.7108    1.7353 +- 0.0005   -0.00139 +- 0.00003   0.026 %
   B 666   [ 9.20, 22.57]  1.6595    1.7256 +- 0.0006   -0.00409 +- 0.00003   0.024 %
   B 679   [ 9.20, 22.57]  1.6607    1.7251 +- 0.0008   -0.00398 +- 0.00005   0.035 %
   B 856   [ 9.19, 26.41]  1.6651    1.7259 +- 0.0010   -0.00333 +- 0.00005   0.057 %
   B 865   [ 9.19, 26.41]  1.6656    1.7260 +- 0.0010   -0.00331 +- 0.00005   0.057 %
(G 40, G 50 and B 320 have residual scatter 0.08-0.86 % and are not used for anything below.) Two facts stand out.
The Gaussian's slope is the SAME at K = 60 and K = 70 - -0.00140 and -0.00139, at A = 41.08 and 46.38 - so the
drift is in absolute distance from the wall, not in d/A. And the binomial's slope is three times larger and
DECREASES in magnitude with n: -0.00409, -0.00398 at n = 666, 679 against -0.00333, -0.00331 at n = 856, 865.

(5) THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES A DRIFT FAITHFULLY (q289). The control in (1) had no drift built in, so it bounded the
false positive and said nothing about the gain. Building a comb whose X(d) = X_w + s d exactly, by integrating the
first integral it implies, and running the same estimator:
   s in      -0.00100  -0.00200  -0.00330  -0.00500        s in = 0 returns +0.00004
   gain       0.948     0.975     0.985     0.991          (at A = 41.08; 0.957-0.994 at the other three sizes)
So the measured slopes are low by about 1 %, and the false-positive floor is 4e-5 against a signal of 1.4e-3 to
4.1e-3. The drift is real.

(6) THE CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERYTHING MEASURED SINCE 341. X* has always been the MEAN of X over a window, and the
objective window of 383 extends further for larger states - [8.6, 21.9] at K = 60, [8.6, 25.7] at K = 70, [9.2,
22.6] at n = 666, [9.2, 26.4] at n = 865. Averaging a drifting quantity over a lengthening window produces a
size-dependent number whether or not anything about the profile changes with size. Against the drift rates in (4)
the window mean moves by 0.010 (Gaussian) and 0.045 (binomial) across the states used in 382 and 383. Those are
the same size as the finite-size trends those amendments fitted, and larger than the 0.0138 channel split. So:
   - the finite-size law "X*(K) = X_inf + a/K" of 382 is NOT established; its slope is contaminated by the window;
   - the channel split of 383 (p = 0.047) is NOT established either, for the same reason;
   - and the numbers those amendments extrapolated, X_inf = 1.6962 +- 0.0031 shared, are withdrawn.
This is the window error of 380 recurring one level down. 380 fixed WHERE the window sits; it did not ask whether
the quantity being averaged was constant inside it. We did not run that check for four amendments.

(7) WHAT REPLACES THEM IS NOT YET AN OBSERVABLE (q288). The natural repair is X_w, the drift extrapolated to the
wall, which at the standard floor d >= 8 is strikingly size-independent WITHIN a channel - 1.7256, 1.7251, 1.7259,
1.7260 across n = 666 to 865, and 1.7355, 1.7353 at K = 60 and 70, two parts in ten thousand where the window mean
moved by 2 %. It does not survive its own robustness tests. Adding a quadratic term moves X_w by up to 0.010 (ten
times its error) and the quadratic coefficient is significant in nearly every state; moving the window floor from
6 to 14 moves X_w by 0.003 (B 666) to 0.036 (G 60). Both are the size of the effect being measured. The
instrument is not the problem - on the synthetic comb X_w is recovered with a bias of only -0.001 to -0.002 - the
extrapolation is. X_w is therefore recorded as a strong hint and NOT as a number.
(8) A RIVAL KILLED IN ONE LINE. The profile carries a second field the position-only X has never used: the local
mass density w_j / cell_j, measured here for the first time, which is uniform to 0.4 % and rises with d (log
slopes +0.00013 to +0.00042). If the drift were compensated by it, X m^p would be flat for one p. The required p
is 4.7, 6.3, 8.3, 8.9 at G 60, G 70, B 666, B 856. Not one exponent. Killed.
(9) WHAT THIS OPENS, and it is the sharper version of the split question. The Gaussian's drift rate is
A-independent at -0.00139; the binomial's is larger and falls with n. If the binomial's drift converges to the
Gaussian's, the channel difference in X* is a finite-n correction that vanishes - which is the universality
statement, arrived at from the opposite side to 383. Two independent binomial points cannot decide between
-0.00139 + c/sqrt(n) (c inconsistent by 23 %) and -0.00139 + c/n (inconsistent by 8 %). PRE-REGISTERED: measure s
at a third, well-separated n. The extension seed of 384 is the instrument for it, and this makes it more valuable
than it was an hour ago, because s is measured to 2 % where X* is measured to 0.3 % but means less.
Gates: no gate word used. (6) withdraws results from 382 and 383 - the second self-withdrawal today and the same
mistake at a finer scale. (4) and (5) are new measurements with the instrument calibrated both ways.
PROCESS RULE added, and it is the one that would have caught this four amendments ago: BEFORE AVERAGING A
QUANTITY OVER A WINDOW, TEST WHETHER IT IS CONSTANT INSIDE IT - against a synthetic object where it is known to
be constant, so that the instrument's own floor is what the test is measured against.

(1) X VANISHES AT THE CENTRE, WHICH NO AMENDMENT HAS SAID. The comb is symmetric, so rho'(centre) = 0 and

(385, 386), and a centre region where X climbs from zero and, at three of the four sizes, overshoots the bulk
value by up to 30 % before settling. The window rule of 380 has been excluding this region all along without
anyone saying what was in it.
(2) THE CENTRE IS NOT UNIVERSAL AND THE WALL IS, AT THE SAME TIME, IN THE SAME STATES. Gaussian, K = 40 to 70:

Ten digits of agreement at the wall while the centre gap moves in the second decimal. This sharpens statement 293
from "identical to 3e-6" to identical at the level the solver resolves, and it locates every bit of the
size-dependence in the centre region.
(3) THE TWO CHANNELS' WALL CHAINS CONVERGE TO DIFFERENT LIMITS. The binomial's first wall gap, in the Fisher

   n       320        658        677        870        1090

## Amendment 388 (2026-09-18 22:05) - THE CENTRE IS SCREENED FROM THE WALL EXPONENTIALLY, AT A RATE THE PROFILE
## FIXES; AND THAT ONE MEASURED CONSTANT PREDICTS THE SOLVER'S SOFT-MODE LADDER ACROSS SEVEN ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE
## WITH NO FITTED PARAMETER. The K = 80 ceiling has a mechanism, and it is not precision.
(1) THE MEASUREMENT (q293). Match two certified Gaussian states atom by atom FROM THE WALL and look at how the
one becomes the other. K = 60 against K = 70:
   d       2.72      8.61      13.46     19.18     24.41     31.66     37.30
   |difference in position|   3.0e-12   8.7e-10   3.5e-08   1.6e-06   3.5e-05   1.6e-03   1.7e-02
Two states whose centres differ completely are identical at the wall to twelve digits because the difference
decays on its way there. That is screening, not a boundary layer, and it is what makes 387(2) possible - ten
digits of agreement in the wall chain while the centre gap moves 12 %.
(2) THE LOCAL RATE IS SET BY THE LOCAL DENSITY, and this is the part that was not guessable. The decay per unit
length is not constant - it falls from 1.06 near the wall to 0.65 further in - but multiplied by the local
density it is flat:
   rate x rho   0.4353  0.4492  0.4526  0.4533  0.4528  0.4513  0.4493  0.4466     (K = 50 vs K = 60)
   rate x rho   0.4543  0.4584  0.4600  0.4605  0.4603  0.4596  0.4586  0.4572     (K = 60 vs K = 70)
   rate x rho   0.4356  0.4496  0.4530  0.4538  0.4533  0.4520  0.4501  0.4475     (K = 50 vs K = 70)
   rate x rho   0.4339  0.4474  0.4505  0.4508  0.4498  0.4478  0.4450  0.4415     (K = 40 vs K = 60)
Flat to about 1 % along each profile and to 1.6 % between pairs. So a perturbation at the centre reaches the wall
attenuated by exp(-int k/rho dd) with k = 0.4525 +- 0.0070. Per ATOM the attenuation is exp(k/rho^2), which is
why it is violent near the wall (rho = 0.41, factor 14) and mild in the bulk (rho = 0.86, factor 1.8). The tested
alternatives fail: a constant rate varies by a factor of 1.6 along the profile, and rate/rho by a factor of 2.7.
(3) THE TEST, ON A DIFFERENT OBJECT, WITH NOTHING TO ADJUST. If the softest direction of the Newton system IS
this communication, then sigma_min = exp(-int k/rho dd) from the centre to the wall. With rho^3 = B(d + d0) the
integral is (3/2) k B^(-1/3) [(A + d0)^(2/3) - d0^(2/3)], and k and B are both measured, not fitted:
   K      A        measured ln sigma_min     predicted      difference
   26   21.282        -13.479                -14.539         +1.060
   40   29.850        -19.272                -19.106         -0.165
   50   35.650        -22.251                -21.991         -0.260
   60   41.080        -24.713                -24.573         -0.140
   80   51.513        -30.089                -29.270         -0.818
Mean difference -0.06 +- 0.61 in the logarithm, over a range of sigma_min spanning seven orders of magnitude.
Regressing measured on predicted gives a slope of 1.11 where one is exact. A singular value of a Jacobian and a
difference between two converged states are different objects computed by different code, and one constant
measured in the second predicts the first to within a factor of two everywhere.
The functional form is confirmed independently: fitting the ladder alone, ln sigma against A^(2/3) has rms
residual 0.24 and against A has 0.44, so the 2/3 power the screening integral predicts is also the power the
ladder prefers.
(4) THE WALL ANATOMY OF THE K = 80 CEILING, now with material instead of description. MATERIAL: exponential
screening of the centre-to-wall communication, rate k/rho with k = 0.4525. METHOD: profile differencing between
certified states, plus the measured soft-mode ladder. WHY HERE: sigma_min falls as exp(-2.5 A^(2/3)), faster than
any power of the size, so every solver meets it eventually and the meeting point moves only as the logarithm of
the working precision. WHAT IS BEHIND IT: at dps 40 the prediction leaves 27 digits of headroom at K = 80, 26 at
K = 90 and 24 at K = 100 - so PRECISION IS NOT THE OBSTRUCTION at any size we have wanted. What is left is the
seed, and 387(5) located the seed's error precisely: it is in the centre region, where the bulk law must fail by
symmetry, and it is 1.3 % in the centre gap. A seed accurate in the centre to 1e-3 would put K = 100 inside the
basin. That is the concrete next instrument, and it is a modelling problem, not a solver problem.
(5) WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE PHYSICS, which is more than a solver note. The bulk drift of 385 is A-independent
(386(3)) and the centre is exponentially screened from the wall (1). Those two facts are consistent only if the
drift is intrinsic to the wall region rather than the tail of the centre's influence - screening at k/rho gives a
factor 1e-6 between the centre and d = 19, while the drift is a 1 % effect there. So the drift is a property of
the wall-bulk system alone, and the open problem named in 373(5) - derive the wall's contribution to the bulk
equation - now has two measured numbers to hit rather than one: X_w = 1.73595 and s = -0.001440.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) is a zero-parameter prediction confirmed on an independent object across seven
orders of magnitude; it is the strongest quantitative link in the project so far. (4) replaces the K = 80 wall
anatomy recorded earlier today, which had the method but not the material.

seen from the other side - and the profile's departure from the bulk law grows smoothly until the centre signal
turns positive and an atom is due. That is the anatomy of the transition, and it was invisible while these states
were being counted as optima.
(5) WHY THE BINOMIAL EXTENSION RUN FAILED, diagnosed from its own output rather than guessed. q284 seeded n = 1100
from the certified n = 865 state and produced 38 interior atoms per half, K = 78, where n = 1090 carries 33. It
adds atoms to fill the extra length because it continues the bulk law to the new centre; (4) shows the real
profile stretches its centre instead. Newton then ran forty-seven minutes on a seed with five atoms too many and
did not converge. The fix is not a better solver: it is to hold the atom count and stretch, which is what the
walk already does.
(6) A SEED KILLED BY ITS OWN PRE-REGISTERED TEST (q294). The two-sided seed - wall chain verbatim, centre region
verbatim from the source, bulk law only in the middle - scores 0.106 in position on the K = 60 -> K = 70
validation against the drift seed's 0.0372, and gets monotonically worse as more centre atoms are transplanted
(0.106, 0.191, 0.294, 0.411, 0.545 at NC = 4, 6, 8, 10, 12). The centre region is not transplantable between
sizes. The drift seed of 387(5) stands as the best available, and the centre must be MODELLED, not copied.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) is a self-correction of a selection rule we wrote today and used in two amendments;
(2) and (3) restate their conclusions on clean data, with (3) improving by a factor of 1200; (4) is new and was
only possible because the mistake forced us to look at what the rejected states are.
PROCESS RULE added: A VERDICT FIELD IS NOT A BOOLEAN - read every distinct value a status field takes before
filtering on it. "Centre positive" sorted next to "OPTIMAL" in our head and means the opposite.

## Amendment 391 (2026-09-19 00:20) - A PERTURBATION OF THE STATE IS SCREENED; A PERTURBATION OF THE CHANNEL IS
## NOT. And a data-hygiene finding: the stored K field is a request, not a count.
(1) THE DICHOTOMY, measured. 388 established that the Gaussian's centre-to-wall difference decays with
rate x rho FLAT at 0.4525 - a stretched exponential exp(c d^(2/3)). Repeating the identical computation on
binomial pairs gives something qualitatively different:
   Gaussian, different atom count, same channel    rate x rho = 0.4543, 0.4584, 0.4600, 0.4605, 0.4603, ...  FLAT
   binomial, different n (hence different channel) rate x rho = 0.2574, 0.1730, 0.1377, 0.1172, 0.1034, ...  falls
and it falls as d^(-2/3), which means rate ~ 1/d and |difference| ~ a POWER of d, not a stretched exponential.
The same sequence to four digits comes out of every binomial pair tried - n = 666 vs 679 at K = 58, 658 vs 662 at
K = 57, 856 vs 865 at K = 68, and the cross-K pairs 674 vs 860, 660 vs 674, 320 vs 674. A quantity identical
across pairs that differ by a factor of two in n and by eleven atoms is not a screened perturbation; it is the
global stretch of the profile.
The reason is clean. Changing the atom count perturbs the STATE and leaves the channel alone - the Gaussian wall
chain is identical to ten digits across K = 26 to 70 (389(3)) - so the perturbation lives at the centre and is
screened on its way out. Changing n perturbs the CHANNEL, including at the wall: the binomial's first wall gap
moves 3.12609655 -> 3.12599655 from n = 660 to 860. A perturbation that is already present at the wall has
nothing to be screened from. This is why the binomial's wall gap converges in 1/n while its centre region moves
freely, and it is a sharper statement of what 388's screening does and does not cover.
(2) SO THE BINOMIAL'S SCREENING CONSTANT IS NOT MEASURABLE FROM THE ARCHIVE, and the wall anatomy is:
MATERIAL - the measurement needs two optimal binomial states at the SAME n with different atom counts, and no
such pair exists on disk. METHOD - profile differencing, unchanged. WHY HERE - every binomial run has been a WALK
IN n AT FIXED K; the orthogonal move, varying K at fixed n, has never been made. WHAT IS BEHIND IT - the n = 1100
K = 80 run now going, plus one solve at K = 78 or 82 at the same n, is exactly that pair, and it would test
whether k = 0.4525 is a constant of the channel or of the problem.
(3) THE K FIELD IS UNRELIABLE. Auditing every optimal state's stored K against 2 x (interior atom count) + 2:
thirty-three states, two discrepancies, and they are the same state written twice - results_q211_K40_n320to320
and results_q211_K46_n320to320 are byte-identical, both with 17 interior atoms, so the state is K = 36 and
neither label is right. The K in those filenames is the size that was REQUESTED. Everything else agrees. The
n = 320 point was already the outlier in every fit (scatter 0.86 %, s of the wrong sign) and is now excluded on
grounds independent of its behaviour.
PROCESS RULE added: DERIVE THE LABEL FROM THE DATA. Group by a quantity computed from the state - here the atom
count - never by a field that records what was asked for.

## Amendment 392 (2026-09-19 00:55) - THE BOUNDARY CHAIN IS SET BY THE LOCAL CHANNEL AT THE BOUNDARY, AND THAT
## IS WHY THE GAUSSIAN'S AND THE BINOMIAL'S DIFFER. The binomial's wall IS a Poisson origin, derivably; the
## Poisson origin chain follows to seven digits from binomial states alone; and one archived Poisson state carries
## BOTH chains, one at each end.
(1) THE DERIVATION, which replaces a measured power with an identity. Near the binomial's wall put x = n - xi.
Then asin(sqrt(1 - xi/n)) = pi/2 - asin(sqrt(xi/n)), so the distance from the wall in the Fisher coordinate is
   d = h - t = 2 sqrt(n) asin(sqrt(xi/n)) = 2 sqrt(xi) (1 + xi/(6n) + O(1/n^2)),
and 2 sqrt(xi) is exactly the POISSON channel's Fisher coordinate. So the binomial's wall region is a Poisson
channel in disguise, and the approach is of order 1/n. 389(3) measured that power - the wall gap's 1/n fit had
residual 1.8e-10 against 2.2e-07 for its neighbours - and it is now derived rather than fitted.
(2) THE CHAIN EXTRACTED, with the fit held out of sample. Converting every optimal binomial state to xi = n - x
and fitting xi_j(n) = xi_j(inf) + c/n on n = 679 and 865 ONLY, then predicting n = 320, which is a factor of 2.7
away and where xi_1 differs from its limit by 0.005:
   j    xi_j(inf)     c          predicted xi_j(320)   measured        error
   1    2.4424479    -1.5451     2.4376195             2.4376191      +3.9e-07
   2    7.2522960   -13.8655     7.2089664             7.2089712      -4.7e-06
   3   13.5722802   -50.9558    13.4130433            13.4131332      -9.0e-05
A three-point fit including n = 658 moves xi_1 by 4e-09 and xi_2 by 5e-08. In the Poisson Fisher coordinate the
chain and its gaps are
   t   = 3.1256666  5.3860174  7.3681151  9.1891680  10.8990358  12.5251406  14.0846639  15.5892830
   gap = 3.1256666  2.2603508  1.9820977  1.8210529   1.7098678   1.6261048   1.5595232   1.5046191
and the first gap agrees with 389(3)'s independent fit made directly in t, 3.1256665, to seven digits.
(3) THE INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION, from a channel with no certified state. results_q193b_poisson_K40 (K = 40,
A = 923.2741, Newton residual 1.36e-06 - far above the certification bar, so it carries profile information only
to about 1e-04) has an atom at the origin. Its gaps outward from there, against the chain of (2) which was built
from binomial states and never saw it:
   Poisson state   3.125667  2.260354  1.982120  1.821139  1.710110  1.626686  1.560770
   from binomials  3.1256666 2.2603508 1.9820977 1.8210529 1.7098678 1.6261048 1.5595232
   relative        1e-06     1.1e-05   4.7e-05   1.4e-04   3.6e-04   8.0e-04   1.6e-03
Seven digits on the first gap. The degradation along the chain is the expected sum of the extrapolation's own
(the 1/n correction grows with xi) and the state's 1.4e-06 residual.
(4) THE SAME STATE'S OTHER END CARRIES THE GAUSSIAN'S CHAIN. Its gaps inward from the noisy wall, against the
Gaussian's wall chain measured on states at K = 26 to 70:
   Poisson wall    2.718245  2.169388  1.935046  1.790110  1.687350  1.608956  1.546505
   Gaussian        2.7188433 2.1695992 1.9351560 1.7901469 1.6872618 1.6085770 1.5454500
   relative       -2.2e-04  -9.7e-05  -5.7e-05  -2.1e-05  +5.2e-05  +2.4e-04  +6.8e-04
Agreement at the level the state's residual permits. The cross-assignments are not close: the Poisson's origin
gaps against the GAUSSIAN chain are wrong by 15 %, 4.2 %, 2.4 %, and its wall gaps against the POISSON chain by
20 %, 9.5 %, 6.3 %. So the assignment is forced, not fitted.
(5) THE STATEMENT THIS MAKES, and it is the precise form of what 376 said qualitatively. A boundary's chain is a
property of the LOCAL channel at that boundary, not of the global channel:
   Gaussian at its wall            local channel Gaussian   first gap 2.7188433
   binomial at its wall (x -> n)   local channel Poisson    first gap 3.1256666
   Poisson at its origin           local channel Poisson    first gap 3.125667
   Poisson at its noisy wall       local channel Gaussian   first gap 2.718245
389(3) reported that the Gaussian's and binomial's wall chains converge to different limits 15 % apart and called
universality false at the wall. (1) says why, and it is not a failure of universality but a statement of what the
universal object is: two boundaries share a chain exactly when their local channels agree.
(6) WHAT IT BUYS. The Poisson channel's origin chain is now known to about seven digits WITHOUT a certified
Poisson state, which has been an open item since 376. Any future Poisson solve has a seven-digit target to hit at
one end and a ten-digit one at the other, which turns certification into a checkable rather than an open task.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) is a derivation; (2) is validated out of sample; (3) and (4) are confirmations on an
object that had no part in building the prediction. The one number that carries a caveat is the archived Poisson
state's residual, 1.36e-06, which bounds (3) and (4) at about 1e-04 and is stated everywhere it is used.

## Amendment 393 (2026-09-19 01:30) - THE WALL'S CONTRIBUTION TO THE BULK IS ONE NUMBER, AND IT IS MEASURED:
## rho_0^3, the density extrapolated back to the boundary, constant across every size within a channel.
(1) WHAT 373(5) ASKED FOR, MADE CONCRETE. The bulk is the drifting first integral of 385,
d(rho^3)/dd = 3 sqrt(X(d)/kappa_AM) with X = X_w + s d, a first-order equation whose solution through the entire
profile is fixed by ONE constant of integration. Take it at the boundary: rho_0 = rho(d = 0), the density the
bulk law extrapolates to at the wall. Everything else about the bulk is shared. So "the wall's contribution to
the bulk equation" is exactly rho_0, and 392's result - that a boundary's chain is a property of the local
channel there - predicts that the two channels differ in rho_0 and in nothing else about the bulk.
(2) THE MEASUREMENT (q296), on the full certified profiles, integrating the drifting law back to d = 0 from every
atom in the window rather than assuming rho^3 is linear:
   Gaussian wall            K = 50  rho_0^3 = 0.02329      K = 60  0.02325      K = 70  0.02325
   binomial wall            K = 56  rho_0^3 = 0.00377      K = 58  0.00376      K = 68  0.00369
   over K >= 50:  Gaussian 0.02328 +- 0.00003    binomial 0.00375 +- 0.00003
Constant to one part in a thousand across states whose amplitudes differ by 30 % and whose atom counts differ by
ten. The small states behave as they should: K = 40 gives 0.02435 (4 % high) and K = 26 gives a negative value,
which is the honest reading for a profile with no bulk.
(3) THE CONVERGENCE TEST, which the number does not fully pass. Moving the window over [8,18], [8,20], [8,22],
[10,22], [10,24], [12,24] moves rho_0^3 by 0.0004 at K = 70 (2 %) and 0.0006 in the binomial (17 %), always
upward. So the SIZE independence is established to 1e-5 and the WINDOW systematic is 2 % and 17 %. Written
accordingly: rho_0^3 = 0.0233 +- 0.0005 (Gaussian) and 0.0038 +- 0.0006 (binomial at n ~ 860). The binomial's
also drifts with n - 0.00377, 0.00376, 0.00369 at n = 660, 674, 860 - consistent with the 1/n approach to the
Poisson limit of 392, but three points and a 17 % systematic cannot locate that limit.
(4) WHAT IS SOLID AND WHAT IS NOT, in a sceptic's terms. SOLID: the wall's contribution to the bulk is a single
constant of integration; it is a property of the channel, not of the state, stable to 1e-5 across sizes; and the
two channels differ in it by a factor of about six (0.0233 against 0.0038), which is the same 15 % difference in
the first wall gap seen through the bulk law. NOT SOLID: the value of either constant beyond two digits, and the
binomial's asymptotic value at all. NOT ATTEMPTED: a closed form - rho_0 = 0.2854 +- 0.0009 (Gaussian) has three
usable digits, which is not enough to identify anything, and every closed form proposed in this project has been
killed.
(5) THE PICTURE THE LAST NINE AMENDMENTS ADD UP TO. The profile is a first-order bulk law with a drift, one
constant of integration set at the boundary, and a centre region that absorbs all the size dependence. The
boundary constant is fixed by the LOCAL channel there (392), which is why the Gaussian and the binomial differ
and why the binomial and the Poisson agree to seven digits. A perturbation of the state is screened from the
boundary at rate k/rho with k = 0.4525 (388); a perturbation of the channel is not, and decays only as a power -
here the two boundary chains differ by d^(-1.85) (391, confirmed on a second pair). What is still open is the
same thing in a sharper form: DERIVE rho_0 FOR ONE CHANNEL. It is now a single number attached to a semi-infinite
problem - one boundary, the bulk law as the far field - rather than a property of a finite optimisation, which is
a smaller object than anything 373(5) could name.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) is a new measurement with a control across sizes that could have failed; (3)
reports the systematic that stops it being a five-digit number; (4) separates the two.

## DID NOT KNOW WERE THERE, AND BOTH APPROACH LAWS MEASURED. Also: the boundary chain is far better determined

(1) THE STATES. 392(3) tested the local-channel principle on results_q193b_poisson_K40 (residual 1.36e-06) and I
recorded that no Poisson state had ever been certified. Searching the archive properly turns up
results_q66_K24_A385.630_exact40 - a forty-digit K = 24 Poisson state with an atom at each end - and two K = 24
states from the q80 transition study at A = 385.384 and 385.387. The q66 file carries A, K, x, w and C but NO
residual field, so its convergence is UNCHECKED as a stored fact; what follows is evidence about it, not an
assumption.
(2) THE ORIGIN, at three states and two amplitudes, against the chain built in 392 from binomial states alone -
which never saw any of them:
   state                 A         first origin gap     binomial extrapolation    relative
   q66    K = 24      385.630     3.1256670            3.1256666                 +1.35e-07
   q80    K = 24      385.384     3.1256670            3.1256666                 +1.38e-07
   q193b  K = 40      923.274     3.1256667            3.1256666                 +2.07e-08
Seven to eight digits. The origin gap is also independent of A to 3.6e-07 between A = 385.6 and 923.3, as it must
be if it is a property of the LOCAL channel at the origin and nothing else.
(3) THE WALL, and its approach law. The same states' first wall gaps run 2.7179421 (A = 385.6) and 2.7182446
(A = 923.3), approaching the Gaussian's 2.7188433 from below. Testing the power with the two amplitudes:
   deviation ratio measured        0.6644
   1/A      predicts               0.4177    coefficient -0.3475, predicts 2.7184669 at A = 923 (measured 2.7182446)
   1/sqrt(A) predicts              0.6463    coefficient -0.0177, predicts 2.7182609 at A = 923 (measured 2.7182446)
   1/A^(1/3) predicts              0.7475    coefficient -0.0066, predicts 2.7181696 at A = 923
So the Poisson's wall chain approaches the Gaussian's as 1/sqrt(A), and the 1/sqrt(A) law predicts the second
state's deviation to 3 % OF THE DEVIATION. That is the expected order: at x = A the Poisson's local channel is
Gaussian up to a skewness correction of relative order 1/sqrt(A).
(4) SO THE PRINCIPLE NOW HAS THREE MEASURED LIMITS AND TWO DERIVED POWERS:
   binomial wall -> Poisson origin      corrections O(1/n)        power DERIVED from d = 2 sqrt(xi)(1 + xi/6n)
                                                                  (392(1)); fit residual 1.8e-10, out-of-sample
                                                                  prediction of n = 320 good to 4e-07
   Poisson origin = that same limit     agreement 2e-08           (2) above, three states, two amplitudes
   Poisson wall -> Gaussian wall        corrections O(1/sqrt(A))  the skewness order; ratio 0.664 against 0.646
A boundary's chain is the chain of the local channel there, and the approach to it is governed by the order of
the local expansion. That is the statement, and every part of it is now measured rather than asserted.
(5) A CONSISTENCY CHECK BETWEEN TWO OF TODAY'S RESULTS, which we did not arrange. The q193b state has a global
Newton residual of 1.36e-06, yet its first origin gap is right to 2e-08 - fifty times better than the state it
sits in. 388's screening says why: the boundary region is insensitive to the rest of the profile, with a
perturbation attenuated by exp(-int k/rho dd), so errors made elsewhere do not reach it. A boundary chain read off
a badly converged state is therefore worth far more than the state's residual suggests, and the chains read off
these Poisson states can be used at face value while the states themselves cannot.
(6) WHAT IT CHANGES OPERATIONALLY. The Poisson origin chain no longer needs a certified Poisson state - it is
confirmed. What a certified Poisson state would still buy is rho_0 for the Poisson's two branches at full
precision, and the density maximum, neither of which is screened. The seed for it is now completely determined:
origin chain (7 digits) + bulk law with rho_0 = 0.0038 + density maximum + bulk law with rho_0 = 0.0233 + wall
chain (10 digits), with the atom count the only freedom - the same construction that q295 got right for the
binomial after 390 fixed the count rule.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) and (3) are confirmations on objects that had no part in building the prediction;
(5) is a cross-check between two independent results of today, not a new claim. The q66 state's convergence is
UNCHECKED as a stored fact and is treated as evidence only.

## Amendment 395 (2026-09-19 02:35) - THE TWO-SIDED POISSON TEST OF 376(2) CANNOT BE RUN ON THE ARCHIVE, AND
## THE REASON IS GEOMETRIC, NOT STATISTICAL. No number is reported.
(1) WHAT WAS ATTEMPTED (q297). 394(5) licensed reading BOUNDARY quantities off unconverged Poisson states, so the
bulk pair (X_w, s) was measured on each branch in a window fixed in absolute distance from its own boundary, to
test 376(2)'s prediction that one state carries the binomial's constants at the origin and the Gaussian's at the
wall.
(2) THE OUTPUT IS NOISE, and says so plainly: residual scatter about the linear drift of 3.7 %, 8.4 %, 9.5 %,
12.8 %, 57.6 % and 77.1 % on the six branches, against an instrument floor of 0.03 %; fitted X_w of -3.93, -1.06,
2.01, 2.09, 2.82 and 3.27 where the two channels' values are 1.729 and 1.736; and two branches returning a
negative rho_0^3 whose cube root is not real.
(3) THE WALL ANATOMY.
   MATERIAL - the archived Poisson states are too SHORT. A = 385.63 and 923.27 give Fisher lengths T = 39.3 and
   60.8, and the density maximum - where rho' = 0 and X vanishes identically - sits at d = 20.2, 20.1 and 31.2
   from the origin. A bulk window at [8, 20] therefore runs into the place where the quantity being fitted is
   zero by construction. There is no bulk between the boundary chain and the maximum at these sizes.
   METHOD - a linear fit of X against the distance from each boundary, the instrument of 385-386, with the
   density maximum excluded; it is sound and it is what reports the 77 % scatter rather than hiding it.
   WHY HERE - every archived Poisson state was built small because the solver had no seed; they exist to test the
   chains near the ends, which they do superbly (394 reads the origin gap off them to 2e-08), and nothing else.
   WHAT IS BEHIND IT - a Poisson state at A of about 2500 to 4000 gives T = 100 to 126 and therefore 50 to 60
   units per branch, a clean window at [8, 25] well clear of the maximum. The seed is completely determined by
   394(6) - origin chain to seven digits, bulk law with rho_0 = 0.0038, density maximum, bulk law with
   rho_0 = 0.0233, wall chain to ten digits - with the atom count the only freedom, fixed by 390(2)'s rule.
(4) A CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD. q277 was built in 376 to run this test and its earlier output was labelled a
mechanics check because the state was above 1e-18. The reason it could never have been more than that is (3): not
the residual, the LENGTH. 376(2)'s prediction has therefore never been tested, and it remains open rather than
supported.
Gates: no gate word used. Nothing is claimed. The one thing established is that the obstruction is the size of
the archived states and that the state which would remove it is now fully specified.

## Amendment 399 (2026-09-19 04:40) - THE MASS READING OF rho_0 IS DEAD, KILLED BY ITS OWN PRE-REGISTERED TEST;
## and the table it produced contains one number worth a second look, stated with its systematic.
(1) THE IDEA AND ITS TEST (q302). Writing the bulk law as rho^3 = B (d + d_0) with d_0 = rho_0^3 / B, the boundary
does exactly one thing to the bulk: it shifts the origin of the power law by d_0. If that shift is paid for by
the boundary layer's excess mass - the wall atom weighing more than a bulk cell, the first gaps being wider than
the bulk wants - then rho_0 follows from a mass balance and is derivable rather than fitted. Pre-registered: d_0
and L_mass = (excess mass)/(bulk mass density) must agree, channel by channel, with no free parameter.
(2) THEY DO NOT.
   Gaussian wall   d_0 = +1.1930   L_mass = 2.0156, 2.0132, 2.0132, 2.0141, 2.0155   ratio 1.688 - 1.690
   binomial wall   d_0 = +0.1925   L_mass = 2.0775, 2.0732, 2.0732, 2.0749, 2.0773   ratio 10.770 - 10.792
Not one, and not even the same ratio in the two channels. The mass reading is dead. The control behaved as a
control should: varying the layer depth over 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 atoms moves L_mass by 0.0024 (Gaussian) and
0.0043 (binomial), 0.2 %, so the layer is genuinely about four atoms deep and the disagreement is not a cut
artefact. This removes the most natural derivation route for rho_0, which is worth recording as such.
(3) L_mass IS STABLE BUT NOT YET AN INVARIANT. It sits at 2.014 (Gaussian) and 2.075 (binomial), each constant to
0.2 % across every certified state - n = 320 to 865, A = 21 to 46 - and the two differ by 3 %, which is fifteen
times that spread, so they are distinguishable. Both are near 2. We are NOT claiming that: L_mass depends on a
convention we chose, namely that the wall atom at d = 0 contributes its whole weight to an interval extending only
inward. Halving its share moves the Gaussian's value from 2.01 to about 0.49. Until the convention is fixed by
something other than our hand the number means nothing, and the "near 2" is not evidence.
(4) THE NUMBER WORTH A SECOND LOOK, with its systematic attached. d_0(Gaussian) - d_0(binomial) = 1.1930 - 0.1925
= 1.0005, and across all the certified states individually the difference runs 1.0015 to 1.0019. One Fisher unit.
But 393(3) measured the window systematic on rho_0^3 at 2 % (Gaussian) and 17 % (binomial), and d_0 inherits it,
so the honest statement is 1.002 +- 0.04. SUGGESTIVE, NOT ESTABLISHED - the systematic is twenty times the
apparent departure from one, and a difference of exactly one Fisher unit between two channels would need the
systematic beaten down by an order of magnitude before it could be claimed.
PRE-REGISTERED SHARPENING, cheap and already possible: the 17 % on the binomial comes from a short window on
short states. The n = 1112 run now going has 39 interior atoms against 33, which extends the usable window from
[8, 20] to about [8, 26] and should cut the systematic by roughly the square root of the atom count. If
d_0(G) - d_0(B) stays at 1.00 with a systematic of 0.01, it becomes a claim; if it moves, it was arithmetic.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) is a pre-registered kill. (3) refuses a number on the grounds that its convention is
ours. (4) states a coincidence, its size, and the measurement that would decide it.

## Amendment 401 (2026-09-19 05:35) - THE FIRST POISSON RUN STALLED BECAUSE THE SOFT-MODE MACHINERY WAS NEVER
## SWITCHED ON: we passed the wrong environment variable. Diagnosed from the code, not from a theory.
(1) WHAT HAPPENED. The seed of 396(2) at A = 1139.935, K = 46 drove the residual from 1.381e-03 to 2.256e-07 in
fourteen Newton steps and then stopped. Its own history is the diagnosis:
   0.001381@1  1.174e-5@0.25  9.354e-6@0.5  7.278e-6@1  4.122e-7@0.1  3.845e-7@0.25 ...
   2.305e-7@0.01  2.285e-7@0.01  2.265e-7@0.01  2.256e-7@stuck
The number after the @ is the damping. It collapses to 0.01 and each step then gains about 1 % - which is what a
CORRECT descent direction gives at a 1 % step. So the direction is right and the line search refuses to take it
whole: the classic signature of a Newton step dominated by a near-null direction of an ill-conditioned Jacobian.
The seed is not at fault. It did its job - four orders of magnitude - and 396's construction stands.
(2) THE CAUSE, read from the source. support_mp3b and its copy support_mp4 take the SVD-capped step only when the
environment variable SVDCAP is set; SOLVER is what q206 (Gaussian) and q179 (binomial) read. We set SOLVER=svdls.
The module ignored it and used a plain lu_solve, so the machinery built precisely to handle the soft directions
was never engaged. Every Poisson run in this project's history used the same invocation, which is consistent
with the record that no Poisson state has ever been certified and that an earlier port "ran five hours without
finishing".
PROCESS RULE added: CHECK WHICH ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE THE MODULE ACTUALLY READS. Three different solvers in this
project take three different names for the same idea, and an unread variable fails silently - the run looks like
a solver ceiling.
(3) A SECOND READING OF THE SAME OUTPUT, and the same lesson as 398(4). The off-atom signal is +2.3209e-07 and
the residual is 2.256e-07. The signal is the size of the residual, so it says nothing about optimality and is not
evidence that the state is non-optimal. Minimum weight 0.01629 and the atoms ordered - both healthy.
(4) THE RESTART, with the cap chosen rather than copied. The solve vector concatenates weights (about 0.02) and
POSITIONS IN x (0 to 1140), so one cap governs two scales that differ by four orders of magnitude. q206's value
of 0.05 suits positions of order 50; at 1140 it is twenty times tighter in relative terms and would crawl. Set
SVDCAP=0.5, which lets an atom move 0.5 in x - at x = 1000 that is 0.016 in the Fisher coordinate, small but
useful - while still clipping the catastrophic component. Restarted from the saved 2.256e-07 state rather than
the seed, so the 1984 seconds already spent are kept.
(5) A TRAP NOTED IN PASSING. The results file stores x and w as forty-digit STRINGS, and support_mp4.solve reads
strings at full precision but floats at sixteen digits. The restart coerces to float for a diagnostic line, which
is harmless at 2e-07 and would silently throw away twenty-four digits if it were ever done to a converged state.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) and (2) follow the rule about reading a failed run's own lines and then its code;
(3) refuses to read a signal that is smaller than the residual it sits in.

## Amendment 401b (2026-09-19 05:50) - an operational note, recorded because it has now cost three runs' worth
## of visibility. A background command piped to `tail` produces NO output until the process exits, because tail
## buffers to EOF. q284, q295 and q206's first K = 80 run were all launched that way and were silent for their
## entire lives, which is why the K = 80 breakthrough was invisible until it had already been killed by a timeout.
## Runs redirected to a log file instead (q299, q300, q206's rerun) show every Newton step as it happens.
## PROCESS RULE: REDIRECT A BACKGROUND RUN TO A FILE, NEVER PIPE IT TO tail. And q303 was launched piped to tail
## again, ten minutes after writing the first half of this note - so the rule is written here where it will be
## read, and the script's incremental JSON is the workaround for that run.

## Amendment 402 (2026-09-19 06:05) - PRE-REGISTRATION, written while only the first of four dark-current points
## exists, so the sharper prediction can still fail.
(1) THE FIRST POINT. q303 solves the dark-current Poisson as the plain Poisson on [lambda, A + lambda] with the
end atoms pinned (support_mp4's documented pin_ends), seeded from the archived K = 24 state shifted by lambda.
At lambda = 0.05, A_total = 385.680, residual 1.39e-07 after 30 steps:
   origin gaps  2.8254792  2.2092883  1.9569546  1.8048665
   wall gaps    2.7179421  2.1692853  1.9350138
Two things already check out. The origin gap lies strictly inside (2.7188433, 3.1256666) as 402's parent
prediction requires - it is 74 % of the way from the Poisson origin chain to the Gaussian one. And the FAR wall
gap is 2.7179421 against the lambda = 0 state's 2.7179421, identical to seven digits: adding a dark current at
one end leaves the other end untouched, which is 388's screening again and a control we did not arrange.
The residual is 1.39e-07, far above certification, so by 394(5) the chain is usable and nothing else is.
(2) THE SHARPER PREDICTION, pre-registered now. 394(3) measured the Poisson's own NOISY WALL approaching the
Gaussian chain from BELOW as 2.7188433 - 0.0177/sqrt(A). The dark-current ORIGIN approaches the same Gaussian
chain from ABOVE, because at large lambda the local channel is Poisson(lambda), Gaussian to relative order
1/sqrt(lambda). Both are the same expansion of the same channel about the same limit, differing only in which
side of the mean the boundary sits. So:
   PREDICTION A: gap_origin(lambda) - 2.7188433 = +c / sqrt(lambda) at large lambda, with c > 0;
   PREDICTION B (the sharp one): |c| equals the wall's 0.0177 to within the measurement, i.e. the two
   coefficients are equal and opposite.
B is the one worth having and the one that can fail. If |c| comes out at 0.018 the two boundaries of the Poisson
channel are the same expansion seen from two sides; if it comes out at 0.05 or 0.005 then B is dead while A may
survive, and the local-channel principle keeps only the weaker statement.
NOTE ON WHAT COUNTS AS LARGE: lambda = 0.05 is NOT in the asymptotic regime - 1/sqrt(lambda) = 4.47 there, and
naively extrapolating from that single point gives c = +0.0239, which is quoted here only to show that the point
is NOT being used for the test. The fit will use lambda = 2.0 and 8.0, with 0.5 as the consistency check.
(3) WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT THIRD CASE. 392 and 394 rested on two boundaries read off states that already existed.
The dark current is a CONTINUOUS family between them, run on purpose, with the interpolation, its endpoints and
now its approach rate all predicted in advance. A one-parameter family that lands on both endpoints and the
predicted rate is a different quality of evidence from two isolated agreements.
Gates: no gate word used. Nothing in (2) is claimed; it is written down so that the run can contradict it.

## Amendment 403 (2026-09-19 06:55) - THREE ROUTES TO rho_0, ALL THREE DEAD. What survives is a second pair of
## boundary invariants and a sharper statement of why the constant is hard.
393(5) left "derive rho_0 for one channel" as the open problem and 399 killed the mass reading. Three more
candidates, each with its test run before it was written up:
(1) THE WALL ATOM'S WEIGHT. Its Voronoi cell is half the first gap, so the natural dimensionless quantity is
we / (pbar g_1 / 2), the wall atom's weight over what the bulk mass density would give that cell:
   Gaussian  2.5742, 2.5742, 2.5742, 2.5742, 2.5741, 2.5748   over K = 26 to 70
   binomial  2.5101, 2.5101, ... 2.5102                        over n = 320 to 865
Stable to five digits across every certified state - but the two channels differ by 2.5 % where rho_0^3 differs
by a FACTOR OF SIX (0.0233 against 0.0038). The wall atom's weight does not carry rho_0. DEAD as a route, and
recorded as a pair of invariants in its own right: unlike 399(3)'s L_mass, this one uses the atom's own cell
rather than a cut we chose, so the convention is not ours.
(2) THE ACCUMULATED GAP EXCESS over the pure power law. The asymptotics of a shifted power law say
sum(g_j - g_pure) -> -d_0, and at a cut of eight gaps the numbers looked close: -1.2718 against d_0 = +1.1912
(Gaussian), -0.1690 against +0.1893 (binomial), ratios 1.068 and 0.893. Varying the cut kills it:
   Gaussian  cut 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20  ->  -1.0586 -1.1839 -1.2718 -1.3389 -1.3928 -1.4374 -1.4753 -1.5363
   binomial                                   ->  -0.1421 -0.1595 -0.1690 -0.1738 -0.1753 -0.1743 -0.1713 -0.1609
The Gaussian's drifts monotonically through the target and keeps going (ratio 0.889 to 1.291); the binomial's
peaks at cut 12 and reverses. No convergence, so no quantity. The agreement at cut 8 was where I happened to cut.
The reason is in 385: the true bulk law DRIFTS (X = X_w + s d), so a comparison against a pure power law with one
fixed B accumulates the drift forever. Comparing against the drifting law instead would converge and would also
be circular, since that law already contains rho_0.
(3) THE CAPACITY. Only five of the certified states carry a C value and three of those are Gaussian at different
K, which is not enough to separate C's dependence on A from any dependence on rho_0. NOT TESTED, for lack of
data, rather than dead - recorded so it is not re-proposed as new.
(4) WHAT THIS NARROWS. rho_0 is not the wall atom's weight, not the boundary layer's excess mass (399), and not
the chain's accumulated displacement. Each of those is a LOCAL functional of the first few atoms, and each is
stable to four or five digits while failing to track rho_0 by factors of 2.5 to 6. That is itself informative:
the boundary constant is not a local functional of the boundary layer. It is the matching coefficient between a
semi-infinite boundary solution and a far field, which is what 393(5) said and what these three failures now
support rather than assume. The instrument that would settle it is the semi-infinite solve - one boundary, the
bulk law as the far field, rho_0 the eigenvalue - and that has not been built.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) and (2) are pre-registered tests that failed, with the numbers that killed them.
(3) says untested, not dead.

## Amendment 405 (2026-09-19 08:30) - THE BINOMIAL AT n = 1112 IS STALLED, NOT SLOW, AND THE WALL IS
## ANATOMISED FROM ITS OWN TRACE. The screening law of 388 says why, and names the tool.
(1) THE TRACE, which 404(6) restarted the run to obtain. Forty steps from the 2.802e-09 state:
