E = 0 is exact; what is approximate is the family of profiles on which we evaluate its sign change. Orders so far:
constant X gave 0.12 %, plus curvature 0.02-0.03 %, plus the cubic term 0.004-0.026 % with no systematic sign.
That is the right qualitative behaviour for a convergent expansion.
(4) THE HONEST LIMIT OF (1). Here c and e are READ OFF the certified profile, whereas 435 made c self-consistent
from the law's own drift. The self-consistent version of e has not been done, and until it is, (1) shows the
SOURCE of the residual without yet being a parameter-free improvement. That is the next computation and it is a
small one: extend 435's fixed point to two coefficients instead of one.
(5) WHERE THE NUMBER STANDS AFTER TODAY. Parameter-free and self-consistent: 0.03 % (435, both channels per
447(4)). With the family carried one order further using measured coefficients: 0.004 to 0.026 % with no
systematic sign (this amendment). The claim we will make until (4) is done is the first of those.
Gates: no gate word used. (4) states that the improvement is not yet parameter-free and (5) quotes the weaker
number accordingly.

AMENDMENT 449. THE TWO-COEFFICIENT FIXED POINT: THE DERIVED BULK LAW AND THE MEASUREMENT AGREE TO THE METHOD'S
OWN NUMERICAL PRECISION.
(1) FIRST ATTEMPT DIVERGED, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING. Iterating c and e to self-consistency on a unit
d-grid blew up - dX/dd went -0.001468, -0.001434, -0.001559, -0.000369, -0.004367, +0.005903, -0.016010,
+0.025323, -0.042148, ending at a 32 % error. Cause, measured not guessed: e needs the SECOND derivative of X*,
and 432(7) puts the method's own precision on X* at about 5e-05, so on a unit grid the noise in d^2X/dd^2 is
about 1e-04 against a true value near 1e-05 - ten times the signal. A quantity that needs two numerical
derivatives of a noisy function cannot be iterated raw.
(2) REPAIRED by fitting X*(d) with a cubic over d = 12 to 27 before differentiating, and damping the update
(0.6 old, 0.4 new). It then settles:
     d        15         18         21         24
   X*      1.714996   1.710108   1.705908   1.702136
   meas    1.714954   1.710099   1.705797   1.702408
   diff    +0.0024 %  +0.0005 %  +0.0065 %  -0.0160 %
   over d = 14 to 24:  rms 0.0059 %, max 0.0160 %
  against 435's one-coefficient fixed point (rms 0.021 %, max 0.028 %) - a factor of three and a half, and now
  PARAMETER-FREE, which 448(1)'s version was not.
(3) THE HONEST LIMIT, which is now the instrument and not the theory. The iteration does not settle to machine
precision: max |dc| wanders between 2.3e-07 and 1.3e-06, and X*(20) moves over 1.706828 to 1.706908 across the
last iterations, a spread of 8e-05 - 0.005 %. That is the same 5e-05-in-X precision of 432(7) showing through. So
the agreement in (2), rms 0.0059 %, IS AT THE LEVEL OF THE METHOD'S OWN JITTER. The correct statement is that the
derived law and the measurement agree to within the precision at which either can currently be computed, and no
residual is resolved. Going further needs extended-precision arithmetic in the E quadrature, not a better fixed
point.
(4) WHAT THE NUMBER IS, FINALLY. The bulk law derived from the exact ripple energy, with kappa_AM and psi as its
only inputs and every coefficient self-consistent, reproduces the measured X(d) on the Gaussian to an rms of
0.006 % over d = 14 to 24. 447(4)'s 0.03 % residual, which two channels agreed on, is accounted for: it was the
trial family truncated at one coefficient. This supersedes 435(2), 436(1), 447(3) and 448(5) as the statement of
accuracy.
(5) STILL TO DO ON THIS THREAD. The binomial has not been redone at two coefficients - 447(3)'s -0.027 % is a
one-coefficient number and should move the same way. That is the cheapest remaining check of the whole
derivation, and it is a cross-channel one.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) records a divergence and its measured cause; (3) declines to claim a residual that
the method cannot resolve.

AMENDMENT 450. 449(5)'s CROSS-CHANNEL CHECK IS INCONCLUSIVE, AND THE REASON IS A SCISSORS BETWEEN TWO VALIDITY
CONDITIONS RATHER THAN A DISAGREEMENT.
(1) THE RUN. The fixed point of 449 re-parametrised in rho (c and e are universal functions of rho, since the
d-map cancels: drho/dd = sqrt(X/kappa_AM)/rho^2), converged over rho in [0.6205, 0.800] to max |dc| = 2.0e-08,
giving c = -5.393e-06 and e = +1.810e-08 at the binomial's rho(12) = 0.61988. Then:
     X* one coefficient  = 1.722268        X* two coefficients = 1.722340
     vs quadratic 1/n over n >= 658 (1.722701):   -0.0251 % -> -0.0210 %
     vs quadratic 1/n over all 18    (1.722721):  -0.0263 % -> -0.0221 %
  The second coefficient moves the binomial by only 0.004 %, where on the Gaussian it moved things from 0.021 %
  to 0.006 %. The binomial residual does NOT close.
(2) WHY, AND IT IS A SCISSORS. The binomial comparison can only be made at d = 12, because that is the only depth
where the n = 320 state's window reaches and therefore the only place the 1/n lever is long enough to determine
the extrapolation (447(2)). But d = 12 is exactly where the trial family is MARGINAL for the binomial:
rho(12) = 0.61988 gives rho^3/b = 12.3 against a kernel reach of 12, so the family's own density very nearly
terminates inside the kernel - the condition 432(8) states. At d >= 16, where the family is safe, only the short
lever exists (n = 658 to 865) and linear versus quadratic extrapolation differ by 0.044 %, eight times the effect
being tested. The two validity conditions - long 1/n lever, and family safely inside its reach - have no overlap
in the certified binomial set.
(3) SO THE CROSS-CHANNEL CHECK AT 0.006 % IS NOT AVAILABLE FROM EXISTING DATA, and 449(4)'s number stands on the
Gaussian alone. What 447(4) established - that both channels see the SAME 0.02-0.03 % one-coefficient residual -
is unaffected and remains the cross-channel evidence.
(4) WALL ANATOMY. MATERIAL: no binomial depth simultaneously satisfies both validity conditions. METHOD: the two-
coefficient fixed point in rho, evaluated at the extrapolated rho. WHY HERE: the certified binomial family spans
n = 320 then jumps to 658-865, so the lever is long only at small d, while the family needs large d. WHAT IS
BEHIND IT: a certified binomial state at an intermediate n - roughly 430 to 520 - whose window would reach
d ~ 18 while keeping the 1/n lever long. That is a solver run at an atom count between K = 17 and K = 27, which
is well inside the range the solver already handles, and it is the cheapest thing that would settle this.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) declines to claim a cross-channel figure the data cannot support.

AMENDMENT 451. THE FIVE-GATES LITERATURE CHECK I OWED, RUN: ABBOTT-MACHTA DO WRITE AN EULER-LAGRANGE EQUATION,
AND IT GIVES X = 1 EXACTLY WHERE THE CERTIFIED STATES GIVE 1.707.
(1) WHY THIS WAS OVERDUE. 432-449 derived a bulk law and we had not once compared it against the EL equation in
the source paper, because we had been carrying the belief - from 356 and 409 - that the two-term Abbott-Machta
functional "cannot predict a shape". That belief was about FITTING kappa_eff. It is not the same statement as
"their paper contains no density equation", and the second is false.
(2) WHAT THE PAPER CONTAINS. Abbott and Machta, J. Stat. Phys. 176:214-227 (2019), arXiv:1710.09351, Eq. (12):
      S(x) = log L - L exp(-(2 pi)^2 rho^2) [ 1 + (128 pi^6/3) rho^4 rho'^2 ]
which is exactly the functional this project has been using, kappa_AM = 128 pi^6/3 included. Immediately after,
they write its Euler-Lagrange equation:
      0 = rho^4 rho'' + 2 rho^3 rho'^2 - 4 pi^2 rho^5 rho'^2 + 3/(32 pi^4) rho.
(3) ITS CONSEQUENCE FOR X, WHICH IS THEIR OWN ARGUMENT. To get eta = 1/3 they balance the last two terms. That
balance is 4 pi^2 rho^5 rho'^2 = 3/(32 pi^4) rho, i.e. rho^4 rho'^2 = 3/(128 pi^6), i.e.
      X := kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 = (128 pi^6/3)(3/(128 pi^6)) = 1, EXACTLY.
Checked numerically: kappa_AM * 3/(128 pi^6) = 1.000000. Direct integration of their ODE from their stated
boundary condition rho(0) = 1 is stiff and blows up by x = 0.5 for every rho'(0) tried, so the balance argument
is the usable route - and it is theirs, not ours.
(4) AGAINST THIS PROJECT'S NUMBERS. Certified Gaussian states give X = 1.7165 down to 1.7018 over d = 14 to 24;
certified binomial states extrapolated in 1/n give 1.7227 at d = 12; 449's parameter-free derivation from the
UNTRUNCATED stationarity condition gives them to an rms of 0.006 %. So their local two-term equation and the
exact nonlocal one differ by a factor of 1.7071 in X.
(5) THIS IDENTIFIES THE 0.59 THAT HAS SAT IN THE RECORD SINCE 356. 1/1.7071 = 0.5858. The recurring "0.59",
recorded then as "a symptom of the wrong FORM", is exactly the ratio of the two-term LOCAL truncation to the
exact NONLOCAL answer. It was never a coefficient to be fitted; it is what truncating the functional costs.
(6) WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE IN THEIR RESULT. A constant X of ANY value gives rho proportional to
x^(1/3), so their exponent - log K ~ I^(4/3), K ~ L^(4/3) - is untouched. K goes as X^(1/6), so the prefactor
moves by 1.7071^(1/6) = 1.0932, +9.32 %. Their scaling law stands; its coefficient does not.
(7) NOVELTY, CHECKED AND LABELLED. Web searches today for a follow-up deriving the profile equation, and for the
nonlocal stationarity condition in this form, returned nothing. That is a LIMITED check - two searches and the
source paper - and it is recorded as such, not as an establishment of novelty. The one question it cannot settle
is whether Eq. (12) was ever INTENDED to hold pointwise for the optimal profile (where rho varies threefold)
rather than perturbatively about a uniform comb under their ordering (11). That is a question about the authors'
intent, and no run of ours can answer it.
(8) CONSEQUENT ACTION. A two-page note on the coefficient was written (Firdaus_2026_abbott_machta_note.pdf,
builder build_note.py).
Gates: no gate word used. (1) records that we held a belief which blocked an obvious comparison for weeks; (7)
labels the novelty check as limited rather than claiming NEW.

AMENDMENT 452. 450's "SCISSORS" WAS OUR OWN MARGIN, NOT AN OBSTRUCTION. THE CROSS-CHANNEL CHECK AT TWO
COEFFICIENTS IS AVAILABLE, AND THE BINOMIAL SITS 0.02 % BELOW THE DERIVED LAW WHERE THE GAUSSIAN AGREES TO
0.006 %.
(1) 450 concluded that no certified binomial state has both a long 1/n lever and a depth where the trial family
is valid. That was drawn from d = 12 (family marginal) and d >= 16 (lever short), and from requiring each state's
window to cover d + 2. Both choices were ours. The family's condition is rho^3/b > UM, which at the binomial's
rho(14) = 0.652 gives 15.2 against a reach of 12 - comfortably valid - and n = 320's window reaches 15.5. So
d = 13 to 15 satisfies both at once, with all EIGHTEEN certified states and a 1/n lever of 2.70x.
(2) THE CHECK, RUN:
     d     states   linear X(inf)  rms      quadratic X(inf)  rms      rho(inf)   X* derived   difference
     13      18      1.718767    1.1e-04      1.720829     5.9e-06    0.63631     1.720470     -0.0209 %
     14      18      1.716869    1.1e-04      1.718925     5.1e-06    0.65191     1.718601     -0.0188 %
     15      18      1.715160    9.8e-05      1.717009     3.5e-06    0.66680     1.716771     -0.0139 %
  The quadratic is again required (linear rms twenty times worse), as 447 found, and it is well conditioned here.
(3) SO THE TWO CHANNELS DO NOT AGREE AT THE GAUSSIAN'S OWN ACCURACY. The Gaussian two-coefficient law reproduces
its measurement to an rms of 0.006 % (449), which 449(3) showed is the method's jitter. The binomial sits
0.014 to 0.021 % BELOW the same law, one-signed, shrinking with d. That is three times the Gaussian's figure and
it does not look like noise.
(4) CANDIDATES, none tested. (a) The binomial's 1/n extrapolation may need a cubic term - eighteen states over a
2.70x lever settled linear vs quadratic, but not quadratic vs cubic, and 447 showed exactly this kind of
under-determination once already. (b) The binomial's Fisher coordinate carries O(1/n) corrections of its own -
the wall chain's first gap moves 3.1259965 at n = 860 against the asymptotic 3.1256666 - so the map itself is
only asymptotically the universal one, and an O(1/n) error in the coordinate feeds straight into rho and X.
(c) A genuine channel dependence in the law, which the derivation forbids, since psi is the same. Test order:
(a) then (b), because both are cheap and (c) would have to survive them.
(5) A DELIVERABLE HAD TO BE CORRECTED. The note drafted for Abbott and Machta stated in section 5 that this check
was blocked. That was 450's conclusion and it is wrong. The note has been rebuilt with the numbers of (2) and the
open item restated as (3) and (4).
Gates: no gate word used. (1) records that our own margin manufactured the obstruction; (5) records a correction
to a document already produced.

AMENDMENT 453. 452(4) CANDIDATE (a) RUN: THE BINOMIAL EXTRAPOLATION CANNOT RESOLVE 0.02 % AT ALL, SO 452(3)'s
"THE TWO CHANNELS DO NOT AGREE" IS WITHDRAWN.
(1) THE TEST. Fit the measured X(d) against 1/n at orders 1, 2 and 3 over the eighteen certified binomial states
and read the extrapolated value:
     d    linear                quadratic             cubic
     13   1.718767 rms 1.1e-04  1.720829 rms 5.9e-06  1.720234 rms 5.9e-06
     14   1.716869 rms 1.1e-04  1.718925 rms 5.1e-06  1.717642 rms 4.8e-06
     15   1.715160 rms 9.8e-05  1.717009 rms 3.5e-06  1.714908 rms 2.1e-06
  The cubic fits as well as the quadratic or better - at d = 15 it is nearly twice as good - and yet the value it
  extrapolates to differs by 0.0035 at d = 13, 0.0013 at d = 14 and 0.0021 at d = 15, which against the derived
  law swings the comparison from -0.021 % to +0.014 %, from -0.019 % to +0.056 %, and from -0.014 % to +0.109 %.
(2) CONCLUSION, AND IT WITHDRAWS OUR OWN AMENDMENT FROM AN HOUR AGO. The residual is not resolved by the data; it
is inside the extrapolation's own ambiguity. The binomial set - eighteen states, n = 320 to 865, a lever of
2.70x - can establish that a quadratic is needed and cannot choose between quadratic and cubic. Its resolving
power on X(infinity) is therefore about 0.1 %, five times the effect 452(3) called a disagreement. The two
channels are CONSISTENT; the binomial simply cannot test the law below ~0.1 %, and 452(3) is withdrawn.
(3) THIS IS THE SAME ERROR AS 447, MADE AGAIN, ONE STEP FURTHER OUT. In 447 we read a linear extrapolation as if
the lever determined it, and the fix was to test the next order. Here we read a quadratic the same way. The rule
We should have applied to ourselves without prompting: AN EXTRAPOLATED VALUE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT UNTIL THE NEXT
ORDER HAS BEEN SHOWN NOT TO MOVE IT. Adding it to the standing rules.
(4) WHAT STANDS. The Gaussian figure (449: rms 0.006 %, itself at the method's jitter) is the only quantitative
test of the derived law at that level. The binomial's role is what 447(3) said - a cross-channel CONSISTENCY
check, at the ~0.1 % its data supports - and 451's comparison against Abbott-Machta's X = 1 is unaffected, since
that disagreement is a factor of 1.7 and dwarfs every extrapolation ambiguity here.
(5) DOCUMENTS CORRECTED AGAIN. The note on the coefficient stated the 0.02 % gap as an unexplained
disagreement. Rebuilt to state the binomial's resolving power instead.
Gates: no gate word used. The amendment withdraws the amendment before it and names the repeated error as a rule.

AMENDMENT 454. THE A-WALK FINISHED; THE COUNT THRESHOLD'S UNCERTAINTY IS DOMINATED BY HOW THE VANISHING SIGNAL
IS MODELLED, AND 438(3)'s "0.51 +- 0.02" UNDERSTATED IT.
(1) THE WALK (bmsy747q3, A = 46.3837 upward at fixed K = 70, cut by its two-hour cap after four steps) gives the
centre signal as a smooth monotone sequence rather than the two points 438(3) had:
     A          46.3837    46.4487   46.4837   46.5137   46.5837   46.6837   46.7837
     off-atom  -2.030e-17  +2.437e-16 +1.089e-15 +2.119e-15 +5.879e-15 +1.547e-14 +3.282e-14
  Every state above 46.3837 certifies to 1e-24 or better and every one is "centre positive", i.e. NOT optimal at
  this count - so they are a clean map of the signal, not a set of optima.
(2) THE POSITIVE BRANCH IS QUADRATIC, NOT LINEAR. Fitting S = c (A - A*)^p to the six positive points gives
p = 2.054 with a log-residual rms of 0.049, and A* = 46.41326. A linear model on the first two positive points
gives A* = 46.4386. The two-point interpolation 438(3) used - which straddles the near-zero NEGATIVE point at
46.3837 - gives 46.38870. The three disagree by up to 0.05 in A.
(3) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE THRESHOLD. On the certified state's own fitted profile, N(A*) - n_half comes out
     two-point through the negative point : 0.53045
     power-law fit to the positive branch : 0.55436
  and the other size in 438(3) (n_half = 29) was obtained by the two-point route as well, so its 0.49230 is
  biased the same way. The honest range across models and sizes is about 0.49 to 0.57, NOT 0.51 +- 0.02.
Exactly 1/2 remains inside that range and remains untested.
(4) WHY THE MODELS DISAGREE, stated as the open question rather than papered over. A signal that vanishes as
(A - A*)^2 cannot change sign at A*, yet the certified state below the transition has a genuinely negative
signal (-2.03e-17, on a state whose residual is 2.58e-28). Either the negative branch has its own much smaller
scale - so the signal is smooth but strongly asymmetric about A* - or the positive branch's apparent p = 2 is a
local effective exponent over a range where a higher term dominates. Distinguishing them needs states BETWEEN
46.3837 and 46.4487, which the walk stepped straight over; that is a walk with dA = 0.01, not a new idea.
(5) PATTERN, AND THE RULE FROM 453 APPLIED TO OURSELVES AGAIN. This is the third time today a number of ours was
quoted more tightly than its model dependence allowed (447 linear-vs-quadratic in 1/n; 453 quadratic-vs-cubic;
now linear-vs-quadratic in the transition signal). The rule stands and generalises: A FITTED OR EXTRAPOLATED
NUMBER CARRIES THE SPREAD ACROSS REASONABLE MODELS, NOT THE SCATTER WITHIN ONE.
Gates: no gate word used. The amendment widens our own error bar and names the computation that would close it.

AMENDMENT 455. 452(4) CANDIDATE (b) KILLED: THE BINOMIAL APPROACHES ITS LIMIT AS 1/n, NOT 1/sqrt(n), SO THE
EXTRAPOLATION BASIS WAS RIGHT AND ONLY THE LEVER IS SHORT.
(1) THE IDEA UNDER TEST. The variance-stabilising coordinate t = 2 sqrt(n) asin sqrt(x/n) is EXACT for the
binomial, but the channel's kernel expressed in it is only asymptotically the unit Gaussian; its leading
correction is a skewness, which is O(1/sqrt n). If that reached X, every extrapolation in this record would have
been done in the wrong variable, and the quadratic-versus-cubic fight of 453 would be the symptom.
(2) THE TEST, on the eighteen certified states at d = 13, 14, 15, fitting the measured X against each variable at
orders 1, 2, 3:
     d = 14   1/n        linear rms 1.1e-04   quadratic 5.1e-06   cubic 4.8e-06   spread of X(inf) 2.06e-03
     d = 14   1/sqrt(n)  linear rms 9.3e-04   quadratic 5.5e-06   cubic 4.8e-06   spread of X(inf) 7.24e-02
  and the same pattern at d = 13 and 15. In 1/n the linear fit is EIGHT TIMES better and the spread of the
  extrapolated value across orders is THIRTY TIMES smaller. The data prefers 1/n decisively.
(3) WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER STRUCTURALLY. X = kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 is even in the kernel's asymmetry - it
depends on the density and its gradient, not on the sign of the skew - so the odd O(1/sqrt n) correction cancels
and the leading surviving term is the even O(1/n) one. The measurement and the structure agree.
(4) WHAT THIS LEAVES. 453 stands unchanged: the binomial resolves X only to about 0.1 % because quadratic and
cubic in 1/n fit equally well. But the cause is now known to be the LEVER, not the variable. The certified set
runs n = 320 to 865, a factor of 2.70; the cure is a certified state at substantially smaller n. The geometric
constraint is that the bulk window, [8, 0.55 h] with h = pi sqrt(n)/2, must still reach the comparison depth:
d = 13 needs n >= 227, d = 12 needs n >= 193. A state near n = 240 would take the lever to 3.6, and near n = 200
to 4.5 at d = 12.
(5) AND IT CANNOT BE REACHED BY WALKING. The count changes roughly every 17 in n (36 atoms at n = 320, 56 at
n = 658), so a fixed-K walk down from 320 leaves its plateau within about eight steps; reaching n = 240 crosses
five count changes. It has to come from the law-seeded builder, which is what failed at n = 480 today - there the
seeder produced 22 interior atoms and the run reported off-atom max +1.48e-07, i.e. one atom short, and could not
build 23 from the chain. Launching the same builder at n = 240.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) states an idea that would have invalidated much of today and (2) kills it.

AMENDMENT 456. THE BINOMIAL EXTRAPOLATION HAS NO USABLE LEVER, AND n = 320 - WHICH I USED ALL DAY TO PROVIDE ONE
- IS AN UNDERDETERMINED FIT. 436, 447, 452, 453 AND 455 ALL REST ON IT.
(1) HOW IT SURFACED. 455(4) said the binomial's limit was the lever, so we built five new certified states at
n = 210 to 250 (q211, seconds each, residuals to 8.06e-35). Adding them made the extrapolation WORSE, not better:
at d = 12 the order-3 fit rms went from 5.9e-06 to 5.7e-04 and the spread across orders 2 to 4 from 2.06e-03 to
2.75e-02. That is the opposite of what a longer lever does, so we counted the data instead of theorising.
(2) THE COUNT, which we should have made weeks ago. The profile model has FIVE free parameters. Bulk atoms in the
window [8, 0.55 h] per state:
     n = 220, 230, 240, 250   ->  3 atoms      n = 320  ->  4 atoms
     n = 658 to 679           ->  9 atoms      n = 856 to 865 -> 12 atoms
  Five of the twenty-two states have FEWER ATOMS THAN PARAMETERS. Their profile fit rms is 5e-16, 3e-15, 2e-15,
  0.00e+00, 2e-15 - machine zero, the signature of an underdetermined system, not of a good fit - and their
  X(12) comes out 1.604, 1.610, 1.611, 1.613, 1.631 against 1.677 to 1.688 for the determined ones. Those are not
  measurements.
(3) n = 320 IS ONE OF THEM, AND IT CARRIED TODAY'S CONCLUSIONS. 447 used n = 320 specifically to extend the lever
and concluded from it that "the linear fit fails outright and a quadratic is required". That conclusion rests on
a four-atom, five-parameter fit. 452, 453 and 455 all used the same eighteen-state set. Every binomial
extrapolation figure produced today is therefore suspect: 447's 1.722701, 452's -0.021 %, 453's "resolves to
~0.1 %", 455's comparison of 1/n against 1/sqrt(n).
(4) WHAT IS LEFT OF THE LEVER. Restricting to states whose fit is determined leaves n = 658 to 865, a lever of
1.31x, in two tight clusters at 658-679 and 856-865 - so a linear fit is effectively determined by two points and
nothing determines the next order. Worse, extrapolating from 1/n in [1.16e-03, 1.52e-03] to 1/n = 0 is a 3.2x
extrapolation BEYOND the data, with a form the data cannot verify.
(5) SO THE BINOMIAL CANNOT TEST THE COEFFICIENT AT ALL. Not to 0.006 %, not to 0.1 %. What the binomial states DO
establish, with no extrapolation anywhere, stands untouched: the wall chain 3.1256666 and its 1/n approach; that
the interior obeys the same FORM with X nearly constant; and the local-channel principle. The quantitative test
of the derived law rests on the GAUSSIAN alone (449: rms 0.006 %, itself at the method's jitter).
(6) THIS IS THE SAME ERROR ONE LAYER DOWN. 453 and 454 caught us quoting numbers more tightly than their model
dependence allowed. Here we did something worse: we never asked whether the underlying per-state measurement was
determined at all. New rule, added to the standing set: BEFORE FITTING ACROSS STATES, COUNT EACH STATE'S DATA
AGAINST ITS OWN MODEL'S PARAMETERS. A fit residual at machine zero is a warning, not a triumph.
(7) WALL ANATOMY. MATERIAL: the binomial's bulk window is [8, 0.55 h] with h = pi sqrt(n)/2, so the atom count in
it grows only as sqrt(n) while the 1/n lever needs small n - the two demands are in direct opposition, and this
time the scissors is verified by counting rather than assumed as in 450. METHOD: count bulk atoms against model
parameters per state. WHY HERE: at n = 250 the window is [8, 13.7] and holds three atoms; nine are needed before
the five-parameter model is even determined, which needs n >~ 650. WHAT IS BEHIND IT: either a REDUCED profile
model (three parameters, no curvature) that small-n states can determine - at the cost of biasing X by dropping
the drift - or a direct measurement of X that does not go through the five-parameter fit at all. The second is
the right one and has not been attempted.
Gates: no gate word used. The amendment invalidates five of our own amendments from today and names the rule that
would have prevented it.

AMENDMENT 457. 456(2) WAS WRONG ABOUT THE SMALL-n STATES: A PARAMETER-FREE ESTIMATOR REPRODUCES THEIR X, SO THE
VALUES ARE REAL. 456's CONCLUSION SURVIVES, FOR A DIFFERENT REASON.
(1) 456(7) said the right instrument was a direct measurement of X not routed through the five-parameter fit.
q285's pointwise estimator is exactly that - rho = 1/gm and rho' = (1/g - 1/mid)/gm from three consecutive
atoms, no fit, no parameters, no window. Applied in the Fisher coordinate to all twenty-three certified binomial
states:
     n        210     220     230     240     250     320  |   658     865
   pointwise 1.5626  1.6006  1.6084  1.6053  1.6023  1.6301 | 1.6761  1.6868
   5-par fit    -    1.6042  1.6099  1.6112  1.6126  1.6310 | 1.6770  1.6878
  The two agree to about 0.4 % at every state. The small-n values are therefore MEASUREMENTS, not artefacts of an
  underdetermined fit, and 456(2)'s "those are not measurements" is WITHDRAWN. What 456(2) got right is narrower:
  those fits ARE underdetermined (three atoms, five parameters, residual at machine zero) - it just happens that
  the quantity read off them survives, because the pointwise estimate confirms it independently.
(2) SO THE REAL FACT IS A STRONG FINITE-n DEPENDENCE. At fixed d = 12, X runs 1.60 at n = 220 to 1.687 at
n = 865 - about 5 % - and it is still climbing at the largest n available. That is the whole difficulty, and it
is physical rather than instrumental.
(3) 456(5)'s CONCLUSION STANDS, WITH ITS REASON REPLACED. Extrapolating the pointwise values in 1/n over all
twenty-three states (lever 4.12x):
     order 1 -> X(inf) = 1.719613   order 2 -> 1.707098   order 3 -> 1.759627,  all with rms about 5.5e-03
  The three disagree by 5 % - far more than the effect being tested - and none of the fits is good. So the
  binomial still cannot test the coefficient. The reason is NOT that its small-n data are garbage (457(1)); it is
  that the approach to the limit is slow, large, and of unknown form over the range available.
(4) ONE OBSERVATION NOT TO OVERREAD. The order-2 extrapolation lands at 1.707098, which is the Gaussian's value
to four digits. Given that order 1 and order 3 give 1.720 and 1.760 on equally poor fits, that is a coincidence
of one model among three, and it is recorded ONLY so that we do not rediscover it later and mistake it for
evidence. It is not evidence.
(5) TWO WITHDRAWALS IN TWO HOURS, BOTH MINE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. 456 over-corrected 453 by declaring the
small-n data invalid; 457 restores them and keeps the conclusion. The stable content across all three is: the
Gaussian carries the quantitative test (449), the binomial confirms form and boundary structure with no
extrapolation, and no binomial number should be quoted to better than a few per cent. That is what the
note now says, and it needs no further change.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) withdraws our own amendment from two hours ago; (4) pre-emptively labels a
suggestive coincidence as not evidence.

AMENDMENT 458. THE FINE WALK ANSWERS 454(4): THE CENTRE SIGNAL IS STRONGLY ASYMMETRIC ABOUT THE TRANSITION, AND
ITS SCALE IS 439(3)'s SCREENING BARRIER EVALUATED AT THE CENTRE.
(1) THE NEGATIVE BRANCH, newly resolved by the dA = 0.01 walk (each state certified below 1e-28):
     A          46.3837      46.3937      46.4037
     off-atom  -2.030e-17   -1.684e-17   -1.317e-17      all OPTIMAL
  That is a slope of about +3.6e-16 per unit A, which reaches zero near A = 46.440. The first POSITIVE point,
  46.4487 at +2.437e-16, then sits 79 times higher than that slope would put it. So 454(4)'s two alternatives are
  decided: the signal is SMOOTH BUT STRONGLY ASYMMETRIC about the transition - nearly flat and slightly negative
  below, steeply rising above - and the apparent p = 2.054 of the positive branch is that steep side, not a
  local effective exponent of a symmetric function.
(2) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE THRESHOLD. The two-point estimate 46.38870 (438(3)) and the positive-branch power law
46.41326 (454(2)) are both biased; the negative branch's own linear trend gives 46.440, and the true crossing
lies between 46.4037 (last OPTIMAL) and 46.4487 (first positive). The walk is still filling that interval, and
when it closes the threshold will be read from a BRACKET rather than from any model - which is the first
model-free determination of it in this record.
(3) WHERE THE 1e-16 SCALE COMES FROM. 439(3) measured the barrier against inserting an atom as
-ln(barrier) = 2.8103 d^(2/3) - 0.3684 over d = 3.8 to 36.8. Extrapolated to the centre, d = A = 46.38, that
predicts 2.5e-16. The observed centre signal at the transition is 2.8e-16 to 6.8e-16 - a ratio of 1.1 to 2.7 on
a 26 % extension of the fit. So the count transition occurs at a signal scale SET BY THE SCREENING BARRIER at
the centre, which is why it is 1e-16 and not 1e-3.
(4) WHAT THE BARRIER DOES NOT DO. Across A = 46.38 to 46.78 the predicted barrier changes by only 1.23x while
the centre signal changes by 119x and changes sign. So the barrier fixes the SCALE and nothing else; the
A-dependence is the KKT condition itself crossing zero. Recorded so that the agreement in (3) is not overread as
the barrier law governing the transition.
Gates: no gate word used. (4) limits the claim in (3) to what was measured.

AMENDMENT 459. THE DERIVED LAW PREDICTS THE SUPPORT SIZE ITSELF, TO 0.14 OF AN ATOM - AND IN THAT OBSERVABLE
ABBOTT-MACHTA's COEFFICIENT IS FIVE ATOMS LOW.
(1) A CORRECTION FIRST, CAUGHT BEFORE IT WAS RECORDED. Our first attempt integrated rho from d = 0 using the
derived X*(rho) evaluated at rho down to 0.29, by CLAMPING the argument. X*(rho) is a cubic fitted over
rho in [0.62, 0.90] and 432(8) says it is not even defined below that; extrapolating it to 0.29 inflated N(A) by
0.44 of an atom and would have put the threshold at 0.98 instead of 0.47. Redone with the law FROZEN at the edge
of its validity and 443's near-wall construction below it, N(46.3837) = 34.50961 against the state's own fitted
34.5256 - agreement to 0.016 of an atom, matching 434(3).
(2) THE SUPPORT SIZE, DERIVED. With N_total(A) = 2 [ int_0^A rho dd - T ], rho^3 = rho_0^3 + 3 sqrt(X/kappa_AM) d,
rho_0^3 = 0.02382 and T = 0.465 (the mean of the threshold band), against eleven certified Gaussian states:
     A         21.28   29.85   35.55   35.60   35.65   40.95   41.08   46.38(x4)
   certified     24      38      48      48      48      58      58      68
   derived    24.14   37.89   47.80   47.89   47.98   57.67   57.91   68.04
   error      +0.14   -0.11   -0.20   -0.11   -0.02   -0.33   -0.09   +0.04
  mean error -0.04 atoms, rms 0.14. The derived law reproduces the NUMBER OF MASS POINTS, which is the quantity
  the source paper is about.
(3) AND IT DISCRIMINATES AGAINST Eq. (12). Running the identical calculation with Abbott-Machta's own
X = 1 (451): predicted counts 22.32, 34.96, 44.05, 44.14, 44.22, 53.11, 53.34, 62.62 against certified 24, 38,
48, 48, 48, 58, 58, 68 - mean error -4.30 atoms, rms 4.44, systematically low and GROWING with A, reaching -5.38
at A = 46.38. Asymptotically N_total = 0.3684 A^(4/3) from their equation against 0.4027 A^(4/3) from the derived
law. This is a thirty-fold difference in rms error, in their own observable, on data certified to 1e-20.
(4) ROBUST TO THE THRESHOLD, which is still being bracketed. T enters as -2T, so the whole T band [0.32, 0.55]
moves every prediction by at most +-0.5 of an atom. The derived law stays within half an atom throughout and
Abbott-Machta's stays four to five atoms low. The discrimination does not depend on the unfinished part.
(5) THE POISSON CONSEQUENCE, STATED AND NOT CLAIMED. The Poisson Fisher coordinate is t = 2 sqrt(x), so
x in [0, A] has Fisher length 2 sqrt(A) and the half-length is sqrt(A). The same law then gives
N*(A) ~ 0.4027 A^(2/3), which lies strictly between the published Omega(sqrt A) (Dytso-Barletta-Shamai 2021) and
O(A) (Dytso 2024). IT CANNOT BE TESTED ON THIS RECORD'S POISSON STATES: at A = 100 to 250 the Fisher half-length
is only sqrt(A) = 10.0 to 15.8, which is entirely inside the near-wall region (d <~ 13) where the constant-X form
does not hold, so those states are boundary-dominated from end to end. As expected in that regime the derived
value under-predicts - 8.67, 11.46, 13.93, 16.20 against 11, 14, 20, 23 - and that discrepancy is not evidence
against the exponent, because the asymptotic form was never applicable there. A real test needs a certified
Poisson state with sqrt(A) >> 13, say A >~ 1600, and no Poisson state has ever certified (438(1)).
(6) WALL ANATOMY for the Poisson exponent. MATERIAL: the asymptotic form needs a bulk region, i.e. Fisher
half-length well beyond the ~13-unit near-wall layer; the Poisson's half-length is sqrt(A), so it needs A in the
thousands where the Gaussian needs only A ~ 40. METHOD: integrate the derived rho over the channel's own Fisher
length. WHY HERE: the square root is the whole difficulty - the Poisson buys Fisher length very slowly in A.
WHAT IS BEHIND IT: a certified Poisson state at A ~ 1000-2000. The q311/q312 states sit at A = 1128 to 1151,
exactly the right size, and floor at 1e-07 against the 1e-20 bar. That floor is now the single obstacle between
this record and a statement about the open problem's exponent.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) records an error caught before publication; (5) states a consequence and refuses to
claim it; (6) names precisely what stands in the way.

AMENDMENT 460. THE POISSON STATE'S SHAPE IS ALREADY RIGHT - THIRD CHANNEL, 0.065 % - AND ITS RESIDUAL IS THE
SOFT MODE, NOT A WRONG PROFILE. "MORE STEPS" IS REJECTED BY ARITHMETIC.
(1) "MORE STEPS" IS NOT AN OPTION, and our own standing note said it was. At damping 0.03 the observed ratios are
5.898/5.931 = 0.99444, 5.867/5.898 = 0.99474, 5.837/5.867 = 0.99489 - a linear rate of 0.9947 per step. Reaching
1e-20 from 5.837e-08 needs ln(1.7e-13)/ln(0.9947) = 5537 STEPS, and at the observed 190 s per step that is twelve
days. 438(1)'s "they need more steps, not analysis" is WITHDRAWN: they need a different method.
(2) THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT CHANGES THE PICTURE. Using q285's pointwise estimator - no fit, no parameters - on the
q312 Poisson state (A = 1151.33, residual 5.81e-08, 46 atoms, Fisher length 67.86):
     d from the wall   2.72   4.89   6.82   8.61  10.30  11.91  13.45  14.95
     pointwise X      1.668  1.711  1.721  1.723  1.721  1.719  1.716  1.713
     bulk mean over d = 8 to 24: 1.7053, spread 0.0603, eleven points
  The DERIVED law says 1.7064. Agreement 0.065 %. Both boundary chains match too, with no extrapolation: from
  the ORIGIN 3.12567, 2.26035, 1.98211, 1.82110 against the Poisson origin chain 3.1257, 2.2604, 1.9821, 1.8211;
  from the AMPLITUDE WALL 2.7183, 2.16941, 1.93505 against the Gaussian wall chain 2.71884, 2.16960, 1.93516.
(3) SO IT IS A THIRD CHANNEL, and the earlier attempt failed for an instrument reason. The Poisson comparison in
this record was previously abandoned because a five-parameter profile fit gave rms 1.3e-02 and X values of 2.12,
1.82, 1.40, 0.88 - garbage. The pointwise estimator, which needs only three consecutive atoms, gives a smooth
profile agreeing with the derived law to 0.065 %. The fit was the wrong instrument for an uncertified state.
(4) AND THE RESIDUAL IS THE SOFT MODE. The less converged state at the same A (q311, residual 8.21e-07) gives a
bulk mean of 1.6382 with a spread of 0.1751; the better one (5.81e-08) gives 1.7053 with a spread of 0.0603. The
SHAPE converges toward the derived law as the residual falls, which is what a soft-mode-limited solve looks like:
the profile is right and one nearly-flat direction is not resolved. CAVEAT, stated plainly: the state is NOT
certified, so this is a measurement on an uncertified configuration and is quoted as such.
(5) THE SUPPORT SIZE AT A SIZE WHERE THE ASYMPTOTIC FORM APPLIES. The Fisher half-length here is 33.9, well
beyond the ~13-unit near-wall layer, so 459(5)'s objection does not apply. Integrating the derived rho from each
end with its own constant - the origin at rho_0^3 ~ 0.0042 (the binomial wall's value, since binomial wall =
Poisson origin) and the amplitude wall at 0.02382 - gives N = 45.210, or 44.28 after one threshold at each end,
against 46 observed: -1.72 atoms, -3.7 %. THREE things can absorb that and none is settled: the state is not
certified so 46 may not be the optimal count; rho_0^3 at the Poisson origin is borrowed from the binomial and is
only asymptotically equal to it; and the threshold convention for a channel whose two ends differ has not been
worked out. So this is consistent, not confirmatory.
(6) THE STATEMENT THAT FOLLOWS, and its status. N*(A) -> 0.4027 A^(2/3) for the amplitude-constrained Poisson
channel, which sits strictly inside the published bracket Omega(sqrt A) <= N* <= O(A). It is DERIVED from the
bulk law and the channel's Fisher length, it is CONSISTENT with the one state large enough to test it (-3.7 %),
and it is NOT confirmed, because that state is uncertified and three conventions in (5) are open.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) withdraws our own standing instruction; (4) and (5) label measurements on an
uncertified state as such; (6) separates derived from confirmed.

AMENDMENT 461. THE BRACKET CLOSED: THE COUNT THRESHOLD IS NOT 1/2, AND THE DERIVED LAW PREDICTS THE INTEGER
SUPPORT SIZE EXACTLY ON 13 OF 13 CERTIFIED STATES WHERE Eq. (12) GETS 1 OF 13.
(1) THE BRACKET. The dA = 0.01 walk closed it: A = 46.4337 is OPTIMAL with off-atom max -9.666e-19, A = 46.4437
is centre positive at +1.524e-16. The negative branch ran -2.030e-17, -1.684e-17, -1.317e-17, -9.308e-18,
-5.240e-18, -9.666e-19 with smoothly accelerating differences 3.46, 3.67, 3.86, 4.07, 4.27 (x1e-18), then jumped
by 1.53e-16 - a factor of 36 - confirming 458's asymmetry.
(2) THE THRESHOLD, READ FROM BRACKETS AT THREE SIZES, no model of how the signal vanishes:
     n_half 19: [0.46866, 0.58743]   width 0.119
     n_half 29: [0.46982, 0.58695]   width 0.117
     n_half 34: [0.57995, 0.58943]   width 0.0095      <- the fine walk
  All three overlap; the intersection is [0.57995, 0.58695], width 0.007. EXACTLY 1/2 IS OUTSIDE IT. Both our
  earlier figures - 438(3)'s 0.51 +- 0.02 and 454's 0.49-0.57 - were too low and are superseded; both came from

(3) CANDIDATE CLOSED FORMS, LABELLED AND NOT CLAIMED. Inside [0.57995, 0.58695] lie 1/X = 1/1.70637 = 0.58604
and 7/12 = 0.58333. Both are UNCHECKED. We record them only so that a later encounter is not mistaken for a
discovery; a bracket of width 0.007 cannot select among them and nothing here suggests either.
(4) A CORRECTION TO 459(2). We reported the support size as "rms 0.14 of an atom" from the CONTINUOUS formula
N_total = 2[N(A) - T]. That conflated a continuous quantity with an integer count: N(A) - n_half sweeps a unit
interval across a count plateau, so the 0.14 only reflected that our states happen to cluster between 0.35 and
0.58 of their plateaus. The correct statement is an integer one, and it is stronger:
       n_half = floor( N(A) - T ) + 1,   N(A) = int_0^A rho dd from the derived law, T from (2).
(5) IT IS EXACT ON EVERY CERTIFIED STATE. 13 of 13 Gaussian states, A = 21.28 to 46.43, predicted exactly, with
one constant and no free parameter. The same calculation with Abbott-Machta's X = 1 gets 1 of 13, short by one
atom at A = 29.85 and by TWO atoms at every A from 35.55 to 46.43. HONEST LIMIT: the 13/13 constrains T only to
exceed the largest observed plateau position (0.532 on this N), so it does not pin T; (2)'s bracket pins T, and
(5) is a separate statement. The 1/13 for X = 1 is robust to T, because being short by two atoms cannot be
absorbed by a constant bounded in [0, 1].
(6) WHERE THIS LEAVES THE CHAIN. Derived, with kappa_AM and psi as the only inputs: the bulk law (three channels
- Gaussian 0.006 %, Poisson 0.065 %, binomial form-only); the near-wall configuration to 1e-04; and now the
integer support size, exactly, on every certified Gaussian state. Measured, not derived: T, to a width of 0.007.
Not confirmed: the Poisson exponent N* -> 0.4027 A^(2/3), which needs a certified Poisson state (460(6)).
Gates: no gate word used. (3) refuses two closed forms; (4) withdraws our own headline figure and replaces it
