AMENDMENT 462. THE POISSON FLOOR IS A TRUNCATED DIRECTION, NOT SLOW CONVERGENCE. THE CAP TEST FAILED ITS
PRE-REGISTERED THRESHOLD AND IDENTIFIED THE MECHANISM ANYWAY.
(1) THE TEST, pre-registered in 461: raise SVDCAP from 0.05 to 0.2 on the q312 state and ask whether
the residual falls below 5.8085e-08 x 0.9947^60 = 4.2e-08 in sixty steps. If yes, the cap was limiting the step;
if no, it was not.
(2) RESULT: it did not. The solve reported "floor 5.8085e-08 after 1 steps, stuck = True", history
['5.808e-8@stuck'] - i.e. it could not take a single useful step and the residual is unchanged to five figures.
The hypothesis is REJECTED.
(3) BUT THE FAILURE LOCATES THE MECHANISM. Raising the cap from 0.05 to 0.2 removed ALL progress. So the slow
progress at SVDCAP = 0.05 was being made in directions whose singular values lie between 0.05 and 0.2, and
everything below 0.05 is already truncated out of the step. The screening law puts the soft mode at
sigma_min ~ exp(-2.81 x 33.9^(2/3)) ~ 1e-13, which is ten orders BELOW the cap. So the soft direction contributes
nothing to any step the solver takes, and the residual floor of 5.8e-08 is the part of the residual that lives in
the truncated subspace. That is why it floors rather than converging, and why 460(1)'s twelve-day extrapolation
of the observed linear rate was the wrong model of the problem - the rate 0.9947 is the stiff directions grinding
down, not the soft one approaching anything.
(4) THE CONSEQUENCE, WHICH REVERSES THE DIRECTION OF THE FIX. The cap has to go DOWN, not up, to admit the soft
direction. The tension that the cap exists to manage is explicit: with sigma_min ~ 1e-13 and a residual of
5.8e-08, an untruncated Newton step along that direction is 5.8e-08 / 1e-13 ~ 6e+05, which would destroy the
ordering of the atoms. So admitting the direction requires a trust region or a line search along it, not simply
a smaller cap - which is precisely what the Gaussian solver's "soft-mode search" does, and what the q220 walk
logs show it doing at every step. A tenfold cap reduction is now running as the next cheap probe, with the same
4.2e-08 threshold.
(5) WALL ANATOMY, now with the material named. MATERIAL: the KKT Jacobian's smallest singular value at
A ~ 1151 is about 1e-13 by the screening law, ten orders below the solver's SVD cap, so the corresponding
direction is truncated from every step and its residual component is structurally unreachable. METHOD: sweep the
cap and read whether progress survives. WHY HERE: sigma_min falls as exp(-c A^(2/3)), so the Poisson at the size
needed for a bulk region (A ~ 1000+, Fisher half-length 33.9) is exactly where the mode becomes untouchable -
the Gaussian at A ~ 46 has a Fisher half-length of 46 and the same problem would appear there too, except that
its soft-mode search handles it. WHAT IS BEHIND IT: a line search along the truncated direction, which exists in
the Gaussian path (q206/q220) and is the thing to port or enable here. That is a solver change, not a new idea.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) records the pre-registered hypothesis as rejected; (3) takes the diagnosis from
the failure rather than from the hope.

AMENDMENT 463. 462(3) IS WITHDRAWN: THE POISSON RUNS WERE BLIND. THE MISSING SOFT-MODE LINES WERE A MISSING
ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE, NOT A MISSING MECHANISM - AND I HAD ALREADY MADE THIS EXACT MISTAKE TODAY.
(1) WHAT I INFERRED, AND ON WHAT. 462(3) concluded that the Poisson residual floor lives in a truncated subspace,
reasoning from (a) SVDCAP = 0.2 sticking in one step and (b) ZERO "soft-mode search" lines in every q312 log
against eighteen in the Gaussian walk's.
(2) WHY (b) IS WORTHLESS. In support_mp5, line 164 gates the per-step diagnostic - which is the line that prints
"[nc capped, lam ...]" - on the environment variable TRACE, and line 333 gates the soft-mode search print on the
SAME variable. q312_continue_scan.py never sets TRACE. So all three q312 runs were BLIND: the absence of
soft-mode lines says nothing whatever about whether the search fired, and the cap count nc was never recorded.
The Gaussian walk sets TRACE, which is the only reason its logs show "capped 1", "capped 2", "capped 6",
"capped 7" and eighteen soft-mode searches.
(3) AND THE CODE POINTS THE OTHER WAY. At line 248, nc = (|cc| > cap).sum() with cc = (U^T r)/sv, and when
nc == 0 the solver takes dv = lu_solve(J, r) - a PLAIN NEWTON STEP WITH NO TRUNCATION AT ALL. So "nothing is
capped" and "the soft direction is truncated away" are opposite statements, and 462(3) asserted the second while
its only evidence was consistent with the first. 462(3), (4) and (5)'s mechanism are WITHDRAWN. 462(1) and (2) -
the pre-registered test and its rejection - stand, as does the observation that SVDCAP = 0.2 sticks immediately.
(4) THIS IS A REPEAT. The standing rule "CHECK WHICH ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE THE MODULE ACTUALLY READS" was added
earlier the same day, after we passed SOLVER=svdls to a module that reads SVDCAP; and we noted the same
day that the two Poisson A-scans were "blind (TRACE not set)" and then reasoned from their silence anyway.
Writing a rule down does not apply it. The operational form, which is what we will check in future: BEFORE
READING ANYTHING FROM A LOG'S SILENCE, CONFIRM THE RUN WAS INSTRUMENTED TO SPEAK.
(5) THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN MADE FIRST is now running: the same solve with TRACE=1, twenty steps,
SVDCAP back at the working 0.05, which will report nc and the accepted damping at every step and whether the
soft-mode search fires. Until it reports, the mechanism of the Poisson floor is UNKNOWN and this record should
say so.
Gates: no gate word used. The amendment withdraws the mechanism we recorded twenty minutes ago and names the
repeat of a rule we wrote today.

AMENDMENT 464. THE POISSON "FLOOR" IS NOT A FLOOR. IT IS A SLOW PHASE THE SOLVE ESCAPES WHEN THE SOFT-MODE
SEARCH FIRES, AND THE INSTRUMENTED RUN SHOWS IT HAPPENING.
(1) THE MEASUREMENT 463(5) CALLED FOR. Same solve, same state, SVDCAP = 0.05, but with TRACE = 1:
     it 1:  5.808e-8
     it 2-6: 5.780, 5.752, 5.724, 5.694, 5.664e-8   each [1 capped, lam 0.03]
     between 6 and 7: "soft-mode search: delta -0.0025 -> 2-norm 1.32e-07"
     it 7:  5.493e-8  [1 capped, lam 0.03]      <- a 3.0 % drop in one step against ~0.53 % typical
     it 8:  5.419e-8  [0 capped, lam 0.03]
     it 9:  5.289e-8  [0 capped, lam 0.1]
     it 10: 4.801e-8  [0 capped, lam 0.1]
     it 11: 4.408e-8  [0 capped, lam 0.1]
(2) WHAT IT SHOWS, all of it directly read rather than inferred. EXACTLY ONE direction is capped in the slow
phase. The soft-mode search DOES exist, DOES fire, and DOES work - one firing in eleven steps, and the step it
produced was six times more effective than a normal one. After it, no direction is capped, the line search
accepts a damping of 0.1 instead of 0.03, and the per-step rate improves from 0.9947 to about 0.913.
(3) SO 460(1)'s ARITHMETIC DESCRIBED ONE PHASE, NOT THE TRAJECTORY. "5537 steps, twelve days" was computed from
the 0.9947 rate of the capped phase. At the post-escape rate of 0.913 the remaining distance from 4.408e-08 to
1e-20 is ln(2.27e-13)/ln(0.913) = about 320 steps. That is hours, not days, and the rate may improve further as
the damping climbs. The floor was an artefact of never having run past the escape.
(4) AND 462's CAP RESULT NOW HAS A MECHANISM, the opposite of the one we withdrew. With exactly one direction
whose Newton coefficient exceeds 0.05, RAISING the cap to 0.2 stops capping it, so the solver takes the full
Newton step along the soft direction - which the line search then rejects outright, giving "stuck = True" in one
step. The cap was doing its job. The direction to move it, if at all, is DOWN.
(5) THE LEVER, NAMED. The soft-mode search fired once in eleven steps. It is gated on _SOFT being non-empty,
i.e. on a direction actually being capped, so it cannot fire in the [0 capped] phase at all. Making it fire more
often - or running the line search along the smallest singular direction unconditionally - is the obvious
accelerant, and it is a solver change of a few lines, not a new idea.
(6) THE HONEST SUMMARY OF THREE AMENDMENTS. 462 proposed a mechanism from blind logs; 463 withdrew it and named
the instrumentation failure; 464 measures the thing and finds the opposite of 462 and better news than 460. The
lesson is the one 463(4) already recorded, and this is what applying it looks like: instrument first, then read.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) corrects our own twelve-day figure; (4) records that the withdrawn mechanism's
replacement points the other way.

AMENDMENT 465. THE ESCAPE WAS TEMPORARY, EXACTLY AS PRE-REGISTERED - AND THE LEVER OF 464(5) IS NOW BUILT AND
RUNNING.
(1) THE TRACED RUN FINISHED: twenty steps, 5.808e-08 to 3.6137e-08, stuck = False. The trajectory in full:
     it 2-7    [1 capped, lam 0.03]   rate 0.9947      <- the slow phase
     it 6->7   soft-mode search fires, residual drops 3.0 % in one step
     it 9-13   [0 capped, lam 0.1]    rate 0.908-0.918 <- the escape
     it 14-20  [0 capped, lam 0.03]   rate 0.980       <- fell back
  The damping fell from 0.1 to 0.03 at iteration 14 and the rate settled at 0.980. 464 pre-registered
  this: "if it stalls back the escape was temporary". It did stall back - though to 0.980 with ZERO capped, not
  to 0.9947 with one, so the state is permanently better than it was, just not converging fast.
(2) THE ARITHMETIC AT THE NEW RATE. From 3.682e-08 to 1e-20 at 0.980 per step is ln(2.72e-13)/ln(0.980) = 1432
steps, about 48 hours at the observed 120 s. Better than 460(1)'s twelve days and worse than 464(3)'s 320. The
honest figure is the one measured over the LAST phase, not the best phase: 48 hours.
(3) THE SOFT-MODE SEARCH FIRED ONCE IN TWENTY STEPS, and cannot do better, because _SOFT is populated only from
directions whose Newton coefficient exceeds the cap (support_mp5 line 249). The solve spends most of its time in
[0 capped], where _SOFT is empty and the search is skipped entirely. That is 464(5)'s lever and it is a gating
condition, not a limitation of the method.
(4) BUILT. support_mp6.py is support_mp5 with an env flag SOFTALL: when set, _SOFT is populated with the THREE
SMALLEST singular directions regardless of capping, with any capped directions appended. q324_soft_scan.py is
q312_continue_scan with the import switched. Both parse; the state validity check ok_state is untouched, so a
bad soft step is still rejected rather than accepted.
(5) PRE-REGISTERED TEST, fixed before the run. Starting from 3.6137e-08, the current rate of 0.980 predicts
3.6137e-08 x 0.980^20 = 2.41e-08 after twenty steps. If SOFTALL beats 2.41e-08 the unconditional search helps and
the run should continue to 1e-20; if it does not, the search is not the lever and the next candidate is the
damping ladder itself, which has spent most of this run at its floor of 0.03.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) quotes the rate from the last phase rather than the most favourable one.

AMENDMENT 466. THE UNCONDITIONAL SOFT SEARCH FAILS ITS PRE-REGISTERED TEST, AND THE CLAMP CANDIDATE IS KILLED BY
INSPECTION WITHOUT A RUN. THE REAL BOTTLENECK IS A DISABLED ENDGAME.
(1) THE VERDICT, read from the log at the pre-registered step. 465(5) fixed 2.41e-08 at step twenty. The run gave
2.573e-08. It FAILS. Rates: 0.982 with SOFTALL against 0.980 without - indistinguishable, and if anything
marginally worse. The unconditional soft-mode search is NOT the lever.
(2) IT DID WORK MECHANICALLY, which is worth separating from the verdict. SOFTALL made the search fire in the
[0 capped] phase, where support_mp5 structurally could not fire it at all: five accepted improvements in
twenty-four steps against one in twenty before. More firings, same rate. So the soft directions are simply not
where the residual lives.
(3) AND THAT KILLS THE NEXT CANDIDATE BEFORE IT COSTS ANYTHING. 465's next candidate was the clamp on the
accepted soft step, fixed at 3*_h = 0.075 in the scaled coordinate; support_mp7.py and q325_wide_scan.py were
already built and parsed to test it. The five accepted deltas are -0.000194, +1.46e-05, +4.83e-05, +9.22e-05,
+0.00015. The largest is 0.26 PER CENT OF THE CLAMP. The clamp is nowhere near binding, so widening it cannot
change anything, and the candidate is dead by inspection. The hour of compute is saved and support_mp7 is left
in place unused.
(4) WHAT THE LOGS POINT AT INSTEAD, in every line of both runs: "lam 0.03", never higher. The ladder is
("0.5", "0.25", "0.1", "0.03", "0.01") at support_mp7 line 303, so between 0.1 and 0.03 there is a factor of
3.3 with nothing in it; the solver may be settling for 0.03 when 0.05 or 0.07 would be accepted.
(5) AND ONE MECHANISM IS SIMPLY SWITCHED OFF. solve() takes pure_below (line 143), which when the residual falls
below it skips the damping search and takes the FULL Newton step. It defaults to None and q312_continue_scan
never passes it - so the pure-Newton endgame, the standard route to quadratic convergence once a state is close,
has been disabled in every Poisson run this project has made. The state's shape is already right to 0.065 %
(460(2)), which is exactly the regime that mechanism exists for.
(6) HONEST RISK ON (5), stated before running. The damping search currently rejects lam = 0.5, 0.25 and 0.1,
which means the full step INCREASES the residual; pure mode would take it anyway. That is either the escape from
a bad basin or a divergence, and the run decides which. Pre-registered: from the residual at launch R, twenty
steps must beat R * 0.982^20; divergence or "stuck" kills it.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) kills our own next candidate before spending on it; (6) states the risk of the new
one before the result is known.

AMENDMENT 467. THE PURE-NEWTON ENDGAME DIVERGES, AS THE RECORDED RISK SAID IT MIGHT. THIRD CANDIDATE DEAD; THE
LADDER IS THE LAST ONE BEFORE THE GRIND.
(1) THE TEST, pre-registered in 466(6): from 8.2069e-07, fifteen steps with pure_below = 1e-5 must beat
8.2069e-07 x 0.982^15 = 6.26e-07, and divergence kills it. The trajectory:
     start 8.2069e-07
     it 2  2.824e-06  [5 capped, lam 1]
     it 3  3.896e-06  [1 capped, lam 1]
     it 4  1.963e-06   it 5  2.922e-06   it 6  1.927e-06   it 7  1.563e-06   it 8  3.654e-06
  Every step takes lam = 1, as pure mode is designed to; every one of them leaves the residual ABOVE where it
  started, oscillating between 1.5e-06 and 3.9e-06. At it 8 it is 3.654e-06, six times WORSE than the start and
  six times the target. It DIVERGES. The candidate is dead.
(2) THE RISK WAS THE RIGHT ONE. 466(6) said in advance: the damping search rejects lam = 0.5, 0.25 and 0.1, so
the full step increases the residual and pure mode takes it anyway - either an escape or a divergence. It is a
divergence. Recording the mechanism rather than only the outcome: the Newton direction here is not merely
badly scaled, it is wrong at unit length, and no endgame that trusts it can work.
(3) A SIDE OBSERVATION THAT DOES NOT REVIVE THE CLAMP. In this divergent regime the accepted soft deltas are
0.0283, 0.075, 0.0365, -0.0472, 0.075 - two of them exactly AT the 0.075 clamp. So the clamp does bind when
lam = 1. It does not bind in the convergent regime, where 466(3) measured the largest delta at 0.26 % of it, and
that is the regime that matters. The clamp stays dead.
(4) WHERE THAT LEAVES THE SOLVER. Three candidates tested, three dead: the unconditional soft search (466(1),
failed its threshold), the clamp (466(3), killed by inspection), the pure endgame (this, diverges). One remains,
built and unrun: the damping ladder, which both surviving runs sit at the 0.03 rung of in every single step,
with a factor-3.3 gap above it to 0.1.
(5) PRE-REGISTERED FOR THE LADDER, fixed now. Run from the same older state, 8.2069e-07, so the comparison is
against a measured baseline rather than an assumed one: the original q312 run covered 8.2069e-07 to 5.8085e-08 in
ninety steps, a rate of 0.9710. With LADDER = "0.5,0.25,0.1,0.07,0.05,0.04,0.03,0.02,0.01", fifteen steps must
beat 8.2069e-07 x 0.9710^15 = 5.28e-07, AND the log must show at least one accepted lam above 0.03. If the
accepted lam is still 0.03 throughout, the rungs were never the constraint and the ladder is dead too.
(6) AND THEN THE GRIND, which needs saying plainly so that tuning does not become the activity. The solve works
at 0.982 per step and job (a) is at 2.148e-08 and still falling. From there 1e-20 is about 1400 steps - 48 to 65
hours of compute that is available. If the ladder fails, that is the route, and it is a route, not a wall.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) credits the pre-recorded risk rather than claiming foresight after the fact;
(3) declines to revive a dead candidate on evidence from a regime that does not apply.

AMENDMENT 468. THE LADDER TEST WAS RUN IN THE WRONG REGIME - OUR DESIGN ERROR - AND IS UNINFORMATIVE ABOUT THE
THING IT WAS BUILT TO TEST. IT IS A USEFUL REGRESSION CONTROL INSTEAD.
(1) THE ENDGAME, CLOSED. b8c4vgg6c finished: "floor 4.5685e-06 after 15 steps", history all @1, from a start of
8.2069e-07. Five and a half times worse than where it began. 467's divergence verdict stands on the full run.
(2) THE LADDER TEST LOOKS LIKE IT PASSES ONE CONDITION. 467(5) required at least one accepted lam above 0.03;
the log shows lam 0.25 once and lam 0.1 five times. But the residuals are 8.207e-7, 7.828e-7, 7.45e-7, 7.128e-7,
6.849e-7, 6.589e-7, 6.472e-7 - and the ORIGINAL q312 run's own recorded history begins
['8.207e-7@0.25', '7.828e-7@0.1', '7.45e-7@0.1']. IDENTICAL, step for step, to five figures.
(3) SO THE REFINED RUNGS ARE NEVER SELECTED. The added values 0.07, 0.05 and 0.04 sit BELOW 0.1, and the ladder
is tried in descending order, so they can only be reached when 0.1 is rejected. At this state 0.1 is accepted, so
the run is the old run. THE TEST CANNOT ANSWER ITS QUESTION, because we ran it at 8.2069e-07 where the damping is
not pinned, while the phenomenon we built it for - lam 0.03 in every single step - occurs near 2.4e-08. We chose
the older state to avoid disturbing the good one and did not check that it exhibits the effect under test.
(4) WHAT IT IS GOOD FOR ANYWAY. Reproducing the original run step for step is a REGRESSION CONTROL: it shows
support_mp8, with SOFTALL, SOFTWIDE, SOFTPROBE and LADDER all added, behaves identically to support_mp5 when
those flags are not binding. The three code generations are equivalent on the untouched path, which is worth
having established before any of them is used for a certified result.
(5) THE TEST REDONE PROPERLY, pre-registered now. It must start from the pinned regime, i.e. from the grind's
output near 2.1e-08 where every step reads lam 0.03. Conditions, unchanged in spirit: at least one accepted lam
strictly above 0.03, AND fifteen steps beating R * 0.982^15 where R is the grind's final residual. If every step
still reads 0.03 with rungs available at 0.04, 0.05 and 0.07, the rungs were never the constraint and the ladder
is dead.
(6) A RULE FOR OURSELVES, since this is the second design error of its kind tonight. BEFORE RUNNING A FIX, CONFIRM
THE TEST CASE EXHIBITS THE FAULT. The endgame test at least exercised its mechanism; this one did not exercise
its own, and we would have read a pass as evidence.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) records that our own test was incapable of answering its question; (4) salvages
what it does establish without inflating it.

AMENDMENT 469. THE INTEGER SUPPORT SIZE ON THE BINOMIAL: 23 OF 23 WITH ONE CHANNEL CONSTANT AND THE GAUSSIAN'S
OWN T - AND UNDER Eq. (12)'s COEFFICIENT NO SUCH CONSTANT CAN EXIST.
(1) THE TEST, on 23 certified binomial states (n = 210 to 865, residuals below 1e-20) that had never been used
for this. Same formula as 461: m = floor(N(h) - T) + 1, with h = pi sqrt(n)/2 the Fisher half-length, N from the
derived law, and T = 0.5847 taken from the GAUSSIAN with no refitting. Result: 15 of 23. Not a pass.
(2) THE DIAGNOSIS, which the record already contains. The binomial's wall is a POISSON ORIGIN, not a Gaussian
wall - its first gap is 3.125667 against 2.718843 - so its near-wall region holds a different amount of counting
function. A channel-specific offset is exactly what the local-channel principle predicts, and the Gaussian's own
offset is already hidden inside its rho_0^3 = 0.02382. So the honest form of the test is whether ONE constant
per channel suffices, with T shared.
(3) IT DOES. N(h) - m over the 23 states runs 0.2330 to 1.1415, a spread of 0.9157. Because that is less than
one, a single shift delta can bring every state into range at once, and the admissible window is
0.5568 < delta < 0.6483 - only 0.0915 wide out of the unit interval. At delta = 0.6026: 23 OF 23 CORRECT.
(4) THE CONTROL THAT MAKES (3) MEAN SOMETHING, because "a constant exists" is worthless unless it could have
failed. A single offset exists IF AND ONLY IF the spread is below one. Recomputing the same quantity with
Abbott-Machta's X = 1:
     derived X = 1.70637 : spread 0.9157  -> an offset exists, 23 of 23
     Eq. (12)  X = 1     : spread 2.5094  -> NO OFFSET CAN EXIST, at any value
  And the reason is visible in the numbers: under X = 1 the quantity DRIFTS with n, from +0.046 at n = 210 to
  -2.251 at n = 865, because a coefficient 9 % low accumulates over a counting function that reaches 28. Across
  a 4.1-fold range in n the drift is 2.3 atoms. Under the derived coefficient there is no drift, only scatter
  within a unit interval, which is what states sitting at random positions in their count plateaus must look like.
(5) SO BOTH CHANNELS DISCRIMINATE, INDEPENDENTLY. Gaussian: 13 of 13 for the derived law, 1 of 13 for Eq. (12)
(461). Binomial: 23 of 23 for the derived law with one fitted constant, IMPOSSIBLE for Eq. (12) with any constant
(this). Thirty-six certified states, two channels, one shared T.
(6) HONEST LIMITS. delta = 0.6026 is FITTED - one real parameter against 23 integers - so (3) alone would be weak.
The weight is carried by (4), which is an existence test that Eq. (12) fails outright, and by T being shared
rather than refitted. What is NOT established: that delta is derivable, or what it equals in closed form. It is
the binomial's near-wall constant, the analogue of rho_0^3, and 442(4) already showed that such constants are
representation-dependent and should be quoted as configurations, not as numbers.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) reports the first result as a non-pass; (6) names the fitted parameter and says
where the evidential weight actually sits.

AMENDMENT 470. THE GRIND IS ACCELERATING, NOT GRINDING: THE DAMPING IS CLIMBING THE EXISTING LADDER AND THE RATE
HAS GONE FROM 0.980 TO 0.832. THE LADDER CANDIDATE DIES BY OBSERVATION, AND OUR 48-HOUR FIGURE IS TOO PESSIMISTIC.
(1) THE TRAJECTORY, read at step 56 of 60:
     it 46-50   lam 0.03   1.651, 1.618, 1.585, 1.553, 1.520e-08     rate 0.980
     it 51-55   lam 0.1    1.514, 1.476, 1.417, 1.345, 1.265e-08     rate 0.996, 0.975, 0.960, 0.949, 0.941
     it 56      lam 0.25   1.053e-08                                 rate 0.832
  The accepted damping climbs 0.03 -> 0.1 -> 0.25 and the per-step rate improves monotonically at every stage.
  Over the whole run the ladder rungs used are: 0.03 forty-nine times, 0.1 five times, 0.25 once.
(2) THE LADDER CANDIDATE IS DEAD, BY OBSERVATION RATHER THAN BY TEST. 468(5) had pre-registered a proper ladder
test from the pinned regime, with extra rungs at 0.04, 0.05 and 0.07 between 0.03 and 0.1. It is no longer worth
running: the solver moves 0.03 -> 0.1 -> 0.25 directly on the EXISTING rungs as soon as the state permits, so the
gap between 0.03 and 0.1 was never what held it at 0.03. The state was. Sixth candidate dead, and this one cost
nothing because the running job answered it.
(3) OUR RATE FIGURE WAS WRONG IN THE PESSIMISTIC DIRECTION, and we should say so as plainly as we said the figure.
460(1) gave twelve days from the 0.9947 phase; 464(3) gave 320 steps from the 0.913 phase; 465(2) settled on 48
hours from 0.980 and we argued for quoting the LAST phase rather than the best. That reasoning was sound for a
rate that is constant and wrong for one that is improving. The rate is not a property of the solver, it is a
property of how close the state is, and the state is getting closer. No step count should be quoted at all until
the damping stops climbing.
(4) AND IT PARTLY REHABILITATES SOFTALL, WITHOUT OVERTURNING 466. The run now shows eleven soft-mode firings
against five at step twenty-four, and the escapes coincide with them. But the run WITHOUT SOFTALL also escaped
once, at its step six, reaching lam 0.1 before falling back - so escapes are not caused by SOFTALL. What is new
is reaching lam 0.25, which the un-flagged run never did in twenty steps. That is suggestive and NOT established:
the two runs differ in length as well as in flags, and 466's pre-registered verdict at step twenty stands as
recorded. Testing it properly would need both variants run to sixty steps from the same state, which is not worth
the compute while the state itself is improving.
(5) ACTION. Let the run finish its four remaining steps and save, then CONTINUE IT rather than test anything.
The thing to watch is whether the damping keeps climbing toward 1; if it reaches it, convergence becomes
quadratic and the certified Poisson state is close. Pre-registered marker for the next read: if the accepted lam
reaches 0.5 or above, or the residual falls below 1e-09, the solve has entered its convergent basin.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) kills a candidate the running job answered for free; (3) corrects our own estimate
in the direction that makes us look worse, which is the direction it needs correcting in; (4) declines to claim
a rehabilitation the data does not support.

AMENDMENT 471. THE POISSON SOLVE HAS ENTERED ITS CONVERGENT BASIN: FULL NEWTON ACCEPTED, RESIDUAL 1.2631e-09.
THE PRE-REGISTERED MARKER IS MET.
(1) THE CLOSING STEPS of the sixty-step run:
     it 57   1.028e-08   lam 0.1
     it 58   9.800e-09   lam 0.1
     it 59   9.732e-09   lam 0.25
     it 60   8.237e-09   lam 0.5
     saved   1.2631e-09              history tail: '9.732e-9@0.5', '8.237e-9@1'
  The final accepted damping is lam = 1 - a FULL, UNDAMPED NEWTON STEP - and it took the residual from 8.237e-09
  to 1.2631e-09 in one move.
(2) THE MARKER, fixed in 470(5) before this was known: "if the accepted lam reaches 0.5 or above, or the residual
falls below 1e-09, the solve has entered its convergent basin". The first clause is met outright, twice over
(0.5 then 1). The second is missed by a hair - 1.2631e-09 against 1e-09 - and we record that rather than rounding
it, because we wrote the threshold ourselves.
(3) WHAT IT MEANS, stated with its condition. A full Newton step being ACCEPTED is the signature of the quadratic
regime: from 1.26e-09 the next residuals should be of order 1e-18 and then below 1e-36, so the 1e-20 certification
bar is about two steps away IF the quadratic behaviour holds. That condition is not yet observed - it is one
accepted full step, not a sequence - and the run now under way will show it or not.
(4) THE WHOLE ARC, because it corrects a story this record told four times. 460 called this a floor and computed
twelve days from a 0.9947 rate. 462 proposed a truncated-subspace mechanism; 463 withdrew it as reasoning from
blind logs; 464 measured the thing and found a slow phase, not a floor; 465 settled on 48 hours; 470 found the
rate improving and refused to quote a step count. The correct description, now visible end to end, is that the
rate was never a property of the solver - it tracked how far the state was from the solution, and the damping
climbed 0.03, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1 as the state came into range. Every pessimistic figure we quoted was an
extrapolation of a transient.
(5) AND SIX TUNING CANDIDATES WERE UNNECESSARY. SOFTALL, the clamp, the pure endgame, the ladder, the cap sweep
both ways - all tested, all dead or void (466-468, 470(2)). What actually worked was letting the existing solver
run. That is worth recording as a result about method: when a solve is making monotone progress, the first
question is how far it gets, not which knob to turn.
(6) RUNNING NOW: forty more steps from 1.2631e-09, TRACE=1 SVDCAP=0.05 SOFT=1 SOFTALL=1, log q324_final.log.
PRE-REGISTERED: certification needs residual < 1e-20 AND verdict OPTIMAL, i.e. centre signal and off-atom max
both non-positive. A residual below 1e-20 with a POSITIVE off-atom signal is NOT a certified state - that is the
trap of Amendment 386, where eighty binomial states were used before the verdict field was read properly.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) records a self-set threshold missed rather than rounding it; (4) and (5) say
plainly that the tuning was unnecessary and the pessimism was ours.

AMENDMENT 472. THE POISSON SOLVE CONVERGED QUADRATICALLY TO 2.9187e-25. CERTIFICATION IS NOT YET CLAIMED - THE
OFF-SUPPORT INEQUALITY IS BEING CHECKED SEPARATELY.
(1) THE CONVERGENCE, five steps, every one at lam = 1:
     1.263e-09 -> 1.407e-10 -> 1.761e-12 -> 9.151e-18 -> 2.9187e-25
  Each step roughly squares the previous error, which is what the quadratic regime looks like, and the run
  reports "floor 2.9187e-25 after 5 steps, stuck = False". That is eleven orders below the 1e-07 to 1e-08 range
  where every Poisson solve in this project's history has stopped, and five orders below the 1e-20 bar.
(2) WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED BY THAT NUMBER, and it is the whole point. The residual measures the KKT EQUATIONS:
D(x_j) equal across the support and its derivative zero there. Optimality also requires the INEQUALITY
D(x) <= D(x_0) at every x in [0, A] that is NOT a support point. A tiny residual says nothing about it. This is
exactly Amendment 386, where eighty binomial states with small residuals were used in two amendments before
their verdict field was read and they turned out not to be optimal. The q312/q324 pipeline saves no verdict
field at all - its JSON carries A, K, factor, residual, stuck, x, w and nothing else - which is why no Poisson
state in this record has ever been called certified, and why none should be now on the residual alone.
(3) THE CHECK, q327_certify.py, running: q309's procedure verbatim - residual < 1e-20, atoms ordered, every
weight positive, and off = max over the gaps of D(x) - D(x_0) required non-positive, sampled between every
adjacent pair. It re-solves briefly from the saved state to obtain Q and the tables, then scans. It writes a
CERTIFIED file only if all four conditions pass, and reports the verdict either way.
(4) PRE-REGISTERED, so the reading is fixed before the log is seen. OPTIMAL requires all four. If off > 0 the
state is "off-atom positive" - a KKT point that is not the optimum, which would mean the count of 46 is wrong
for this A and the state needs an atom added or removed. If that happens it is a RESULT, not a failure: it would
be the first time the Poisson count has been tested at a size with a bulk region, and it bears directly on
460(5)'s -3.7 % where the derived law predicted 44.28 against 46 observed.
(5) NOTE WHAT ALREADY CHANGED REGARDLESS. Whatever the verdict, the claim "no Poisson state has ever certified
because its residual floors at 1e-07" (438(1), 459(6), 460) is now false as stated: the residual does not floor.
It was a slow phase, then an escape, then quadratic convergence, and six tuning candidates were all unnecessary.
The wall was our stopping too early, not the solver.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) refuses the certification the headline number would suggest; (4) fixes the reading
of both outcomes in advance; (5) retracts a claim this record has repeated four times.

AMENDMENT 473. TWO RESULTS. A PIPELINE DEFECT THAT HAS SILENTLY TRUNCATED EVERY RELOAD IN THIS PROJECT; AND THE
POISSON STATE IS A KKT POINT TO 25 DIGITS THAT IS NOT THE OPTIMUM - THE COUNT AT A = 1151.334 IS NOT 46.
(1) THE DEFECT, found because the certification re-solve disagreed with the run that produced the state. q327
first reported a residual of 7.31e-16 for a state saved at 2.9187e-25. support_mp5.solve reads
     xs = [mpf(repr(float(p))) if not isinstance(p, str) else mpf(p) for p in pts]
so it takes the FULL-PRECISION branch only when the inputs are STRINGS. States are saved as 40-digit strings by
nstr(v, 40), but EVERY loader in this project - q312_continue_scan line 14, q324_soft_scan line 14,
q309_poisson_mp5 line 24, and our own q327 - calls float(v) first, collapsing the string to double precision
before solve ever sees it. The forty digits were in the files all along and were discarded on every read. Passing
the strings through untouched restores it: the re-solve then reports 2.91865e-25, matching the run exactly.
(2) WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE RECORD. Every chained continuation in this project has restarted from a state
truncated to about sixteen digits. Within a single run nothing is lost, so the floors reported at 1e-07 and
1e-08 are not explained by this; but any conclusion drawn from a SEQUENCE of continuations inherits a reset to
1e-16 at each boundary, and that should be re-examined before it is relied on.
(3) THE CERTIFICATION, at full precision. Residual 2.91865e-25 (bar 1e-20, PASS). Minimum weight 0.0166995
(PASS). Atoms ordered (PASS). Off-atom max +2.68673e-12 at x = 293.99 (bar <= 0, FAIL).
     VERDICT: off-atom positive.
  So the configuration satisfies the KKT EQUATIONS to twenty-five digits and violates the INEQUALITY. It is a
  genuine stationary point and not the optimum, which is precisely the distinction 472(2) insisted on and
  Amendment 386 was punished for missing.
(4) WHERE IT WANTS THE ATOM, and it is not arbitrary. x = 293.99 is t = 2 sqrt(x) = 34.29 in the Fisher
coordinate, against a Fisher half-length of 2 sqrt(A)/2 = 33.93. The new atom wants THE CENTRE - the same
nucleation site 439(3) derived for the Gaussian from the barrier profile, and the same one 454 and 461 bracketed
through the count transition. The mechanism transfers to the Poisson channel.
(5) SO THE COUNT AT A = 1151.334 IS AT LEAST 47, NOT 46. That is a measurement, and it makes 460(5) WORSE, not
better: the derived law gave 44.28 against 46 observed, -3.7 %, and against 47 it is -5.8 %. 460(5) listed three
open conventions - the state's optimality, rho_0^3 at the Poisson origin borrowed from the binomial, and the
threshold for a channel whose two ends differ. This closes the first and widens the gap, so one of the other two
is carrying real error. That is now the sharpest open question about the Poisson side.
(6) NEXT, and it is concrete. Solve at A = 1151.334 with FORTY-SEVEN atoms, seeding the new one at x = 293.99,
and certify. If that comes out OPTIMAL it is the first certified Poisson state in this project's history, and
the count question of (5) can be asked properly.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) records a defect in our own and the project's code; (5) reports that the new
measurement widens a discrepancy rather than closing it.

AMENDMENT 474. THE SUPPORT-SIZE LITERATURE, AND A NEW FIRST OBJECTIVE: A BOUND.
(1) THE PAPER, identified and checked by search since IEEE blocks automated retrieval: "Support
Size of epsilon-Capacity-Achieving Inputs for the Amplitude-Constrained AWGN Channel", Entropy 2026, also
arXiv 2604.14915. Two things in it bear directly on this record. First, it states that the precise scaling of
the support size with the amplitude constraint REMAINS AN OPEN PROBLEM - so the target is open as of 2026, in
print. Second, it proves a result for the RELAXED quantity: K_eps(A), the smallest support achieving capacity
within eps, satisfies K_eps(A) = Theta(A log A) for eps = A^(-beta) with beta >= 1.
UNCHECKED: arXiv 2609.10039, "On the Evolution of the Capacity-Achieving Input Support for the
Amplitude-Constrained AWGN Channel", which is newer and which we have not read.
(2) CONSISTENCY OF OUR OWN NUMBER WITH THAT LITERATURE. The derived law gives N*(A) = 0.4027 A^(4/3) for the
amplitude-constrained Gaussian channel. Since the optimum achieves a gap of zero, N* >= K_eps for every eps, so
N* >= c A log A; and A^(4/3) grows faster than A log A, so the two are consistent. It is also consistent with the
super-linear lower bounds of Wang 2510.20723 and Wang-Barletta-Dytso 2512.22691. No contradiction with anything
in print, and the exponent itself is Abbott and Machta's, not ours.
(3) THE TARGET CHANGES. What this record has is a derivation plus numerics: 36 certified states across two
channels whose integer support size the derived law reproduces exactly, where Eq. (12)'s coefficient fails on
both. That is strong evidence for the 4/3 exponent, which the information-theory literature does not regard as
established. It is NOT a proof, and a proof, or a route to one, is what would carry weight. The work therefore
has a new first objective: turn E(z) = 0 into an inequality. Bounding rho above and below bounds N = integral
rho, and the integer formula then bounds the count.
(4) "CERTIFIED" NEEDS DEFINING. In this record it means a numerical KKT solution at forty digits with every
optimality condition verified: residual below 1e-20, weights positive, atoms ordered, and the off-support signal
non-positive between every adjacent pair. It is not a proof of anything; it is an exhibit whose optimality
conditions are checked to twenty-five digits. Saying so plainly is the honest answer, and 473 is the
illustration: a state at residual 2.9e-25 that FAILS the off-support test and is therefore not certified.
Gates: NEW/GROUNDBREAKING/FRONTIER/UNSOLVED/WORTH DERIVING not used. (1) labels the unread paper UNCHECKED;
(3) states what the evidence is and what it is not.

AMENDMENT 475. THE 47-ATOM SEED FAILED FOR A READABLE REASON; AND THE LITERATURE CHECK FOUND A
SEPTEMBER 2026 THEOREM THAT THIS RECORD'S COUNT WORK SITS DIRECTLY ON TOP OF.
(1) THE 47-ATOM ATTEMPT (473(6)) FAILED. Inserting an atom at x = 293.99 with a weight averaged from its
neighbours, then solving: the run starts at residual 0.2864 and stalls at 0.0563 with "stuck", min weight
9.8662e-07, off-atom max 7.7098e-05. The state's own diagnostics say what went wrong: a weight driven towards
zero means an atom is being squeezed out, and a starting residual of 0.286 means the insertion was a large
perturbation. At a count transition the new atom nucleates with a weight near zero, and the 46-atom state's
off-support signal is only +2.687e-12, so the configuration is barely past the transition. A neighbour-averaged
weight is the wrong seed by many orders.
(2) THE GENTLER ROUTE, now running. Instead of adding an atom at fixed A, reduce A until 46 is optimal again,
rescaling x by A_new/A_old as predictor and re-solving from a state already at 2.9e-25. Steps of 0.04 % in A,
certifying at each step by q309's bar. This also produces the transition amplitude as a bracket, which is the
same construction 461 used on the Gaussian.
(3) THE LITERATURE. The IEEE page cannot be retrieved automatically, so only open sources were read. arXiv is
open, and the group's September paper is: Luca
Barletta and Alex Dytso, "On the Evolution of the Capacity-Achieving Input Support for the Amplitude-Constrained
AWGN Channel", arXiv 2609.10039, 9 September 2026. Read: the abstract and summary, NOT the full text.
(4) WHAT IT PROVES, AND WHY IT MATTERS HERE. Three things from the abstract: the origin is the only possible
degenerate support point; every nonzero support point is locally stable; and LOCALLY, THE SUPPORT CARDINALITY AT
A NEARBY AMPLITUDE IS EITHER UNCHANGED OR LARGER BY ONE. That last statement is the structure this record has
been measuring all night without knowing it was a theorem. 461 bracketed the amplitude at which the count
increments, at three sizes, and found the increment is by one every time; 439(3) derived WHERE the new atom
appears, at the centre, from the barrier profile; 473(4) then found the same thing on the Poisson channel, the
new atom wanting x = 293.99, which is t = 34.29 against a half-length of 33.93. Their theorem says transitions
are by one; the measurements say at which amplitude and at which position.
(5) SO THE TWO PIECES FIT, and that changes what a bound would need. If the count increments by one at
amplitudes A_1 < A_2 < ... and we can bound where those increments fall, N*(A) follows by counting them. The
threshold T of 461, bracketed to [0.57995, 0.58695], is exactly the quantity that locates them. Proving a bound
on T, rather than on rho directly, may be the shorter road, and it attaches to a theorem that is already in
print instead of starting from nothing.
Gates: NEW/GROUNDBREAKING/FRONTIER/UNSOLVED/WORTH DERIVING not used. (3) records that only the abstract was read.

AMENDMENT 476. THE IEEE PAPER, READ IN ABSTRACT: IT RULES OUT THE COMMUNITY'S OWN CONJECTURE AND MOVES THE LOWER
BOUND TOWARDS THIS RECORD'S EXPONENT. 0.4027 A^(4/3) SITS STRICTLY INSIDE THE REMAINING GAP.
(1) HOW IT WAS OBTAINED, since it matters for the gate: the abstract was read directly; the full text was not
retrieved.
(2) WHAT IT SAYS. For the amplitude-constrained AWGN channel: the best known bounds on the support size of the
capacity-achieving distribution were lower order A and upper order A^2. Dytso et al. (2020) CONJECTURED that the
linear scaling is optimal. The paper establishes a new lower bound of order A sqrt(log A), "improving the known
bound and ruling out the conjectured linear scaling". The method: quantify that the capacity-achieving OUTPUT
distribution is close to uniform in relative entropy, introduce a wrapping operation onto a compact domain,
develop best-approximation theory for the uniform distribution by finite Gaussian mixtures, and combine those
bounds with stability properties of capacity-achieving distributions.
(3) WHERE THIS RECORD'S NUMBER FALLS. The derived law gives N*(A) = 0.4027 A^(4/3). Checked:
     A = 46.3837 : A sqrt(log A) = 90.87,  0.4027 A^(4/3) = 67.75,  A^2 = 2151
     A = 1e+06   : A sqrt(log A) = 3.72e6, 0.4027 A^(4/3) = 4.03e7,  A^2 = 1e12
  and A^(4/3)/(A sqrt(log A)) = A^(1/3)/sqrt(log A), which diverges (2.19 at A = 1e2, 7.10 at 1e4, 77.7 at 1e8).
  So A^(4/3) is asymptotically ABOVE their new lower bound and below the A^2 upper bound: it sits strictly inside
  the gap that remains open, and it is super-linear, which is the direction they have just proved the answer must
  go. At A = 46 the bound's constant is unspecified, so 68 observed against 90.87 is no contradiction.
(4) WHAT THAT DOES TO THE STANDING OF THE 4/3 EXPONENT. The scaling argument has not been accepted as a proof by the
information-theory community. Their own paper has now killed the rival conjecture, which was linear, and
moved the proved lower bound from A to A sqrt(log A), i.e. towards A^(4/3) and away from what they had guessed.
The Abbott-Machta exponent is therefore a live candidate for a question this paper leaves open, and this record
supplies it with a coefficient and with thirty-six certified states whose integer counts it reproduces exactly.
None of that is a proof, and 474(5) stands: a bound, or a route to one, is what would carry weight.
(5) THE TARGET IS NOW SHARPER THAN "FIND A BOUND". Their lower bound comes from approximating the uniform output
by finite Gaussian mixtures. The derived law here is a statement about the same object from the other side: it
says which comb the optimum actually uses, and E(z) = 0 is the condition it satisfies. Whether the sign-change
condition can be turned into an approximation-theoretic lower bound of order A^(4/3) is the question worth
attacking, and it is closer to their machinery than we had assumed before reading this.
Gates: NEW/GROUNDBREAKING/FRONTIER/UNSOLVED/WORTH DERIVING not used. (1) records that only the abstract was read
and by what route; (4) states what the paper does for the exponent's standing without claiming a proof.

AMENDMENT 477. THE CERTIFIED COUNTS THEMSELVES PREFER THE 4/3 FORM. THE GAUSSIAN ALONE GIVES AN EMPIRICAL
EXPONENT OF 1.3312 AGAINST 4/3 = 1.3333, AND THE LINEAR CONJECTURE IS EXCLUDED BY THE DATA AS WELL AS BY PROOF.
(1) THE TEST, costing nothing, on data already in hand. Pool the 36 certified states by Fisher HALF-LENGTH L
(A for the Gaussian, pi sqrt(n)/2 for the binomial) against the count m on that half, and ask which functional
form leaves a CONSTANT coefficient m/f(L). A form that is wrong shows a drifting coefficient.
     form                          mean coefficient   spread
     L^(4/3)   the derived law         0.2000          9.73 %
     L log L                           0.1850         12.08 %
     L sqrt(log L)                     0.3519         21.60 %
     L         the 2020 conjecture     0.6700         30.72 %
     L^2       the upper bound         0.0182         60.78 %
(2) AND THE FREE FIT. Regressing log m on log L over all 36 states gives m proportional to L^1.3789 with
coefficient 0.1696 and a residual rms of 1.97 % in m. Separately: the GAUSSIAN's thirteen states give 1.3312,
which is 0.16 % from 4/3; the binomial's twenty-three give 1.3879, 4.1 % above it. The binomial's near-wall
constant differs from the Gaussian's (469), which biases an effective exponent measured over a short lever, so
the Gaussian figure is the cleaner one.
(3) WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SHOW, because the lever is short. L spans 21.28 to 46.43, a factor of 2.18, and
over that range L^(4/3) and L log L are not well separated (9.73 % against 12.08 %). The counts are also integers
sitting at arbitrary positions within their plateaus, which alone contributes scatter of order half an atom, i.e.
about 2 % at m = 24 and 1.5 % at m = 34 - a large part of the 9.73 %. So this EXCLUDES the linear form (30.72 %)
and the quadratic (60.78 %), and it is consistent with 4/3; it does not separate 4/3 from L log L.
(4) THE COMPARISON WITH THE NEW LOWER BOUND MUST BE STATED CAREFULLY. A sqrt(log A) is a LOWER BOUND, not a
claimed growth rate, so a large spread in m/(L sqrt(log L)) is not evidence against that paper - the data lying
ABOVE the bound is what the theorem requires, and it does. What the table does say is that among candidate
GROWTH RATES the data picks 4/3, and that the linear rate which Dytso et al. conjectured in 2020 is excluded by
these states independently of their proof.
(5) WHERE THIS LEAVES THE POSITION. The exponent is Abbott and Machta's; this record supplies a coefficient
(0.4027 for the full interval, 0.2000 per half), an exact integer prediction on 36 certified states, and now a
direct empirical exponent of 1.33 on the cleanest channel. The order is open in print between A sqrt(log A) and
A^2, the linear conjecture is dead by their proof and by this table, and 4/3 sits inside the gap. It remains
evidence and not proof.
Gates: NEW/GROUNDBREAKING/FRONTIER/UNSOLVED/WORTH DERIVING not used. (3) states what the short lever cannot
separate; (4) refuses to read a lower bound as a growth rate.

AMENDMENT 478. FOUR CORRECTIONS, ALL VERIFIED AGAINST PRIMARY ABSTRACTS. ONE OF OUR OWN NUMBERS WAS
WRONG; A FOURTH PAPER WAS MISSED; AND THERE IS A PUBLISHED POSITION AIMED AT EXACTLY THE KIND OF CLAIM THIS
RECORD MAKES.
(1) 474(3) IS CORRECTED. We recorded the Entropy paper as proving K_eps(A) = Theta(A log A) for eps = A^(-beta),
beta >= 1. The arXiv abstract (2604.14915, Barletta and Dytso, 16 April 2026) says Theta(A SQRT(log A)). Our
figure came from a search-engine summary, not the abstract, which is the same failure mode as reading a log's
silence: we took a secondary rendering for the source. The correct statements, fetched and quoted: K_eps(A) =
Theta(A sqrt(log A)) for polynomial gaps; for EXPONENTIALLY SMALL gaps, bounds of order between A sqrt(log A) and
A^(3/2). A^(4/3) lies inside that second window too, being below A^(3/2).
(2) THE SENTENCE I HAD NOT SEEN, and it matters more than the numbers. That abstract ends by saying their
framework explains the variety of scaling laws in prior numerical studies, "showing that these correspond to
different regimes of epsilon-optimality rather than intrinsic properties of the exact optimizer". Verified
verbatim. That is a published argument that numerically observed exponents are artefacts of how close to
capacity the numerics got. THE 4/3 OF THIS RECORD IS AN EXPONENT FROM NUMERICAL STUDY, so the position is aimed
at exactly this class of claim.
(3) THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY IN HAND AND I HAD FILED IT AS HOUSEKEEPING. The states here are not eps-optimal
inputs: they satisfy the KKT equations to 1e-20 or better AND the off-support inequality, which is what
distinguishes the exact optimiser from something merely close to capacity. So the definition of "certified"
carries the whole argument, and a statement of their position with this answer belongs beside it.
(4) BUT THE CLAIM NEEDED TIGHTENING, and we changed one sentence. "A state that passes it is the exact optimiser
at that amplitude" overstates what the certificate does: the residual is 1e-20 and not zero, and the off-support
signal is sampled at three points between each adjacent pair, not proved non-positive on the whole interval. The
record now says the state satisfies the exact optimality conditions "to the precision quoted and at sampled
points between the mass points", and adds that this is the claim a referee should press on. Overclaiming here
would hand them the objection.
(5) THE FOURTH PAPER, MISSED. Mohammadamin Baniasadi, Luca Barletta, Alex Dytso, "An Improved Lower Bound on
Support Size of Capacity-Achieving Inputs for the Binomial Channel", arXiv 2605.12472, 12 May 2026. Verified:
new lower bound of order sqrt(n log log n), previous best sqrt(n), upper bound n/2; they also give
C(n) = (1/2) log(n pi / 2e) + o(1). This record leans on 23 certified BINOMIAL states and had not cited it.
(6) AND THE BINOMIAL INSTANTIATION, checked. In the binomial's Fisher coordinate the full length is L = pi
sqrt(n), so L^(4/3) gives K of order n^(2/3), with coefficient pi^(4/3) = 4.6012. Against the proved window:
n^(2/3) / sqrt(n log log n) rises (1.74, 3.12, 12.6, 244 at n = 1e2, 1e4, 1e8, 1e16) and n^(2/3)/(n/2) falls
(0.431 to 9.3e-06), so n^(2/3) sits strictly inside. Quote the ORDER only: the prefactors are not carried, so
finite-n instantiations mean nothing. The Abbott-Machta exponent therefore sits inside the proved window on TWO
channels with the same structure.
(7) UNVERIFIED, recorded as such. A secondary source reports that the Wang-Barletta-Dytso lower-bound paper won
the 2026 Jack Keil Wolf ISIT Student Paper Award. Not checked against a primary source.
Gates: NEW/GROUNDBREAKING/FRONTIER/UNSOLVED/WORTH DERIVING not used. (1) corrects our own recorded number and
names how we got it wrong; (4) weakens a sentence because the certificate does not support it;
(7) is labelled UNCHECKED.

## Amendment 479 (2026-09-19) - the Poisson "residual floor" was the loop's exit test, not Newton

(1) THE FAULT, read in the source. `support_mp5.py:167` ends a Newton pass with

        if nr < mpf(10) ** (-dps + tol_pow): break

Every Poisson script calls `solve` with `dps=40, tol_pow=22` (q311:24, q312:16, q324:16, q325:16, q326:17,
q328:27, q329:23), which sets that threshold to 1e-18. The certification bar from q309's procedure is 1e-20.
So the loop's exit sits TWO ORDERS ABOVE the bar the same run is judged by. A pass that lands anywhere in
[1e-20, 1e-18] stops there and is reported as the final residual.

(2) WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT EXPLAIN, kept separate. It does NOT mean the residuals were bad: the exit fires
on the first iterate below 1e-18 and a Newton step near convergence is long, so where it lands is not
controlled. q312 landed at 2.9187e-25, fourteen decades past its own exit. q329's first step landed at
1.2635e-20, just above the bar. Both broke at the same test. What the fault does explain is the specific
reading we wrote last night: "the residual stalls at 1.2635e-20 because 30 Newton steps is not enough." That
diagnosis is WRONG. The run did not exhaust its steps; it satisfied the break and left. We cannot say at which
iteration, because TRACE was not set - which is the same instrumentation rule 463 cost us, applied correctly
this time: we are reading the CODE, not the log's silence.

(3) THE CORRECTION TO THE PLAN. We had announced three fixes - bigger A-steps, more Newton steps, save every
step. The middle one addressed a fault that does not exist. The replacement q330 carries `tol_pow=10`
(exit at 1e-30, a decade below the bar), so the loop runs until it converges or exhausts steps, and the word
"not converged" recovers its meaning.

(4) AND THE A-STEP IS TOO TIMID, from a number already derived. Overshooting DOWNWARD past a count transition
costs nothing: below it, 46 atoms is optimal and the state certifies at a lower A, which is the object wanted.
The only floor is the next transition down, and dN/dA = (2/3)(0.4027) A^(-1/3) = 0.0256 at A = 1151, so
transitions are ~39 apart in A while the secant puts the crossing ~4 below. q329's FRAC = 0.0004 moved 0.46 per
step inside a corridor 39 wide. q330 secants on the two measured off-atom values, deliberately aims 15 % past
the estimate, and caps the move at 0.6 % of A.

(5) PROCESS RULE, third of its kind and the sharpest. BEFORE BLAMING AN ITERATION COUNT, READ THE EXIT TEST.
The two earlier ones (463: confirm the run was instrumented before reading silence; 468: confirm the test case
exhibits the fault) are the same rule at different distances from the code. A solver's stated limit is a claim
about the solver's SETTINGS until the settings have been read. This is the second time on this project that a
"floor" dissolved on inspection - the first was the Poisson residual floor of the third correction listed earlier,
which turned out to be a slow damping phase.

Gates: NEW/GROUNDBREAKING/FRONTIER/UNSOLVED/WORTH DERIVING not used. (2) withdraws our own diagnosis from
last night and says exactly how far the withdrawal reaches; (2) also declines to state the iteration count
because the run was not instrumented to report it.

## Amendment 480 (2026-09-19) - PRE-REGISTRATION: three routes to T, and why the first is cheap

T is now the weakest link in the chain. Everything else is derived from kappa_AM and psi; T is MEASURED, to a
width of 0.007 (461(2)). And 478 established that T is also the shortest route to a bound, because Barletta and
Dytso (2609.10039) prove the count steps only by one, so bounding T bounds the support size. Three candidates,
each with its test fixed here, BEFORE computing.

CANDIDATE 1 - T IS THE ATOMS' PHASE OFFSET AGAINST THE CONTINUUM COUNT.
The claim. Number the atoms j = 1..m from the amplitude wall inward, at Fisher distances d_j, with d_1 = 0
because the edge atom sits AT x = A (437, verified to 1e-15). Let N(d) = int_0^d rho dd' from the derived law.
Then define c := lim_j [ N(d_j) - (j - 1) ], the phase the wall region costs.
  At a transition the new atom nucleates at the CENTRE (439(3)), so at the transition amplitude the centre is
  itself an atom, the (m+1)-th, and N(A) = m + c. The count formula n_half = floor(N(A) - T) + 1 holds with
  n_half = m up to that amplitude, which forces c < T <= c + 1; the transition is the boundary case, so
  PREDICTION:  T = c,  and c must land inside [0.57995, 0.58695].
The test. Compute c on the 13 certified Gaussian states. PASS = c inside the bracket AND agreeing across states
to better than the bracket's own width of 0.007. FAIL = c outside, or drifting with A. Either outcome is
informative: a pass turns a measured constant into a WALL constant, which puts it inside the near-wall system
q321-q323 that is already built; a fail kills the identification and says the count formula's T is not a local
quantity at all. Cost: minutes, every input already on disk.
WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS A NULL RATHER THAN A TAUTOLOGY, asked before running. rho is by construction the atoms'
density, so N(d_j) - (j-1) is near-constant by definition and that alone proves nothing. The content is (i) the
VALUE, which is predicted to be T and could be anything, (ii) the constancy ACROSS states at different A, and
(iii) the PRECISION, which is set by the states and not by a bracket. If c matches T only to 0.007 it has told
us nothing we did not have.

CANDIDATE 2 - THE CENTRE BARRIER'S PREFACTOR CHANGES SIGN.
The barrier L(mid) - L_0 decays as exp(-2.8103 d^(2/3)) over 17 orders (439(3)) and is therefore smallest at the
centre, which is WHY a new atom nucleates there. But an exponential never reaches zero, and the transition
requires the centre barrier to reach zero, so its PREFACTOR must change sign - the same structure as E(z) = 0,
where the exponential exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2) factors out and only the sign change carries information.
The test. Divide the measured centre barrier by exp(-2.8103 h^(2/3)) on the fine-walk states of 461(1) and plot
against N(A) - m. PASS = one curve through zero at T, independent of A. Cost: hours; D(x) on ~14 states.
KNOWN OBSTACLE, recorded now: 461(1) saw the signal jump by a factor 36 across the transition, so the curve is
NOT smooth there and a naive fit through the crossing will lie.

CANDIDATE 3 - THE BRACKET OF E, EXPLICITLY.
With psi Gaussian of variance 2, int psi(u) cos(2 pi rho u) du = exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2) exactly, which IS the
recorded size of E; and int psi(u) sin(2 pi rho u) du = 0 exactly, psi being even. So the linear part of the
phase contributes nothing and E is driven entirely by the curvature of N. Writing
N(z+u) - N(z) = rho u + (rho'/2) u^2 + ..., expanding, and doing the Gaussian moments should give
E = exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2) x B(rho, rho', rho'', ...), with the law being the root of B.
The test. B's root must reproduce q318's X* = 1.7064 to the quadrature's own precision. PASS = it does, and then
B is an explicit function that can be bounded. Cost: algebra plus one numerical check.
Gates: no gate word used. Each candidate carries a stated FAIL condition; candidate 1 carries, in addition, the
condition under which a PASS would still be worthless.

## Amendment 481 (2026-09-19) - THE BULK LAW HAS A CLOSED FORM, AND ITS ASYMPTOTIC VALUE IS pi^2/6

(1) THE DERIVATION. On the constant-X family rho^3 = rho_c^3 + b u, expand the phase in u:
      2 pi [N(z+u) - N(z)] = alpha u + beta u^2 + gamma u^3 + delta u^4 + ...
      alpha = 2 pi rho,  beta = pi b/(3 rho^2),  gamma = -2 pi b^2/(27 rho^5),  delta = 10 pi b^3/(324 rho^8),
with b = 3 sqrt(X/kappa_AM). KEEP THE PHASE TO QUADRATIC ORDER AND THE INTEGRAL IS EXACTLY GAUSSIAN:
      int psi(u) e^{i(alpha u + beta u^2)} du
          = (1+16 beta^2)^(-1/4) exp(-alpha^2/(1+16 beta^2)) exp(i[(1/2)arctan(4 beta) - 4 alpha^2 beta/(1+16 beta^2)])
so E = Im(...) is a POSITIVE AMPLITUDE times the SINE OF A PHASE. That is the structural reason for everything
432(1) found empirically: the amplitude is exp(-alpha^2/(1+16 beta^2)) = exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2 + ...), which is why E
is exponentially small for every smooth profile and why least squares on |E| minimises the wrong thing; and the
sine is the only factor that can vanish, which is why the law had to be imposed as a sign change.
THE LAW IS THEREFORE A PHASE CONDITION:
      PHI(X, rho) := 4 alpha^2 beta/(1+16 beta^2) - (1/2) arctan(4 beta) = pi.
As rho -> infinity, beta = pi sqrt(X/kappa_AM)/rho^2 -> 0 and this collapses to 16 pi^3 sqrt(X/kappa_AM) = pi:
      X_inf = kappa_AM/(256 pi^4) = (128 pi^6/3)/(256 pi^4) = pi^2/6 = 1.6449340668,
      rho^4 rho'^2 -> 4.010149e-05,   with the first correction X(rho) = (pi^2/6)[1 + 1/(4 pi^2 rho^2) + O(rho^-4)].

(2) TWO QUADRATURE FAULTS HAD TO BE FIXED FIRST, and the second is the one that mattered. Every version of this
integral in the record truncates at UM = 12. The integrand carries exp(-u^2/4), so the discarded tail is of order
exp(-UM^2/4) while the ANSWER is of order exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2); the truncation is negligible only while
      UM > 4 pi rho,   i.e. only while rho < 12/(4 pi) = 0.9549 at UM = 12.
Measured at rho = 1.00, X = 1.70: UM = 10 gives -6.170e-13, UM = 12 gives -2.351e-18, UM = 14 gives +1.2191e-19,
UM = 16 gives +1.2189e-19. UM = 12 has the WRONG SIGN and is twenty-fold too large. q318's own range was
rho in [0.62, 0.90], where 4 pi rho <= 11.31 < 12, SO q318 STANDS - but what we had recorded as a precision
ceiling was a truncation condition, and it is now a formula instead of an observation. (The first fault, float64
roundoff at E ~ 1e-17, is real too and is fixed by mpmath with dps tracking 4 pi^2 rho^2/ln 10.)

(3) THE TEST, PRE-REGISTERED IN 480 AND PASSED. Fit X*(rho) = X_inf + a rho^-2 + c rho^-4 to the corrected
quadrature over rho in [0.80, 2.20], 15 points, X* falling monotonically 1.7012037 -> 1.6534235:
      X_inf = 1.6447166   against pi^2/6 = 1.6449341        -0.013 %    PASS (bar was 0.2 %)
      a     = 0.0428171   against X_inf/(4 pi^2) = 0.0416667  +2.76 %   PASS (bar was 10 %)
      c     = -0.0042453, rms residual 3.48e-05.
The competing hypothesis, 8928's extrapolated X_inf = 1.7036, is 3.58 % away and is excluded.

(4) THREE CHECKS THAT COULD HAVE KILLED IT (q336). (a) THE GAUSSIAN IDENTITY against direct integration at the
physical parameters: agreement to 40 and 31 digits at (alpha, beta) = (4.4, 0.025) and (6.3, 0.0249); the third
sample at alpha = 12.6 is a limit of the CHECK, whose answer is 1e-49 at dps 40, not of the identity. (b) THE
BRANCH: evaluate the closed-form phase AT THE QUADRATURE'S OWN ROOT - it must be pi. It runs 3.0817, 3.1252,
3.1354, 3.1388, 3.1401, 3.140592 at rho = 0.80 .. 2.20, and PHI - pi falls as rho^(-4.045), which is EXACTLY the
order of the first phase term dropped. A coincidence of two nearby roots does not converge on the right power.
Only one branch lies in the search bracket. (c) THE COUNT COEFFICIENT by integrating the ODE instead of trusting
the algebra: 0.4002442492 against (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) = 0.4002442498.

(5) THE CONSEQUENCE, in closed form and with nothing fitted:
      K(A) -> (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) = 0.4002442498 A^(4/3)   (Gaussian, amplitude A)
and by the Fisher lengths, 0.4002442 A^(2/3) for the Poisson and 0.4002442 (pi/2)^(4/3) n^(2/3) = 0.7389 n^(2/3)
for the symmetric binomial. Against Abbott-Machta: their Eq. (12) balance gives X = 1 EXACTLY (451), so the
discrepancy is now a PURE NUMBER, pi^2/6, and their prefactor of K is low by (pi^2/6)^(1/6) = 1.0864875, i.e.
8.65 %. This replaces "1.707" and "9.32 %", which were the values at the rho of the certified states.
STATED PLAINLY SO IT IS NOT DRESSED UP: pi^2/6 here is kappa_AM/(256 pi^4) with kappa_AM = 128 pi^6/3. It is
arithmetic in their own constant. It is not the Basel constant arriving from anywhere.

(6) WHAT THIS FORCES US TO WITHDRAW.
  (a) 8928's "1/X_inf = 0.5870 +- 0.0012 (Gaussian)" and every use of X_inf = 1.7036 as an ASYMPTOTE. The true
      asymptote is 3.58 % below it. Cause: extrapolating from rho in [0.62, 0.90], where the rho^-2 correction is
      still 4 to 7 %. This is our own recorded rule - AN EXTRAPOLATED VALUE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT UNTIL THE NEXT
      ORDER HAS BEEN SHOWN NOT TO MOVE IT - failing for the third time on this project.
  (b) 461(3)'s candidate closed form for the count threshold, 1/X = 1/1.70637 = 0.586039. X is not a constant, so
      "1/X" names no constant; and the asymptotic 6/pi^2 = 0.607927 lies OUTSIDE the bracket [0.57995, 0.58695].
      That candidate is dead. 7/12 = 0.583333 survives, still unchecked and still not claimed.
  (c) "X* = 1.7064" as THE bulk law. It is X*(rho) at the rho of the certified states. The law is a function.
(7) WHAT STANDS UNCHANGED. The exponent 4/3 (any constant X gives rho ~ x^(1/3)); the 13/13 and 23/23 integer
count tests, which used X*(rho) evaluated where the states live and not the asymptote; the sign-change principle;
and q318, whose range never violated (2)'s condition.

## Amendment 485 (2026-09-19) - E IS AN EXPONENTIAL TIMES A CONVERGENT O(1) SERIES, EXACTLY

(1) WHY THE OBVIOUS INEQUALITY FAILS, recorded so it is not tried again. With
2 pi [N(z+u) - N(z)] = alpha u + beta u^2 + R(u), the bound |e^{iR} - 1| <= |R| gives
|E - Im I2| <= int psi |R| du = 2.5e-04 at rho = 0.9, against an amplitude of 1e-14. That is
|sin(phase)| <= 2.5e10, which says nothing. Absolute values inside the integral destroy the oscillation that
makes E exponentially small, and any bound of that shape will.

(2) THE ROUTE THAT KEEPS IT. Every moment against the quadratic-phase Gaussian is exact:
      M_n = int psi(u) u^n e^{i(alpha u + beta u^2)} du = i^n a^{n/2} H_n(alpha sqrt a) I2,
      a = 1/(1 - 4 i beta),   I2 = a^{1/2} e^{-alpha^2 a},
with H_n the Hermite polynomial. I2 is a COMMON FACTOR of every term, so writing
exp(i R(u)) = sum_m c_m u^m and G := sum_m c_m i^m a^{m/2} H_n(alpha sqrt a),
      E = Im[I2 G] = |I2| |G| sin(Theta_0 + arg G),   Theta_0 = (1/2)arctan(4 beta) - 4 alpha^2 beta/(1+16 beta^2).
THE EXACT LAW IS THEREFORE   Theta_0 + arg G = -pi,  where 481's closed form is the arg G = 0 truncation.
The phase coefficients are exact: theta_k = (3 pi/2) binom(4/3, k) b^(k-1) rho^(4-3k), b = 3 sqrt(X/kappa_AM),
verified against the four computed by hand (2 pi rho, pi b/3 rho^2, -2 pi b^2/27 rho^5, 5 pi b^3/162 rho^8).

(3) IT IS NOT AN APPROXIMATION - IT REPRODUCES THE QUADRATURE EXACTLY. E/|I2| against the corrected 40-digit
quadrature at X = 1.70, partial sums through m:
     rho = 0.80:  m<=4  +0.01536094,  m<=10 -0.00070931,  m<=18 -0.00087404,  m<=26 -0.00087405   quad -0.00087405
     rho = 1.40:  m<=4  +0.03024086,  m<=10 +0.02978964,  m<=18 +0.02978873,  m<=26 +0.02978873   quad +0.02978873
     rho = 2.00:  m<=26 +0.0404865205                                                             quad +0.0404865205
And the ROOT of the series against the quadrature's X*: 6.9e-10 at rho = 0.80 and 1e-15 at rho >= 1.1, against
the bare quadratic form's 4.1e-02 and 9.4e-04. TRUNCATION CONTROL: (K, M) = (18, 34) and (22, 40) agree to 1e-12
in E/|I2| and 1e-11 in X*.

(4) WHAT THIS OPENS. E = 0 is equivalent to sin(Theta_0 + arg G) = 0 with G an absolutely convergent series of
O(1) terms, and c_0 = 1 with c_1 = c_2 = 0 since R starts at u^3. A bound on |G - 1| bounds |arg G|, hence bounds
Theta_0, hence bounds X two-sidedly, hence bounds rho and N = int rho. The ingredients are all explicit: |a| =
(1+16 beta^2)^(-1/2) <= 1, the c_m are the coefficients of exp(i sum theta_k u^k) and are majorised by those of
exp(sum |theta_k| u^k), and what remains is a bound on |H_m(alpha sqrt a)| at complex argument. That is standard
analysis, not a new idea, and it is the first route to an INEQUALITY this record has had.

(5) THE CAVEAT THAT DOES NOT GO AWAY, stated before any of this is called a bound. All of it bounds X GIVEN
E = 0, and E = 0 comes from the stationarity of the ripple energy (427, 429), which is derived and not proved.
A completed bound would read: IF the ripple energy is the exact leading functional, THEN K(A) =
(81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) (1 + explicit). That is a conditional statement, and calling it a resolution of the
published open problem would be false.

(6) AN INSTRUMENT FAULT, THIRD OF ITS KIND. The rho = 2.00 quadrature first came back as 1.6e19 because we called
Etrap from a script whose mp.dps was 50 while E there is 1e-69. The value was noise and we nearly read it as a
number. FIXED IN THE INSTRUMENT: Etrap now calls setdps(rc) itself. RULE: WHEN AN INSTRUMENT'S PRECISION MUST
TRACK A PARAMETER, IT TRACKS IT INSIDE THE INSTRUMENT, NEVER AT THE CALL SITE. This joins 463 (confirm the run
was instrumented before reading silence), 468 (confirm the test case exhibits the fault) and 479 (read the exit
test before blaming an iteration count).
Gates: no gate word used. (5) states in advance what the bound would and would not be.

(1) THE COUNT THE CORRECTED LAW PREDICTS. The Poisson Fisher coordinate t = 2 sqrt x gives length L = 2 sqrt A

maximum. Marching both (q345): at A = 1151.334, L = 67.863, the branches meet at d = 34.44 with rho_max =
0.87555, and N = 45.2440. 459(5) got 45.210 with the old law, so the correction moves it by 0.034.
(2) THE DISCREPANCY, RESTATED AND UNRESOLVED. The count is floor(N - T) + 1, which for any T in (0, 1) gives 45
or 46. The state has 46 atoms and its off-support signal is +2.687e-12 at the centre, so a further atom is WANTED
and the true count there is at least 47. Matching that needs T_eff <= -0.756, outside [0, 1]. The law
under-counts this channel by 1.7 to 1.8 atoms, which is exactly 459(5)'s figure, and THE CORRECTED LAW DOES NOT
FIX IT. Nor can the borrowed origin constant: N = 45.16, 45.24, 45.45, 45.89, 46.64 at rho_origin^3 = 0.0020,
0.0042, 0.0100, 0.0238, 0.0500, so reaching 47 would need a value ten times the borrowed one and still fall
short. So the Poisson gap is a property of the LAW'S TREATMENT OF THE TWO ENDS, not of the state, and certifying
a state will not close it.
(3) WHAT THIS DOES TO THE WALK, which is running now. We set its target at A = 1147.1 from a LINEAR extrapolation
through two values of the off-support signal, 2.687e-12 at A = 1151.334 and 2.3953e-12 at 1150.873. That signal
is a BARRIER: 439(3) has it decaying as exp(-2.8103 d^(2/3)) and 461(1) saw it jump by a factor 36 across a
transition. Extrapolating an exponentially varying quantity linearly through two points is the error this record
names in three places. Taking the same two points as exponential gives a rate of 0.251 per unit A and no zero at
all. Two points cannot distinguish the two, and they disagree by tens of units in A.
(4) THE SCALE THAT DOES FOLLOW. dN/dA = 0.0258 for this channel, so ONE ATOM IS 38.7 IN AMPLITUDE. Whatever the
signal is doing, a count change is either essentially at A = 1151.3 already or about 38.7 below it. There is no
mechanism that puts it at 4 below, which is where the walk is pointed.
(5) WHAT THE WALK IS STILL FOR, since it stays running. Every step now saves its state, so each one adds a point
to the signal curve; three or four points settle the shape that two cannot. And a certified Poisson state remains
worth having for its own sake: it would fix the count at one amplitude and so pin the end constants that (2) says

the state.

and since X = kappa s^2,   a/X_inf = 2 u2 = 1/(4 pi^2) EXACTLY, matching the fit to 5e-05 relative.

(4) THE rho^-4 COEFFICIENT, DECOMPOSED AND ONLY HALF DERIVED. The same expansion gives the QUADRATIC-ONLY value

## Amendment 490 (2026-09-19) - the architecture of the inequality, with one piece left to write

(1) THE SENSITIVITY, EXACT. The law is PHI(X, rho) = pi + arg G, and PHI is monotone in X, so a bound on
|arg G| brackets X. The conversion factor is a pure number:
        dPHI/dX = 8 pi^3 / sqrt(X kappa_AM),  and at X = pi^2/6, kappa_AM = 128 pi^6/3,  X kappa_AM = 64 pi^8/9,
        so dPHI/dX = 3/pi   and   dX/d(arg G) -> pi/3 = 1.0471976.
Measured along the exact solution: 1.0691, 1.0581, 1.0536, 1.0501, 1.0488, 1.0479, 1.0475, 1.0473, 1.0472 at
rho = 1 .. 30. So |X(rho) - X_closed form(rho)| <= (pi/3) |arg G| with no further approximation.

(2) WHAT arg G ACTUALLY DOES, measured at the root. |arg G| = 2.417e-02, 4.678e-03, 1.468e-03, 2.881e-04,
9.094e-05, 1.793e-05, 2.322e-06, 3.542e-07, 2.866e-08 at rho = 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 10, 16, 30. Fitted power
-4.0014, amplitude arg G rho^4 -> 0.02321. So arg G ~ 0.0232 rho^-4, which is why the closed form's residual
falls as rho^-4 and why the rho^-2 coefficient of X is untouched by it.

(3) AND WHY THE NAIVE BOUND IS LOOSE BY rho^2, which matters for how the bound is written. |G - 1| decays as
rho^-1.997 with amplitude 0.1667, NOT as rho^-4: it is dominated by the m = 3 term, which at rho = 16 is
6.51e-04 against |G-1| = 6.508e-04, i.e. the whole of it. That term is very nearly REAL, so it moves |G| and not
arg G. The phase is carried by m = 4 and m = 6: at rho = 16 they are 2.53e-07 and 2.12e-07 against
arg G = 3.54e-07. So |arg G| <= |G-1|/(1-|G-1|) is VALID but gives rho^-2 where the truth is rho^-4. A bound
that tracks the imaginary part is worth the extra work; one that does not still suffices for an asymptotic
statement.

(4) WHAT REMAINS, stated as a finite task and not as a hope. Everything in
        |arg G| <= |G-1|/(1-|G-1|),   |G-1| <= sum_{m>=3} |c_m| |a|^{m/2} |H_m(alpha sqrt a)|
is explicit except the last factor: |a| = (1+16 beta^2)^(-1/2) <= 1, and the c_m are the Taylor coefficients of
exp(i sum_k theta_k u^k) with theta_k = (3 pi/2) binom(4/3, k) b^(k-1) rho^(4-3k), majorised termwise by the
coefficients of exp(sum |theta_k| u^k). The missing piece is a bound on the Hermite polynomial at COMPLEX
argument alpha sqrt a. The series is geometric with ratio about 4 pi b/rho^2 = 0.24/rho^2, and the measured term
sizes confirm it: at rho = 4 the terms run 1.04e-02, 6.46e-05, 5.38e-05, 7.33e-09, 3.41e-09, 1.98e-13, 1.35e-18
at m = 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 14, 20.

(5) WHAT A COMPLETED BOUND WOULD SAY, written now so it cannot be inflated later.
        X(rho) = (pi^2/6)[1 + 1/(4 pi^2 rho^2)] + R(rho),  |R(rho)| <= (pi/3) B(rho),  B explicit and O(rho^-4),
and hence, through rho^3 = 3 sqrt(X/kappa) d and N = int rho dd,
        K(A) = (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) (1 + O(A^(-2/3))) with an explicit constant.
IT WOULD REMAIN CONDITIONAL on E = 0, which is the stationarity of the ripple energy - established numerically
in 427 by an eps-scaling test on three perturbation shapes, and not proved. 485(5) says this and it stands.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) records that our first bound is loose by two powers rather than presenting it as
the answer; (5) restates the conditionality before anything is built on it.
