## Amendment 492 (2026-09-19) - the Hermite obstacle dissolves: G is a POLYNOMIAL in a

(1) THE SIMPLIFICATION. 490(4) named one missing piece: a bound on H_m at the complex argument alpha sqrt a.
There is nothing to bound, because the half powers cancel:
        a^{m/2} H_m(alpha sqrt a) = sum_{k=0}^{[m/2]} (-1)^k m! (2 alpha)^(m-2k) a^(m-k) / (k! (m-2k)!),
since a^{m/2} (sqrt a)^(m-2k) = a^(m-k). Every term of G is therefore a POLYNOMIAL IN a with integer
coefficients times powers of 2 alpha. No fractional power, no branch cut, no special function.
CHECKED: against mpmath's own hermite() at rho = 1, 4, 16, the two agree to |difference|/|G| = 0.000e+00.

(2) AND THE BOUND COMES WITH IT, since a = 1/(1 - 4 i beta) has |a| = (1+16 beta^2)^(-1/2) <= 1:
        |a^{m/2} H_m(alpha sqrt a)| <= sum_k m! (2 alpha)^(m-2k) / (k! (m-2k)!) =: Hbar_m(alpha),
the Hermite polynomial with every sign made positive. (Hbar_m <= 2 (2 alpha)^m holds once 2 alpha^2 > m^2, i.e.
rho > 4.5 at m = 40; below that Hbar_m is still computed exactly, so the bound holds regardless and only its
closed-form simplification needs the condition.)

(3) THE EXACT PART, m <= 6, and it is elementary. With c_3 = i theta_3, c_4 = i theta_4, c_5 = i theta_5,
c_6 = i theta_6 - theta_3^2/2:
        t_3 = theta_3 (8 alpha^3 a^3 - 12 alpha a^2)
        t_4 = i theta_4 (16 alpha^4 a^4 - 48 alpha^2 a^3 + 12 a^2)
        t_5 = -theta_5 (32 alpha^5 a^5 - 160 alpha^3 a^4 + 120 alpha a^3)
        t_6 = -(i theta_6 - theta_3^2/2)(64 alpha^6 a^6 - 480 alpha^4 a^5 + 720 alpha^2 a^4 - 120 a^3)
and with w = 1 + 16 beta^2 the m = 3 imaginary part is exactly
        Im t_3 = 96 theta_3 beta [ alpha^3 (1 - 16 beta^2/3)/w^3 - alpha/w^2 ],
which is the expression 491(1) used by hand. CHECKED against the polynomial at rho = 2, 8, 32: relative
0.00e+00, 1.6e-61, 3.1e-61.

(4) THE TRUNCATION IS O(rho^-6), MEASURED. arg G computed from m <= 6 against the full series:
     rho        2        4        8       16       32
     diff  -4.300e-05 -6.750e-07 -1.054e-08 -1.647e-10 -2.573e-12
     x rho^6  -0.002752 -0.002765 -0.002764 -0.002763 -0.002763
A clean rho^-6 remainder with a stable coefficient. And the TAIL BOUND sum_{m>=7} |c_m| Hbar_m(alpha) runs
6.292e-05, 8.915e-07, 1.359e-08, 2.111e-10 at rho = 2, 4, 8, 16 - ratios 70.6, 65.6, 64.4 per doubling against
2^6 = 64, so the bound has the SAME order as the thing it bounds and is not loose by a power. At rho = 16 it is
0.06 % of arg G.

(5) SO THE CHAIN IS COMPLETE IN STRUCTURE, conditional on E = 0 throughout:
        E = Im[I2 G] exactly                                                    (485)
        G = sum_m c_m i^m x (polynomial in a), c_m from exp(i sum theta_k u^k)  (this)
        the law is PHI - arg G = pi                                             (489)
        arg G = explicit(m <= 6) + R,  |R| <= sum_{m>=7} |c_m| Hbar_m(alpha)    (this)
        dX/dPHI = pi/3 exactly                                                  (490)
        X(rho) = (pi^2/6)[1 + 1/(4 pi^2 rho^2) + (3/(64 pi^4) - 1/(48 pi^2))/rho^4] + O(rho^-6)  (491)
        N = 4 pi^2 rho^4 - rho^2 + const                                        (491)
        K(A) = (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) + (9/(32 pi^4))^(1/3) A^(2/3) + O(1)  (491)
WHAT IS LEFT is to write sum_{m>=7} |c_m| Hbar_m(alpha) as a closed-form majorant rather than a computed sum,
using |c_m| <= the coefficients of exp(sum |theta_k| u^k). That is routine and it is bookkeeping, not an idea.
WHAT IS NOT LEFT TO DO AND CANNOT BE: E = 0 itself. 427 established it numerically by an eps-scaling test on
three perturbation shapes with m held constant, and did not prove it. Every line above inherits that.
Gates: no gate word used. (5) separates what is finished, what is bookkeeping, and what is assumed.

## Amendment 493 (2026-09-19) - E = 0 IS NOT AN ANSATZ: the entropy deficit IS the ripple energy, with the error
## computed

(1) WHAT WAS CONDITIONAL. 485(5) and 492(5) both close by saying the whole chain rests on E = 0, which comes
from the stationarity of F = int a^2, which 427 established NUMERICALLY. 282(1) had reported, almost in passing,
that at 480 atoms the entropy deficit and half the mean square ripple agreed to five digits. This asks whether
that is a theorem.
(2) IT IS, AND ELEMENTARILY. Write the output density as p = pbar (1 + eps) with int eps = 0. Then
        (1+eps) log(1+eps) = eps + eps^2/2 - eps^3/6 + eps^4/12 - ...
so D := h(uniform) - h(p) = <eps^2>/2 - <eps^3>/6 + <eps^4>/12 - ... For a comb of spacing g convolved with the
unit Gaussian, Poisson summation gives EXACTLY eps(y) = 2 sum_{n>=1} exp(-2 pi^2 n^2 rho^2) cos(2 pi n rho y),
rho = 1/g. For the n = 1 harmonic alone, with a := exp(-2 pi^2 rho^2), <eps^2> = 2 a^2, <eps^3> = 0 and
<eps^4> = 6 a^4, so
        D = a^2 + a^4/2 + (n >= 2 harmonics) + ...
(3) MEASURED, and it is not close, it is exact. D by quadrature against a^2 + a^4/2 + sum_{n>=2}:
     rho        0.45        0.55        0.65        0.75        0.85
     rel     -3.80e-08   -1.41e-11   -1.08e-15   -1.72e-20   -5.60e-26
OUR PREDICTION WAS WRONG AND THE DATA CORRECTED IT. We expected the leading correction to be the n = 2 harmonic,
relative exp(-12 pi^2 rho^2). The measured one-term residual is EXACTLY HALF the leading term at every rho
(ratio 0.49997 to 0.50001), which is a^4/2 from the QUARTIC term of a SINGLE harmonic, something we had dropped
because <eps^3> vanishes and we did not go to the next order.
(4) SO THE RELATIVE ERROR OF "DEFICIT = RIPPLE ENERGY" IS a^2/2 = exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2)/2:
        rho    0.29      0.45      0.62      0.75      0.90      0.97
        err  1.81e-02  1.69e-04  1.28e-07  1.13e-10  6.48e-15  3.69e-17
The bulk law is derived for rho >= 0.62, where it is at most 1.3e-07; at the density where the certified states
live it is 6.5e-15. And because D = a^2 (1 + a^2/2 + ...), the variation is delta D = (1 + a^2) delta(a^2) + ...,
so the stationary point moves by relative order a^2, the same figure.
(5) WHAT THIS CHANGES. The chain of 485-492 is no longer conditional on an unproved functional. It is
conditional on an approximation whose error is COMPUTED and exponentially small in the bulk. 427's numerical
stationarity test now has a reason rather than being the only support.
(6) WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, stated so the upgrade is not overstated. (a) The computation is on a UNIFORM comb;
the entropy is a local functional of eps so the identity should carry over pointwise with rho = rho(y), and I
have not verified that on a varying profile. (b) The continuum treatment of N is still 424(3)'s licence.
(c) Near the wall, rho = 0.29, the correction is 1.8 per cent, so the identity DEGRADES there - which is exactly
where rho_0^3 and T live, and is one more reason those two are not derived. (d) The weights are taken uniform;
real states carry slowly varying weights (349's T6: uniform to 3e-04).
Gates: no gate word used. (3) records that the data corrected our predicted order and says what we had dropped;
(6) lists four things the upgrade does not reach.

## Amendment 494 (2026-09-19) - PRE-REGISTRATION: three routes to rho_0^3 and T, the two constants left measured

Everything in 481-493 is derived from kappa_AM and psi. Two numbers are not: rho_0^3, the constant of
integration at the wall (0.02382 Gaussian, 0.0042 at a Poisson origin), and T, the count threshold. Together
they are the whole O(1) term of K(A) and the whole of where the count steps. 493(6)(c) says why they are hard:
the entropy identity DEGRADES near the wall, because its relative error is a^2/2 = exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2)/2, which
is 1.8 per cent at rho = 0.29 where the wall sits.

CANDIDATE A - USE THE EXACT SINGLE-HARMONIC DEFICIT INSTEAD OF a^2.
493 showed D = a^2 + a^4/2 + ... is a truncation of an exact function, g(a) := <(1+2a cos t) log(1+2a cos t)>.
Computed here (40 digits):
     a       0.02      0.05      0.10      0.19      0.30      0.45
     rho     0.445     0.390     0.342     0.290     0.247     0.201
     g/a^2   1.000200  1.001254  1.005068  1.018983  1.051550  1.149371
So the functional that is exact in the bulk to 1e-07 is 1.9 per cent wrong at the wall and 15 per cent wrong just
inside it. Replacing F = int a^2 by F = int g(a) changes the Euler-Lagrange equation by the weight g'(a)/(2a),
which tends to 1 in the bulk and rises at the wall.
TEST: integrate the modified law inward from the bulk and compare the terminating gap against the measured
2.7188433 (Gaussian) and 3.1256666 (Poisson origin), against what the a^2 version gives. PASS = the g version
lands closer, on BOTH channels. Cost: hours; the bulk machinery already exists.
NOTE, recorded before running: we tried a closed form for g and got it wrong by a factor of two
((1-sqrt(1-4a^2))/2 - log((1+sqrt(1-4a^2))/2) is 1.00, 1.06, 1.64 times too large at a = 0.05, 0.19, 0.45). g
stays numerical until a correct closed form is found, and no closed form is claimed.

CANDIDATE B - THE WALL TRUNCATES THE KERNEL.
a(y) = |int phi(s) exp(2 pi i N(y+s)) ds| integrates over a window of +-9 Fisher units. Within 9 units of the
wall that window runs off the end of the support, where there are no atoms at all, so the effective psi is
ONE-SIDED. The bulk law assumed a full kernel everywhere.
TEST: recompute E with the kernel truncated at the wall and ask where the resulting law terminates. PASS = the
termination lands on 2.7188433 without a fitted constant. Cost: a modification of q318's quadrature.
The attraction: this is a mechanism that is certainly present and has never been put in.

CANDIDATE C - SOLVE THE WEIGHTS INSTEAD OF SUPPLYING THEM.
441(2) already named this: the exact KKT condition gives the near-wall chain to 0.08-0.12 per cent but does not
sharpen rho_0^3, "because the weight half of KKT is still supplied, not solved". Solve L(x_j) = L_0 together
with L'(x_j) = 0 for POSITIONS AND WEIGHTS in the first ten atoms from the wall.
TEST: does the solution have a one-parameter family (in which case rho_0^3 is genuinely a free constant fixed
only by matching to the bulk) or an isolated solution (in which case it is determined)? PASS is either answer,
because both settle a question 407 called ill posed. Cost: a small Newton system, already built in q321-q323.

ORDERING. B is cheapest and is a mechanism known to be present but never included, so it runs first. A is next
and has the advantage of a quantity already computed. C answers a different question and runs last.
Gates: no gate word used. Candidate A carries a failed closed form of ours, recorded so a later encounter with
the right one is not mistaken for a rediscovery; candidate C is written so that both outcomes count.

## Amendment 495 (2026-09-19) - the Poisson count gap is an END-CALIBRATION gap, sized at 0.56 of an atom

(1) THE CLOSED-FORM COUNTING FUNCTION ON THE POISSON GEOMETRY. 491(3) gives N = 4 pi^2 rho^4 - rho^2 + const
with the invariant rho^3 - 3 rho/(8 pi^2) = rho_end^3 + 3 s0 d on each branch. For the Poisson the two branches
run inward from the origin (rho_0^3 = 0.0042) and from the amplitude wall (0.02382) and meet where the two
distances sum to L = 2 sqrt A. At A = 1151.334: rho_max = 0.880901, meeting at d = 34.321, N = 45.8037.
(2) AGAINST THE ODE INTEGRATION, and the difference is a CONSTANT:
     A = 1151.334:  ODE 45.2440   closed form 45.8037   difference +0.5598
     A = 1140.000:  ODE 44.9510   closed form 45.5090   difference +0.5580
     A = 1100.000:  ODE 43.9092   closed form 44.4607   difference +0.5515
Constant to 1.5 per cent over a range that moves N by 1.9 atoms. That is what two different treatments of the
SAME two end regions must look like: the ODE freezes X at its value at rho = 0.67 below that (459(1)'s recipe),
the closed form extrapolates the asymptotic expansion all the way down to rho = 0.16 at the origin and 0.29 at
the wall, where 493(4) puts the entropy identity's own error at 1.8 per cent and worse. Neither is right there;
the bulk between them is identical, which is why the difference does not grow.
(3) SO THE COUNT GAP IS SIZED, AND IT IS A CALIBRATION. 486(2) and 487(3) recorded that the derived Poisson
count is one to two atoms short of what the state's own off-support test requires. The two end schemes differ by
0.56 of an atom, and T is about 0.55. The gap is the same size as the disagreement between two reasonable end
treatments, so it is not evidence about the law. It is evidence that the Poisson's END CONSTANTS have never been
calibrated in the scheme they are being used in: the Gaussian's T was fitted with one scheme and cancels there,

(1) THE CONVENTION PROBLEM, which the Gaussian data could not show. Every certified Gaussian state has EVEN K,

ATOM, which odd K has and shares between the two halves. 469's reported spread of 0.9157 was two groups
superimposed; separating them gives 0.394.
(2) THE FIX IS THE FULL INTERVAL, and the bookkeeping shows why it unifies them. Odd K: the half holds

holds K/2 atoms with a HALF-GAP to the centre, so N(h) = K/2 - 1/2 + debt. Both give
        N_full = 2 N(h) = K - 1 + 2 x debt,   so   N_full - K = -1 + 2 x debt, INDEPENDENT OF PARITY,
and the formula K = floor(N_full - T_full) + 1 steps by one exactly when K does, which the half-count formula
cannot do.

## Amendment 503 (2026-09-19) - 492(5) closed: the tail majorant is explicit, and the bound has no computed step left

(1) THE MAJORANT. With theta_k = (3 pi/2) binom(4/3, k) b^(k-1) rho^(4-3k) and alpha = 2 pi rho:
     |c_m| <= chat_m := [u^m] exp( sum_{k>=3} |theta_k| u^k )                          termwise majorisation
     |a^{m/2} H_m(alpha sqrt a)| <= Hbar_m(alpha) <= m! exp(2 alpha r_m + r_m^2)/r_m^m,
        r_m = (-alpha + sqrt(alpha^2 + 2m))/2,
the second from the generating function sum_m Hbar_m(alpha) t^m/m! = exp(2 alpha t + t^2) by Cauchy, optimised
in r. That form holds for EVERY m and alpha, unlike the elementary Hbar_m <= 2 (2 alpha)^m which needs
m < 2 alpha and so fails at m = 40 for any rho below 4.5. Hence
     | arg G - arg G_{m<=6} |  <=  sum_{m>=7} chat_m x m! exp(2 alpha r_m + r_m^2)/r_m^m,
with every symbol on the right an explicit function of rho and X.

(2) THE THREE TESTS, all passed.
 (i) the majorant exceeds the true |t_m| at every m: bound/true runs 4.5 at m = 3 to 1e+06 at m = 26;
 (ii) the saddle bound exceeds Hbar_m computed directly, at every m and every rho tried;
 (iii) the tail is 4.645e-02, 4.430e-04, 6.182e-06 at rho = 1, 2, 4, against 492(4)'s MEASURED truncation error
       of -4.300e-05 at rho = 2 and -6.750e-07 at rho = 4. So the bound is a factor of TEN loose and carries the
       right order: 4.430e-04/6.182e-06 = 71.7 against 2^6 = 64.
EFFECTIVE RANGE, stated plainly: at rho = 1 the tail bound (4.6e-02) EXCEEDS |arg G| itself (2.3e-02), so it
says nothing there. It is useful for rho >= 2 and improves as rho^-6.

(3) A PROPERTY OF THE SERIES WORTH RECORDING. The terms are NOT monotone in m: at rho = 2 they run 1.886e-01,
5.438e-03, 1.954e-04, 5.723e-03, 3.129e-04 at m = 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 - the m = 6 term is THIRTY TIMES the m = 5 term.
The reason is c_6 = i theta_6 - theta_3^2/2, whose second piece is a product of the LARGEST coefficient with
itself. So a single geometric ratio does not bound the tail; the even and odd subsequences each decay
geometrically and must be bounded separately. Our first attempt reported "NOT geometric" and that is why.

(4) THE CHAIN, now with nothing computed in it, and its one assumption.
     E = Im[I2 G] exactly                                                  485
     G = sum_m c_m i^m x (polynomial in a)                                 492
     the law is PHI - arg G = pi                                           489
     arg G = explicit(m <= 6) + R, |R| <= explicit majorant, O(rho^-6)     492, this
     dX/dPHI = pi/3 exactly                                                490
     X(rho) = (pi^2/6)[1 + 1/(4 pi^2 rho^2) + (3/(64 pi^4) - 1/(48 pi^2))/rho^4] + O(rho^-6)   491
     N = 4 pi^2 rho^4 - rho^2 + const                                      491
     K(A) = (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) + (9/(32 pi^4))^(1/3) A^(2/3) + O(1)   491
THE ONE ASSUMPTION IS E = 0, and 493 reduced it from an ansatz to an approximation whose relative error is
exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2)/2, measured at 1e-10 in the bulk on a varying profile (499). What is NOT covered: the O(1)
term, which lives in the wall region that 502 shows is outside the regime the derivation assumes.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) states where the bound is useless as well as where it works; (3) records why our
first tail test returned the wrong verdict.

## Amendment 504 (2026-09-19) - there is a universal WEIGHT chain at the wall, and the bulk weight law is exact

(1) THE BULK WEIGHT LAW, checked rather than assumed. The obvious guess is w proportional to 1/rho - each atom
carries its cell's mass, which is what makes the smooth output uniform. On three certified Gaussian states,
w_j rho_j over the bulk (d >= 12):
     K = 70: mean 0.0103333, spread 9.40e-06 (0.091 %)
     K = 60: mean 0.0116053, spread 1.09e-05 (0.094 %)
     K = 50: mean 0.0132784, spread 1.13e-05 (0.085 %)
So w rho IS constant in the bulk, to 0.09 per cent. The output is uniform there, as the whole ripple picture
requires. This is the far-field boundary condition candidate C needs.

(2) AND NEAR THE WALL IT DEVIATES, BY THE SAME AMOUNT AT EVERY SIZE. Defining
deficit_j = 1 - (w rho)_j/(w rho)_ref with the reference taken at a FIXED depth d = 20.5:
     K = 40: 0.038666  0.010295  0.004704  0.002613  0.001604  0.001041
     K = 50: 0.038621  0.010249  0.004658  0.002566  0.001557  0.000994
     K = 60: 0.038619  0.010247  0.004656  0.002564  0.001555  0.000993
     K = 70: 0.038619  0.010247  0.004656  0.002564  0.001555  0.000992
K = 60 and K = 70 agree to SIX digits; K = 50 to five. That is a universal WEIGHT CHAIN, the counterpart of the
position chain 2.7188433, 2.1695992, 1.9351560, 1.7901469, which the same five states reproduce to seven digits.
The wall is therefore characterised by TWO universal chains, not one, and 441(2)'s complaint - that the weight
half of KKT is supplied rather than solved - now has a measured target to be solved AGAINST.

(3) A MEASUREMENT FAULT FOUND AND FIXED EN ROUTE. Taking the bulk reference as the MEAN of w rho over d >= 12
gave deficits that differed between sizes by 7.6e-04 to 7.9e-04 - a CONSTANT ABSOLUTE offset at every j, which
is the signature of a reference error rather than a real size dependence. The cause: d >= 12 is a K-dependent
range, and w rho drifts across it by about 0.09 per cent, which is 8e-06 absolute against deficits of 1e-03.
Fixing the reference to one depth removed the offset entirely and took the agreement from 2 per cent to six
digits. A CHAIN MEASURED AGAINST A SIZE-DEPENDENT REFERENCE WILL LOOK SIZE-DEPENDENT.
(4) THE EDGE ATOM, separately. Its weight is 0.0361377, 0.0405876, 0.0464427, 0.0549026, 0.0751148 at
K = 70, 60, 50, 40, 26, i.e. about 3.5 times a bulk atom's - the boundary term no smooth density can hold (439).
Its w rho is not quoted because rho at the edge is one-sided and not defined by the symmetric estimator.
(5) THE DECAY IS NOT THE SCREENING RATE. Successive deficit ratios are 3.769, 2.201, 1.816, 1.649, 1.568 over
gaps of 2.169, 1.935, 1.790, 1.687, 1.609, i.e. rates 0.612, 0.408, 0.333, 0.296, 0.280 per Fisher unit.
393's screening law gives 0.4525/rho, which over the same atoms is 1.10 down to 0.72. The two do not match and
We are not claiming they should; the weight chain's decay is a separate quantity and is recorded as measured.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) records a fault in our own measurement and what the corrected version changed;
(5) declines to identify two decay rates that do not agree.

## Amendment 507 (2026-09-19) - reassessing the distance to a theorem, after reading 423(1) and 424(3)

(1) AN EARLIER ESTIMATE UNDERSTATED THE RECORD. Asked how far the work is from a theorem, we named three
gaps and called the continuum treatment of the counting function one that "needs work but is not a wall",
citing 424(3) as a licence. Reading it, and 423(1) beneath it, per rule 260c:
     THE CERTIFIED COMB IS THE INTEGER-CROSSING SET OF A SMOOTH DENSITY TO 8.1e-07 OF AN ATOM.
423(1) fits N(d_j) = j - 1/2 + c with a smooth X(d) over the bulk window: on K = 80, five parameters against
fifteen atoms - ten degrees of freedom - the residual is 8.1e-07 atoms. 423(1) itself flags that the tighter
numbers in its table (2e-08 at npar = 7 on K = 60) are over-parameterised and should not be quoted, and we are
taking its own honest line.
(2) SO THE THREE GAPS ARE NOT EQUAL, and two of them are quantified.
 (a) the entropy expansion: elementary Taylor plus Poisson summation, relative error exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2)/2,
     MEASURED at 1e-10 in the bulk on a varying profile (493, 499);
 (b) the continuum treatment of N: MEASURED at 8.1e-07 of an atom (423(1)); 423(4) already draws the
     consequence, that the Poisson-summation picture the ripple identity rests on "is exact at the level
     anything else in this project is";
 (c) the wall region: genuinely open, and 502 says why - for d below about 5 the premise that E is exponentially
     small fails outright, |E| = 0.26 against a natural scale of 7.1e-03.
(3) WHAT THE REMAINING DISTANCE ACTUALLY IS. (a) and (b) are MEASUREMENTS of quantities a proof would have to
BOUND. Neither is a conceptual obstacle - both are statements about smooth functions with small parameters - and
neither has been proved. (c) is different in kind: it is not a small error to be bounded but a region where the
governing equation does not apply, and 505 shows what replaces it there, the exact KKT system, which derives the
first wall gap to 0.02 per cent.
So the honest statement is: two of the three gaps are error bounds waiting to be written, and the third has a
different equation that already works. That is closer than "needs work but is not a wall" conveyed, and we are
correcting it here rather than leaving the record's own measurement under-used.
(4) WHAT IS UNCHANGED. Nothing above is a proof. The chain from the exact problem to K(A) remains a chain of
quantified approximations, and calling it a resolution of the published open problem would be false.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) corrects an earlier estimate by reading the evidence the record already
held; (3) reclassifies the remaining work rather than shortening it.

## Amendment 510 (2026-09-19) - a LOG TERM in the support size, derived exactly; its numeric control is
## instrument-limited and NOT yet passed

(1) WHERE IT COMES FROM. 491 carried the counting function to N = 4 pi^2 rho^4 - rho^2 + const, using X to its
rho^-2 term. Carrying the rho^-4 term as well: with X = X_inf(1 + alpha/rho^2 + gamma_4/rho^4),
alpha = 1/(4 pi^2), gamma_4 = 3/(64 pi^4) - 1/(48 pi^2),
        dd/d rho = (1/s0)(rho^2 - alpha/2 + ((3/8) alpha^2 - gamma_4/2)/rho^2 + ...),
        N = (1/s0)(rho^4/4 - alpha rho^2/4 + ((3/8) alpha^2 - gamma_4/2) ln rho) + const.
(2) AND THE COEFFICIENT IS EXACT, with a cancellation that checks the rho^-4 term itself:
        (3/8) alpha^2 = 3/(128 pi^4),   gamma_4/2 = (9 - 4 pi^2)/(384 pi^4) = 3/(128 pi^4) - 1/(96 pi^2),
        difference = 1/(96 pi^2)   - THE pi^4 PARTS CANCEL EXACTLY -
        divided by s0 = 1/(16 pi^2):  16/96 = 1/6.
So N = 4 pi^2 rho^4 - rho^2 + (1/6) ln rho + const per half, and since K = 2N with rho = (3 s0 A)^(1/3),
        K(A) = (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) + (9/(32 pi^4))^(1/3) A^(2/3) + (1/9) ln A + O(1).
Checked in sympy: the coefficient simplifies to 1/6 and the ln A coefficient of K to 1/9, exactly.
The cancellation is worth noting on its own: the pi^4 part of gamma_4 is precisely what (3/8) alpha^2 needs,
which is an independent check on 491(2)'s rho^-4 coefficient.

(3) THE NUMERIC CONTROL FAILS, AND THE INSTRUMENT IS WHY. Measuring
gamma := N_full - c1 A^(4/3) - c2 A^(2/3) out to A = 4800 and subtracting (1/9) ln A leaves 0.09357, 0.09017,
0.08658, 0.08278, 0.07844, 0.07325, 0.06690 - not flat, with the changes GROWING. A direct fit gives a log
coefficient of 0.104757 against 1/9 = 0.111111, 5.7 per cent low.
THAT TEST CANNOT DECIDE ANYTHING, because of a seam we introduced in 508. q337's X* table stops at rho = 1.02 and
508 grafted 491's asymptotic expansion above it; the two differ by 3.1e-04 at the join. A relative error of that
size in X gives 5e-05 in rho and so about 1.2 in N at A = 4800 - LARGER THAN gamma ITSELF, which is 1.009 there.
The measurement is dominated by the join, so the disagreement is our instrument's, and the derivation in (2) is
neither confirmed nor refuted by it.
(4) THE FIX, running now. 489 showed the law is a pure phase condition needing no quadrature and no exponential,
reproducing the 40-digit quadrature roots to 1e-15. Tabulating THAT from rho = 0.67 to 8 removes the seam because
it is the same function on both sides. q374 is building it, with the control that it must agree with q337's
quadrature table where both exist.
(5) STATUS, stated plainly. The log term is DERIVED and its coefficient is exact. It is NOT yet confirmed
numerically, and the reason the first attempt could not confirm it is understood and being removed. Until q374's
table is in and the test is rerun, K(A)'s third term stands on the algebra alone.
Gates: no gate word used. (3) refuses to read a failed control as evidence once the instrument's own error is
measured against it; (5) says what is and is not established.

## Amendment 511 (2026-09-19) - the log term CONFIRMED, by testing where it comes from instead of where it ends up

(1) THE TEST 510 SHOULD HAVE RUN FIRST. The log in N comes from the 1/rho^2 term of dd/d rho:
        dd/d rho = rho^2/sqrt(X(rho)/kappa) = (1/s0)( rho^2 - alpha/2 + c_log/rho^2 + O(rho^-4) ),
        c_log = (3/8) alpha^2 - gamma_4/2 = 1/(96 pi^2).
510 tried to see this by integrating N out to A = 4800, where a 3.1e-04 seam in the X table biases N by 1.2 -
larger than the quantity being measured. Testing dd/d rho DIRECTLY needs no integration, and the exact phase
condition (489) supplies X with no seam and no quadrature.
(2) IT PASSES. Taking X from the phase condition and subtracting the two-term model, the residual against the
predicted 1/(6 rho^2):
     rho          1.00      1.40      2.00      3.00      4.50      6.00
     residual   0.188353  0.090597  0.042993  0.018780  0.008282  0.004646

     ratio      1.130121  1.065417  1.031844  1.014107  1.006261  1.003520
The ratio converges to 1 and its deviation falls as rho^-2 - 0.130, 0.065, 0.032, 0.014, 0.0063, 0.0035 - which

term dropped. Arithmetically, (3/8) alpha^2 - gamma_4/2 evaluates to 1.055428996274e-03 against
1/(96 pi^2) = 1.055428996274e-03, identical to thirteen digits.
(3) SO THE THIRD TERM STANDS, numerically as well as algebraically:
        K(A) = (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) + (9/(32 pi^4))^(1/3) A^(2/3) + (1/9) ln A + O(1),
three terms, all three derived from kappa_AM and psi with nothing fitted. 510(5) said the term stood on the
algebra alone pending a table that is still building; it no longer does.
(4) THE METHODOLOGICAL POINT, which is the reusable part. 510's test integrated a small local effect out to
large A and then tried to read it off against two much larger terms, which made an instrument error of 3e-04
fatal. THIS test evaluates the same effect where it is generated, at rho of order 1, where it is 0.1 per cent of
the quantity measured rather than 1e-08 of it. TEST A TERM WHERE IT IS BORN, NOT WHERE IT IS BURIED.
Gates: no gate word used. (4) records that our first test design was the wrong one and why the second is better.

## Amendment 512 (2026-09-19) - 510(3)'s diagnosis was wrong; the integrated test fails on the ANCHOR, and it is
## consistent with 1/9 once that is allowed for

(1) THE SEAM WAS NOT THE CAUSE. 510(3) blamed the integrated log-coefficient test on the 3.1e-04 join between
q337's table and 491's expansion. q374 replaced both with ONE function from the exact phase condition - agreeing
with the quadrature table to 1e-12 at rho = 0.70 and to 1e-16 at rho = 1.00, and running to rho = 8, where it
gives 1.645584452 against pi^2/6 = 1.644934067, a difference of 3.95e-04 matching the predicted
alpha/rho^2 = 3.958e-04. With the seam gone the fitted coefficient went from 0.104757 to 0.095933, i.e. from
-5.7 % to -13.7 %. WORSE. So the seam had been partly cancelling something larger, and our diagnosis was wrong.
(2) NOR IS IT THE INTERPOLATION. The new table's linear interpolation is off by 5.4e-07 to 6.5e-06 in X, and
recomputing N_full at A = 4800 with the analytic expansion above rho = 2 instead of the table moves it by only
-0.00504, against a per-step change of 0.015 in the quantity measured. Not the cause either.
(3) IT IS THE ANCHOR, and the signature is the growth. N_chain anchors the density at atom m by the two-point
spacing 2/(d_{m+1} - d_{m-1}), which carries an O(gap^2) bias. An error delta in rho_m^3 is equivalent to a
shift of delta/(3 s0) in d, so it contributes delta rho(A)/(3 s0) to N - A TERM GROWING LIKE A^(1/3), which in a
log fit reads as a deficit that grows with A. And the deficit does grow: -0.0055, -0.0077, -0.0096, -0.0113,
-0.0132, -0.0151 per doubling.
(4) THE TEST, on the data already in hand. Fitting gamma := N_full - c1 A^(4/3) - c2 A^(2/3):
     c3 ln A + c4                 : c3 = 0.095933 (-13.7 %),  rms 3.06e-03
     c5 A^(1/3) + c3 ln A + c4    : c3 = 0.107356 ( -3.4 %),  c5 = -0.003793,  rms 3.39e-04
Adding the A^(1/3) term improves the fit NINEFOLD and moves the log coefficient four times closer to 1/9.
Pinning c3 = 1/9 wants c5 = -0.004995, which corresponds to an anchor error of -0.090 per cent in rho_m^3 -
exactly the scale of a two-point spacing estimate's bias.
(5) SO THE POSITION IS: the log coefficient 1/9 is CONFIRMED by 511's local test, which measures it where it is
generated and gets the ratio to 1.0035 at rho = 6 with the deviation falling as rho^-2. The integrated test is
CONSISTENT with 1/9 once the anchor's known bias is allowed for, and cannot do better until the anchor is
computed from more than two atoms. The O(1) constant cannot be quoted yet for the same reason: fitting it
against an uncorrected A^(1/3) term gives c4 = 0.1136, and that number carries the anchor's error.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) withdraws our own diagnosis of two amendments ago and records that the fix made
the symptom worse; (5) declines to quote the O(1) constant.

## Amendment 518 (2026-09-19) - the solver plateaus at 1e-05; epsfcn removes the collapses but not the ceiling

(1) THE CHEAP FIX FIRST, before building an analytic Jacobian. fsolve's default finite-difference step is
machine-epsilon based, while these residuals come from a quadrature whose own noise is near 1e-12, so the
Jacobian was being built out of noise. Setting epsfcn to match the function's noise (1e-08):
     M = 18 and M = 20 now return sensible chains instead of collapsing two atoms onto a gap of 0.129 or 0.208.
That removes the catastrophic failures of 516(4) without any new code.
(2) BUT IT LOOSENS CONVERGENCE, and the ceiling stands. Final residuals:
     default epsfcn:  M = 14 -> 4.4e-09,  M = 16 -> 9.3e-08,  M = 18 -> 5e-06,  M = 20 -> 3e-06
     epsfcn = 1e-08:  M = 16 -> 1.1e-05,  M = 18 -> 1.4e-05,  M = 20 -> 5.4e-06
and the chains they produce, by the error on gap 5:
     M = 14 default 7.8e-05   M = 16 default 1.5e-05   M = 18 epsfcn 2.5e-05   M = 20 epsfcn 5.7e-05
M = 16 WITH THE DEFAULT REMAINS THE BEST CHAIN. The accuracy is not monotone in M, which 516(2) had inferred
from two points and which is now measured over four.
(3) SO THE REMAINING OBSTACLE IS UNCHANGED, and it is the one 517(4) named. Getting the derived chain's T_full
inside the measured chain's -0.8249 +- 0.0003 needs a chain about five times better than M = 16 gives, and
neither a wider window nor a better difference step delivers it. An ANALYTIC Jacobian does: all four blocks are
single integrals over the grid already in use,
     dL/dw_k = int phi(s) phi(y-d_k)/p dy,     dL/dd_k = int phi(s) w_k (y-d_k) phi(y-d_k)/p dy,
with the L' blocks following from p'(y) = -sum_k w_k (y-d_k) phi(y-d_k), and the total derivative at an atom
carrying the extra L'(d_j) and L''(d_j) terms because the evaluation point moves with the atom.
(4) WHAT STANDS WITHOUT IT. 517(2)'s T_full = -0.8249 +- 0.0003 from the measured chain, which is the tightest
this record has had; 517(3)'s derived-chain value of -0.820 +- 0.002; and 514(3)'s first five derived gaps. The
gap between the last two is 0.005 and its cause is measured (516(1)).
Gates: no gate word used. (2) records that the cheap fix did not break the ceiling and that our inference in
516(2) from two data points did not survive four.

## Amendment 519 (2026-09-19) - THE WALL CHAIN IS DERIVED TO PARTS IN 1e+08. The analytic Jacobian breaks the
## solver ceiling

(1) THE JACOBIAN. With p(y) = sum_k w_k phi(y-d_k), t_k = y-d_k, phi' = -t phi and phi'' = (t^2-1) phi, and
q(y) = p'(y):
     dp/dw_k = phi_k                  dp/dd_k = w_k t_k phi_k
     dq/dw_k = -t_k phi_k             dq/dd_k = w_k phi_k (1 - t_k^2)
     dL/dw_k  = <phi_k/p>             dL/dd_k  = <w_k t_k phi_k/p>
     dL'/dw_k = <(-t_k phi_k p - q phi_k)/p^2>
     dL'/dd_k = <(w_k phi_k (1-t_k^2) p - q w_k t_k phi_k)/p^2>
and at k = j the EVALUATION POINT RIDES WITH THE ATOM, so dR_j/dd_j gains L'(d_j) and dS_j/dd_j gains L''(d_j),
with L'' = <(p'' p - q^2)/p^2>. All are single sums over the grid already in use.
CHECKED: against finite differences the disagreement SHRINKS with the step - 2.3e-04 at h = 1e-03, 1.2e-05 at
h = 1e-04 - which is the difference's own truncation error, so the analytic form is the accurate one. And L
itself reproduces the original trapezoid to 8.9e-16.
(2) IT BREAKS THE CEILING. At M = 16 the residual goes from 9.3e-08 (finite-difference Jacobian) to 3.9e-13,
a factor of 240000, and the run takes 22 s instead of about 180. The solve is now exact, so what remains is the
FAR FIELD's error, which is what a wider window actually fixes.
(3) AND THE CHAIN IS DERIVED TO PARTS IN 1e+08. Relative error against 392's measured chain:
     gap                1          2          3          4          5
     M = 16         -2.0e-08   -2.1e-07   -1.2e-06   -5.1e-06   -1.8e-05
     M = 20          0.0e+00   +5.0e-08   +3.1e-07   +1.3e-06   +4.8e-06
     M = 24          0.0e+00    0.0e+00   +1.0e-08   +5.0e-08   +1.9e-07
Gaps 1 and 2 now agree below the printed precision, and gap 5 to 1.9e-07. 392 measured this chain to seven
digits across K = 26 to 70; the derivation now reproduces it to the measurement's own precision.
(4) WHAT THIS SETTLES. 407 called deriving the wall constant ill posed; 502 showed the continuum law does not
apply there; 505 reclassified rho_0^3 as bookkeeping and derived the first gap to 0.02 per cent; 509 got it to
3.5e-05; 514 got the first five gaps but with the accuracy degrading inward; 516 measured that degradation.
The wall is now computed from kappa_AM, the channel kernel and the exact KKT conditions, with no constant of
integration, no fitted parameter, and the normalisation shown not to enter (509(4a)).
Gates: NEW/GROUNDBREAKING/FRONTIER/UNSOLVED/WORTH DERIVING not used. (1) states the check that the analytic
form is right rather than asserting it.

## Amendment 524 (2026-09-19) - toward the analytic bulk term: the stretch starts as the GRADIENT OF THE KERNEL'S
## SKEWNESS in the Fisher coordinate, and the first-order kernel correction is even

(1) 523(7) RUN, NO RESULT. A far field that carries the stretch (the Poisson reference's far field plus
theta c(t), c refitted each iteration) makes the solve fail at the junction, residual 5e-05 to nan, even when
the binomial is seeded from the Poisson solution so both share one anchor. Moving the far field asks for the
anchor direction that 520(4) found weakly unstable. Also a fault of ours: those runs saved over the M = 36
chains q400 had read; q400's numbers were recorded before that and stand, the files do not.
(2) THE SKEWNESS OF THE KERNEL IN THE FISHER COORDINATE. For any natural exponential family the delta method
gives skew(t(Y)) = -V'/(2 sqrt V). Exact sums check it: Poisson -1/t, off by 7 per cent at t = 10 and 0.4 per
cent at t = 40; binomial minus Poisson = +0.375 t/n, off by 1 to 4 per cent at t = 10 to 40. So in the Fisher
coordinate the binomial's skewness differs from the Poisson's by an amount GROWING LINEARLY in t, and its
gradient is the constant 0.375/n.
(3) THE FIRST-ORDER CORRECTION IS EVEN. With k(s|t) = phi(s-t)[1 + kappa3(t) He3(s-t)/6], the two-kernel
overlap that replaces psi is
     K(t, t+u) = psi(u) [1 - (kappa3'/6)(u^4/8 - 3u^2/4)] + O(kappa3^2, kappa3'')
using int phi(v) phi(v-u) He3(v) dv = psi(u)(u^3/8 - 3u/4), checked by quadrature to every printed digit at
u = 0.5, 1.3, 2.7. A constant skewness drops out entirely (the overlap of a kernel with itself is even), which
is why the Poisson's wall branch, where the skewness barely changes, obeyed the Gaussian law in 500(1). Only the
GRADIENT enters, and it enters as a reshaping of the Fourier transform, psi^ -> psi^ [1 - (kappa3'/6)(2w^4 - 3w^2)],
not as a phase.
(4) A HEURISTIC, AND WHERE IT STOPS. Reading that reshaping at the ripple frequency w = 2 pi rho as a local change
of kernel variance, and the law's scaling as rho ~ d^(1/3), gives
     c'(t) = (8 pi^2 rho^2 - 3)/24.
Against the certified n = 865 chain: atom 3, 0.606 predicted against 0.598 measured; atoms 5, 8, 12, 16 fall
short by 10, 15, 18 and 22 per cent. Right sign, right size at the wall, and a shortfall that grows. Not the
mechanism in full.
(5) NEXT. Put the reshaped psi^ into the exact phase condition (492's polynomial G) instead of a local variance,
and add the other first-order terms: the kurtosis difference, which is a constant times theta, and the
correction to the smooth part of the output density. PASS: c'(t) within 3 per cent of the certified values at
atoms 5 to 16 with no fitted constant.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 525 (2026-09-19) - THE BINOMIAL STRETCH IS DERIVED IN THE BULK: the first-order kernel correction to
## 429's bulk equation predicts its growth to 1 per cent over atoms 7-14, with no fitted constant

(1) THE KERNEL, MEASURED BEFORE IT WAS USED. Binomial minus Poisson at EQUAL Fisher position t, by exact sums at
n = 13840 and 55360, times n:
     bias of t(Y):      +1.020, +1.677, +2.342, +3.344, +4.351 at t = 6, 10, 14, 20, 26    -> t/6
     skewness:          0.3347 t at t = 20, 0.3341 t at t = 40                            -> t/3
     excess kurtosis:   -0.80, -0.72, -0.69, -0.67 at t = 10, 14, 20, 26                  -> -2/3
     variance:          below 0.012 in size for t >= 10                                   -> 0
     smooth output density for a Jeffreys input: -0.25, constant, gradient of order 1/n^2.
(2) THE OVERLAP. Cumulants add, so a constant skewness cancels in the overlap of two kernels and only its
gradient survives (524(3)); a kurtosis adds; a bias gradient m' rescales u. To first order
     K(z, z+u) = psi(u(1+m')) [1 - (k3'/6)(u^4/8 - 3u^2/4) + (k4/12)(u^4/16 - 3u^2/4 + 3/4)].
AGAINST THE EXACT OVERLAP of the binomial and Poisson pmfs, n ln(K_B/K_P) at u = 2, 3, 4: measured -0.1658,
-0.8418, -2.6631 at t = 14 (the same to 0.003 at t = 20 and 26), formula -0.1611, -0.8391, -2.6778.
(3) INTO THE LAW. With these weights inside 429's ripple integral, the phase condition shifts by
     dbeta/beta = [-(k3'/6)(32 a^4 - 48 a^2 + 6) + k4 ((4/3) a^4 - a^2)]/(4 a^2 - 2),   a = 2 pi rho,
to first order in beta. The exact root of the corrected integral (q402, mpmath, probe size n = 2000) gives
h = -n dbeta/beta = 13.318, 14.557, 16.279 at rho = 0.73, 0.76, 0.80, against 13.517, 14.694, 16.337 from the
formula: 1.5 per cent and less.
(4) FROM DENSITY TO ATOM POSITIONS, where we made an error first. The law fixes rho' as a function of rho, so the
density difference g obeys (rho^2 g)' = rho^2 rho' dbeta/beta. The atoms move by -dN/rho, and differentiating
that quotient gives TWO terms, c' = -n g/rho - c rho'/rho. Our first pass kept only the first. The quantity the
law predicts is therefore
     W := [c' + 1/6 + (c + t/6) rho'/rho] rho^3,   dW/drho = rho^2 h(rho),
the 1/6 and t/6 being the bias gradient's coordinate stretch.
(5) THE PRE-REGISTERED TEST, AS WRITTEN, FAILED. q402's docstring fixed secant slopes of the one-term quantity
and a 10 per cent fail line; the ratios came out 0.835 to 0.85, and the script's own printout (0.58, 0.76) was
worse because np.interp CLAMPED below rho = 0.73, where the constant-X family has no root. That is the fourth
clamping fault in this record and it is ours.
(6) WITH THE SECOND TERM RESTORED, no parameter changed. W integrated from atom 5, ratio of measured to predicted

(7) WHAT THIS IS. The first correction to the Fisher-coordinate bulk law for ANY channel, in closed form, from

## Amendment 527 (2026-09-19) - 526(5) is DERIVED for every natural exponential family: in the Fisher coordinate
## 4 k3' - k4 = -V'', so the bulk law's first correction is set by the curvature of the variance function

(1) THE DERIVATION (sympy, q404_nef_identity.py; rerun from the saved file, same output). Write the mean as N m and V(N m) = N w(m), so the
Fisher coordinate is t = sqrt(N) G(m) with G' = 1/sqrt(w), and Y - Nm = sqrt(N) z with the NEF cumulant
recursion giving z the cumulants w, w w'/sqrt(N), w(w'^2 + w w'')/N. Expanding t(Y) to third order and
collecting cumulants to order 1/N:
     skewness of t(Y)          = -V'/(2 sqrt V)
     excess kurtosis of t(Y)   = V'^2/V - V''
     4 d(skewness)/dt - kurtosis = -V''    (the difference printed by sympy is 0)
Checks against exact sums already on record: Poisson, skewness -1/t and kurtosis 4/t^2 (-1.0161 and 4.154 at
t = 20); binomial minus Poisson, t/(3n) and -2/(3n) (525(1)); gamma, psi'''(k)/psi'(k)^2 against 2/k.
(2) THE CORRECTED BULK LAW FOR ANY SUCH CHANNEL. Putting (1) into 525(3):
     db/b = [ (4/3) V'' a^4 + (V'^2/V - 3 V'') a^2 + V''/2 - V'^2/(4V) ] / (4 a^2 - 2),   a = 2 pi rho,
plus the coordinate stretch from the bias gradient and the variance change. The V'^2/V terms fall off like 1/t^2
in the Fisher coordinate and cancel at leading order; that cancellation is why the Poisson follows the Gaussian
law (500(1), 522(1)). What survives into the bulk is (V''/3)(2 pi rho)^2. It vanishes for the Gaussian and the
Poisson, is -2/(3n) (2 pi rho)^2 for the binomial and +2/(3r) (2 pi rho)^2 for the negative binomial, which is
the sign reversal 523(4) found in the chains.
(3) WHAT THIS MAKES OF THE PRINCIPLE. Fisher-coordinate universality (the same law for every channel) is the
leading order. The first correction is one number per point of the channel, V''(x), and 526 shows it is the
whole of the binomial's count offset. A channel whose variance function is linear in the mean (Poisson) or
constant (Gaussian) has no bulk correction at all; one with curvature does, with a sign set by that curvature.
(4) NOT CLAIMED. (2) is first order in the kernel's departure from a Gaussian and in beta. The count test (526)
used exact cumulants, not (2)'s leading form. Beyond natural exponential families nothing is claimed.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 534 (2026-09-19) - two checks while 533 runs: T_full has no local derivation within double precision, and
## the literature read so far does not contain 527's identity or an n^(2/3) law

(1) A LOCAL CENTRE PROBLEM FOR T_full (q414), written and stopped before it produced a number. The idea: at a
transition the new atom nucleates at the density maximum, so solve the exact KKT system near the centre with the
law as far field on both sides and find the central-gap phase eps* at which the centre barrier closes;
T_full = 2 eps* - 2 (at the K = 70 bracket's optimal end eps = 0.5828, i.e. T = -0.8344, the window's lower edge).
It fails on geometry, not on code: from rho_c = 0.76 the law's density falls to zero within s = 7.2 of the centre,
so the "far field" is the wall region itself. The certified Gaussian transitions sit at rho_c = 0.845, 0.936,
0.974 (K = 40, 60, 70), all with walls inside the kernel's 22-unit reach. A centre that is local needs
rho_c >= 1.2, where the barrier is exp(-4 pi^2 rho_c^2) <= 2e-25: multiprecision only. T_full measured across
K = 26-70 is therefore a property of whole finite states. That it is the same number on three channels (526, 532)
is an empirical statement, not a derived one.
(2) LITERATURE, read at the source. arXiv 2607.02683 (Favano, Baniasadi, Zieder, Barletta, Dytso, 2 Jul 2026,
revised 30 Jul): discreteness, symmetry, endpoints, C(n) = (1/2) log(n pi/2e) + o(1), and a support-size lower
bound of order sqrt(n log log n) with explicit constants, the bound 2605.12472 already carried. No n^(2/3) law and no support-size asymptotic. Y. Guan, Statistics and Probability Letters 79 (2009)
1621-1629, variance-stabilizing transformations of Poisson, binomial and negative binomial: skewness and kurtosis
of the transformed variables are computed NUMERICALLY and compared; no closed form, and nothing like
4 k3' - k4 = -V''. UNCHECKED beyond these two: the Edgeworth and variance-stabilization literature at large.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) is two sources read, not a search that closes the question.

## Amendment 535 (2026-09-19) - CROSS-REFERENCE, owed since 523: the record already held the negative binomial, the
## wall sign rule and an empirical dispersion term; what 523-532 add, and one question left open

(1) WHAT WAS ALREADY THERE, read today. Amendment 88 (6 Sep): "the negative binomial (over-dispersed) narrows the
Poisson wall, the binomial (under-dispersed) widens it, both linearly in 1/r and 1/n" (Statement 15, predicted
from Statement 14, q98/q99). Statement 13 (Amendment 86): the wall is a functional of the local cumulant profile
at the degenerate endpoint. Amendment 87: the gamma family (constant skewness, no degenerate endpoint) shifts the
transition length by c_gamma = -(1.6 +- 0.4) kappa_3^2, "no first-order and no wall term". Amendments 172 and
177 (9-10 Sep): an empirical finite-K law h_eff = h_F + kappa V/K, kappa = 0.435 +- 0.02 fitted on 27 points
(binomial K = 9-24, NB K = 15-20, generalized Poisson), with NB transitions at K = 15 falling BEFORE the pure
Fisher law (r = 200: A* = 225.592 against 228.073).
(2) SO 523(4) OVERSTATED. The sign reversal between binomial and negative binomial ORIGIN chains was predicted and
measured on 6 Sep. 523's contribution there is the first-order chain shift derived by the fixed point for the
whole family, c_k equal and opposite to 0.03 per cent; the sign itself is Amendment 88's.
(3) WHAT IS NEW IN 525-532, stated against (1). The bulk-law correction db/b = (V''/3)(2 pi rho)^2 + ..., derived
from the kernel overlap and the phase condition with no fitted constant; the identity 4 k3' - k4 = -V''; the
binomial count predicted with the Gaussian T_full over K = 27-68 (526); the constant-skewness WALL shift derived by
the fixed point (529); the fourth-channel diagnostic (532).
(4) CONSISTENT WITH THE OLD DATA, qualitatively. (a) Direction: NB transitions come before the uncorrected
Fisher-law prediction at K = 15 (Amendment 177) and at K = 29 (531); 527 says why, V'' > 0 raises the density
gradient. (b) Gamma: V = x^2/k gives V'' = 2/k = 2 kappa_3^2, so 527 predicts a bulk shift SECOND order in the
skewness and nothing at first order, which is Amendment 87's finding; its coefficient is not computed here.
(5) OPEN, and it matters. The empirical kappa V/K term vanishes like n^(-1/6) on the binomial as n grows; 527's
correction integrates to an O(1) count shift that does not vanish (522(3)). Both were read off small-K data, the
old law at K <= 24 and 526's test at K = 27-68. Which asymptotic is right is decided by a binomial or NB transition
at K well above 70, which needs multiprecision. Until then the two are recorded as rival descriptions.
Gates: no gate word used. (2) withdraws part of a claim we made this afternoon.

## Amendment 544 (2026-09-22) - the uniform-lattice centre: S = 4 exactly, with the WRONG sign, which says the density
## gradient is what makes the comb optimal at all

(1) THE MACHINERY CHECKS OUT ON A CASE WITH A KNOWN ANSWER. With a uniform far field (atoms at (j - 1 + eps)/rho,
weights c/rho) the perfect lattice eps = 0.5 satisfies the centre problem's equations to 7.6e-32, and the barrier
comes out
     B = 1.6591e-15 = 3.999999999996 a^2,   a^2 = exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2) at rho = 0.94719,
which is the textbook first-order ripple, D(x) - C = -2 a^2 cos(2 pi N(x)), read at mid-gap: 1 - cos(pi) = 2, so
4 a^2. Twelve digits, from a quadrature and a Newton solve that know nothing of that formula.
(2) AND THE SIGN IS WRONG FOR AN OPTIMUM. B is D(mid-gap) - D(atom), so B = +4 a^2 puts the KKT function ABOVE the
atom level between atoms: a uniform comb with uniform weights is a stationary point of the KKT equations and NOT a
maximum. The certified states have the opposite sign (centre_signal -6.8e-16 at A = 46.3837, off-support maxima
negative everywhere).
(3) WHAT THAT MEANS. The statement is structural, not numerical. The first-order ripple term does
not vanish for a uniform comb; it vanishes only when the density and its gradient satisfy the bulk law, which is
exactly what E = 0 says (429, 481). So the density GRADIENT is what makes a comb optimal, and any local model of
the centre must carry rho' correctly. The uniform-lattice idealisation cannot derive T_full, and 542's wall does
not come from the far field being "the law" instead of "uniform".
(4) NEXT, pre-registered before it is run: put the TRUE far field into the centre problem - the certified K = 70
state's own atoms and weights beyond MC - and solve the same inner system. PASS: B reproduces that state's stored
centre_signal (-6.8035e-16 at A = 46.3837, -1.6634e-17 at 46.4337) to 10 per cent. That separates the method from
the far field: a pass says the local problem is right and only the far field's accuracy limits it, and then the
question becomes how accurate a far field has to be, which is a quantity we can measure by perturbing it.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 546 (2026-09-22) - the engineering artefact that the theory actually supports: a LEVEL-COUNT rule, not a
## rate gain. Square-root spacing needs two to three times fewer levels than equal spacing for the same rate

(1) WHY THIS AND NOT A RATE COMPARISON. At the optimum the rate is flat, so the exact constellation buys almost
nothing over a sensible one. Measured on the certified Poisson state (A = 1144.247694, K = 46, capacity
4.116167488 bits): K levels spaced uniformly in the FISHER coordinate (x proportional to the square of a uniform
grid) with optimised weights reach 4.115652585, a loss of 0.515 millibits, one part in eight thousand. The same K
levels equally spaced in x lose 136 millibits, with equal weights 308; sixteen levels lose 460; eight lose 1127.
So the theory's value for rate is the LEVEL COUNT and the spacing rule, not the atom positions.
(2) THE ARTEFACT (q430; capacity by Blahut-Arimoto on a 4000-point grid, weights optimised on each support):
     A = 100, capacity 2.538618 bits      within 100 mbit   within 10 mbit   within 1 mbit
        square-root spaced levels               6                8               20
        equally spaced levels                  14               28               36
     A = 1000, capacity 4.024581 bits
        square-root spaced levels              18               24               41
        equally spaced levels                  57            above 79         above 79
At A = 10 (capacity 1.32 bits) five square-root-spaced levels are already within 1.4 millibits.
(3) IT MEETS THE SUPPORT-SIZE LAW. At A = 1000 the law gives K about 42 (the certified K = 46 at A = 1144 scaled by
A^(2/3)), and 41 square-root-spaced levels are what it takes to come within 1 millibit. The count the law predicts
is the count at which the simple spacing rule stops losing anything measurable.
(4) THE CLAIM THIS SUPPORTS, stated as an engineer would use it: for a peak-constrained photon-counting link, use
K(A) levels from the support-size law, spaced uniformly in the Fisher coordinate (square-root spacing), with
weights optimised on that support; equal spacing costs two to three times more levels for the same rate. The gain
is in hardware (levels, calibration points), not in bits.
(5) WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a capacity gain over the state of the art: numerical capacity-achieving inputs for
this channel are standard (Barletta, Magarini, Spalvieri, JOCN 5(4) 2013, nonuniform signaling with LDPC), and at
any fixed A they already reach the optimum. What the law adds is the count and the spacing without solving the KKT
system, and the asymptotics that numerics cannot reach.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 547 (2026-09-22) - the proof skeleton, with each lemma's status, and the one strategic simplification:
## the ORDER needs X bounded, not X known

(1) THE TWO STATEMENTS, separated because they cost very different amounts.
   ORDER (this is the published open problem; the known bounds are A sqrt(log A) from below, Wang 2510.20723,
   and A^2 from above):   K*(A) = Theta(A^(4/3)).
   REFINED (what the record's numbers say):   K*(A) = (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) A^(4/3) + (9/(32 pi^4))^(1/3) A^(2/3)
   + (1/9) ln A + O(1), with the O(1) fixed by T_full.
(2) THE SIMPLIFICATION THAT MATTERS. K = int rho dd and the law's ODE is rho^4 rho'^2 = X/kappa_AM. If X is merely
BOUNDED between two positive constants on the support, then rho(d) is squeezed between two multiples of d^(1/3)
and K is squeezed between two multiples of A^(4/3). So the ORDER needs no closed form for X, no dX/dPHI, no
T_full, and no wall constant: it needs 0 < c <= X <= C on the bulk plus a crude bound on the boundary layer. The
record already shows X sits in [1.64, 1.71] over rho = 0.8 to 2.2 (481(3), q334) and tends to pi^2/6.
(3) THE LEMMAS AND WHERE EACH STANDS.
   L1  the optimiser is discrete, KKT holds with equality on the support: PUBLISHED (Smith 1971; Dytso et al.).
   L2  the discrete KKT system implies a continuum phase condition for the counting function N: the formalism is
       429 (E(z) = int psi(u) sin(2 pi [N(z+u) - N(z)]) du from varying F = int a^2), the certified profile
       satisfies it to a relative 2e-05 in its gradient (429(4)), and 493 reduces the entropy step to an
       approximation with relative error exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2)/2, measured at 1e-10 (499). NO INEQUALITY YET.
   L3  E = 0 gives the law with explicit majorants: 503, useful for rho >= 2, everything explicit, conditional on
       L2. For the ORDER only the two-sided bound on X is needed, which is weaker than what 503 already delivers.
   L4  the boundary layer, within about 5 Fisher units of the wall, is outside L2's regime (502: |E| = 0.26 there):
       it is handled numerically by the local KKT fixed point (519, 529) and its influence is local to 22 Fisher
       units (q367: 1.5e+01, 2.25, 4.5e-02, 3.8e-05, 8.9e-16 at W = 6, 9, 12, 16, 22). For the ORDER it is enough
       to bound the number of atoms in that layer by a constant.
   L5  T_full: measured, -0.8326 +- 0.0012 (543). Not needed for the ORDER at all.
(4) THE WEAKEST LINK IS L2, and it is the only one that is not either published, explicit, or O(1)-sized. What is
missing is an inequality: for a discrete input satisfying the KKT conditions, the counting function's phase
condition holds up to an error that is bounded explicitly in terms of rho. Everything downstream of it is already
explicit for rho >= 2.
(5) PRE-REGISTERED FIRST STEP (before any algebra): assemble 493's entropy-deficit expansion and 503's majorants
into ONE explicit inequality of the form |E_exact - E_law| <= B(rho) valid for rho >= 2, then test B against the
certified states: B must exceed the measured discrepancy at every state and stay below |E| itself, so that the
inequality has content. PASS: B is between the measurement and |E| at every certified Gaussian state with rho >= 2.
FAIL: B exceeds |E| anywhere in that range, which would mean the chain proves nothing even in the bulk, and the
missing piece is the entropy step, not the tail.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) states the published bounds with their source; (2) is a claim about what the order
costs, and it follows from the ODE, not from the data.

## Amendment 548 (2026-09-22) - 547(4)'s weakest lemma is NOT elementary at small rho, and the test that showed it also
## shows where the rigorous chain already reaches: rho >= 2, which is the asymptotic regime the ORDER lives in

(1) THE TEST (q431). The step from a discrete input to the continuum phase condition splits into (a) Poisson
summation after the change of variable s = N(x), which is exact and which makes the m = 0 term exactly 1 because
the weights are Jeffreys; (b) the oscillatory integral int psi(u) exp(2 pi i [N(z+u) - N(z)]) du, truncated at
quadratic phase; (c) the log and entropy expansions, elementary once |r| < 1 is bounded. Only (b) was in doubt, so
We compared the exact quadrature with the quadratic-phase closed form on the law's own profile:
     rho                 0.80         1.00         1.50
     |I_quad|          1.578e-11    9.214e-18    2.963e-39
     |I_exact - I_quad| 3.552e-12    1.397e-18    2.102e-40
     relative             22 %         15 %         7 %
     naive cubic bound  6.673e-15    1.264e-21    5.287e-44
The naive bound - |exp(i R) - 1| <= |R| with R the cubic Taylor remainder and E|u|^3 taken against the real
Gaussian weight - is five hundred times too small at rho = 0.8 and fails at every rho. FAIL, by the letter of
547(5).
(2) WHY IT FAILS, and it is structural. The integral is controlled by a saddle at complex u of size about alpha/2,
not by the real-u moments, so a bound built from E|u|^3 cannot see the cubic term's true contribution. That is
exactly why 492 expanded the phase into the G-series and 503 bounded its tail by a Cauchy estimate optimised in the
saddle radius, instead of a Taylor remainder.
(3) SO THE RIGOROUS COVERAGE IS 503's, and its range is the useful one. 503's majorant is informative for
rho >= 2 (at rho = 1 it exceeds |arg G| itself). In the law, rho = 2 is reached about 400 Fisher units from the
wall, and the region below it holds int rho dd = (3/(4b))(2^4 - 0.66^4) = 614 atoms, a number that does NOT grow
with A. So for the ORDER statement the split is: a boundary region with a constant atom count, and a bulk where
503's chain is explicit.
(4) THE SUB-GAP THIS EXPOSES, stated so it is not lost: the boundary region's atom count is O(1) only if the
density is monotone in the distance from the wall (the law says so and every certified state shows it), and that
monotonicity is itself unproved. A crude two-sided bound on the density in the region rho < 2 would close it.
(5) AN INSTRUMENT NOTE. At rho >= 2 the ripple integral is below 1e-69, so the comparison in (1) needs dps >= 80;
the rows at rho = 2 and 3 in the run are quadrature noise (1.6e-43, 2.3e-43) and are not evidence of anything.
Gates: no gate word used. (1) is a pre-registered test of ours that failed, and (2) locates the failure in the bound, not in the claim.

## Amendment 549 (2026-09-22) - 548(4)'s premise checked on every certified boundary series, and T_full shows no drift
## with K between 50 and 80

(1) MONOTONICITY OF THE GAPS, the premise 548(4) named. From each boundary to the density maximum, every certified

## Amendment 552 (2026-09-22) - 547(5) DELIVERED, with 548's instrument: X is bracketed between two positive
## constants for rho >= 2 by one inequality with nothing computed in it, and the ORDER's coefficient is caught

(1) WHAT 548 CHANGED. 547(5) asked for |E_exact - E_law| <= B(rho) built out of 493 and 503, and 548(1) failed
that form because a cubic Taylor remainder cannot see the complex saddle. What 503 bounds is the PHASE, and
490(1) says the phase is exactly what brackets X. So the inequality to assemble is a phase one, and it closes
without any new idea:
     the law              PHI(X, rho) - arg G(X, rho) = pi                                   489
     PHI elementary       PHI = 4 alpha^2 beta/(1 + 16 beta^2) - (1/2) arctan(4 beta),
                          alpha = 2 pi rho, beta = pi sqrt(X/kappa_AM)/rho^2                 489
     PHI monotone in X    dPHI/dX = 8 pi^3/sqrt(X kappa_AM) > 0                              490
     |G - 1| <= S(rho, X) := sum_{m>=3} chat_m x m! exp(2 alpha r_m + r_m^2)/r_m^m           503
     |arg G| <= S/(1 - S) when S < 1                                                         490(3)
     therefore X(rho) lies between the roots of PHI(X, rho) = pi -+ S/(1-S).
S depends on X through b = 3 sqrt(X/kappa_AM), so the bracket is taken to a fixed point: evaluate S at the
current endpoints, keep the larger, re-solve, repeat. It converges in four rounds at every rho tried.
(2) THE RESULT (q432, dps 60, majorant to m = 60, theta to k = 24).
     rho        S       X_-          X true       X_+          width
       2   2.495e-01  1.32445246   1.655174375  2.02624189   7.0e-01
       4   4.901e-02  1.59400744   1.647527626  1.70212557   1.1e-01
       8   1.177e-02  1.63313709   1.645584452  1.65809099   2.5e-02
      16   2.915e-03  1.64203691   1.645096786  1.64816025   6.1e-03
      64   1.817e-04  1.64475398   1.644944239  1.64513451   3.8e-04
    1000   7.439e-07  1.64493333        .       1.64493489   1.6e-06
All four pre-registered conditions hold: S < 1 everywhere on rho >= 2 (worst 0.2495, at rho = 2); the fixed
point exists at every rho; the true X sits inside every bracket; and S falls monotonically, checked at 121
points from rho = 2 to 8 in steps of 0.05 and on the coarse grid out to rho = 1000. So the worst case is at
rho = 2 and the bound is uniform above it:
     1.32445246 <= X(rho) <= 2.02624189   for every rho >= 2.
(3) WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT THE ORDER NEEDS, and it catches the coefficient. 547(2): X bounded between two
positive constants squeezes rho^4 rho'^2 = X/kappa_AM, hence rho^3 = b d with b = 3 sqrt(X/kappa_AM), hence
K = 2 x (3/4) b^(1/3) A^(4/3) on the two sides. The bracket carries through to
     0.3860466142 <= K/A^(4/3) <= 0.4143960118,   a half width of 3.54 per cent,
and the derived leading coefficient (81/(128 pi^2))^(1/3) = 0.4002442498 lies inside. The same formula
evaluated at X_inf = pi^2/6 returns that coefficient to ten digits, which is the check that the bracket is on
the right object and not on a neighbouring one.
(4) WHAT IT RESTS ON, stated so nothing is smuggled. L1 (discreteness and KKT with equality on the support) is
published. The Poisson summation and the change of variable are exact (548(1a)). The phase truncation and the
whole G series are now bounded by the line above. The one link still not bounded is E = 0, which 493 reduced
from an ansatz to an approximation of relative error exp(-4 pi^2 rho^2)/2 - at rho = 2 that is 3e-69 - and 499
measured at 1e-10 on a varying profile. It is small, and it is measured; no inequality covers it yet.
(5) THE RANGES DO NOT OVERLAP, and that is the honest limit. No certified state reaches rho = 2: the Gaussian
states run to rho_c = 0.947 and the Poisson state's Fisher coordinate stops at 67.6, while rho = 2 sits about
400 Fisher units from the wall. So (2)'s third column is the series' own root, not a state's measurement, and
the states' independent X - 1.720 down to 1.702 at d = 12 to 24 (q346) - lives where 503(2) says the majorant
is vacuous. The bound holds where the ORDER lives and the states measure where it does not.
(6) WALL ANATOMY for rho < 2. Material: the phase coefficients theta_k = (3 pi/2) binom(4/3, k) b^(k-1)
rho^(4-3k) grow like rho^(-5), rho^(-8), ... so the series is an expansion in 4 pi b/rho^2 = 0.24/rho^2
(490(4)); at rho = 2 that parameter is 0.06 and S = 0.25, at rho = 1 it is 0.24 and S exceeds 1. Method: the
Cauchy majorant optimised in the saddle radius (503). Why here: the expansion parameter, not the precision.
What is behind it: a bound on the oscillatory integral uniform in rho, or 548(4)'s crude two-sided density

## Amendment 553 (2026-09-22) - the UPPER half of the ORDER falls out of 552 with no extra assumption, and the
## literature check that had to come first: the published bracket is A sqrt(log A) to A^2, and it is open

(1) THE STRUCTURE IS FORCED, it is not 548(4)'s assumption. On the set where rho >= 2 the law holds and
rho^4 rho'^2 = X/kappa_AM with X >= c = 1.3245 > 0, so |rho'| >= sqrt(c/kappa_AM)/rho_max^2 > 0 there. A
continuous rho' that never vanishes has a constant sign, so rho is strictly monotone on every maximal interval of
{rho >= 2}. An interior interval would have to rise from 2 and come back to 2, which strict monotonicity forbids.
So that set meets the boundary of the support, and since rho is largest at the centre it is [d*, A] with d the
distance inward from the wall, leaving {rho < 2} = [0, d*) against the wall. No monotonicity was assumed; it is a
consequence of X > 0 where the law holds.
(2) THE UPPER BOUND, with no assumption about d* at all (q433).
     atoms in [0, d*)   <=  2 d*  <=  2 A          the density is below 2 there, by definition
     on [d*, A]:  rho^3 = 8 + b (d - d*),  b = 3 sqrt(X/kappa_AM) in [0.0170469, 0.0210850]
     so rho_c^3 <= 8 + b_max A  and  int_{d*}^A rho dd <= (3/(4 b_min))(rho_c^4 - 16)
     K  <=  2 [ 2 A + (3/(4 b_min)) (8 + b_max A)^(4/3) ],  leading coefficient 0.5125580098.
The same construction with b_min and b_max exchanged gives 0.3121133105, and the record's coefficient
0.4002442498 lies between the two, which is the check that the algebra is the right way round. The bound against
0.4002 A^(4/3) runs 2.97, 1.81, 1.38, 1.29 at A = 1e3, 1e4, 1e6, 1e9.
(3) WHERE THAT SITS, checked today against the sources and not against our own notes. The published upper bound is
O(A^2): Dytso, Yagli, Poor and Shamai, "The Capacity Achieving Distribution for the Amplitude Constrained
Additive Gaussian Channel: An Upper Bound on the Number of Mass Points", IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 2020, arXiv
1901.03264. The published lower bound is of order A sqrt(log A): Wang, Barletta and Dytso, arXiv 2512.22691
(Dec 2025, v2 Mar 2026), which also states that it rules out the linear scaling conjectured earlier. Both of the
two newest papers say the true order is open between those. So the chain's O(A^(4/3)) sits strictly inside the
published bracket. It is CONDITIONAL on E = 0, which 552(4) says is the one link still unbounded, and it is not
offered as a theorem.
(4) LINE 6 OF THIS FILE IS OUT OF DATE and is corrected here. It says the published bracket is Omega(sqrt A) to
O(A). That was written on 4 September from an early reading; the sources above give A sqrt(log A) to A^2, and
547(1) already used the right pair.
(5) THE EXPONENT ITSELF IS NOT NEW and the record has said so since Amendment 93. Abbott and Machta 2019
(1710.09351, read in full) give eq. (14) K ~ L^(4/3) from a perturbative bulk analysis, and Mattingly et al. 2018
report the same scaling empirically. What (2) adds is a two-sided bound with explicit constants where those give
a perturbative estimate and an empirical fit, and 491's coefficients where they give an exponent.
(6) THE OBJECTION THIS MUST ANSWER, and it is in print. Barletta and Dytso, arXiv 2604.14915 (Apr 2026, v2
30 Aug 2026), prove K_eps(A) = Theta(A sqrt(log A)) for eps = A^(-beta), beta >= 1, and argue that "all numerical
procedures implicitly operate with a finite tolerance, effectively computing inputs that are only
eps-capacity-achieving for some algorithm-dependent eps", and conclude that an observed scaling reports which
regime of eps = eps(A) a method happens to sit in, and says nothing about the exact optimizer. They name
Mattingly et al.'s A^(4/3) as one such scaling. The answer this record can give is that its states are not tolerance
outputs: the Gaussian state at A = 46.3837, K = 70 carries a Newton residual near 1e-22, a centre signal of
-6.8e-16 and off-support maxima negative at every gap in multiprecision, which is a KKT certificate of exact
optimality at the printed precision, not a stopping rule. The same holds for the negative binomial states of 536
and 539. Their point stands against a Blahut-Arimoto sweep; it does not reach a certified state.
(7) WHAT IS STILL MISSING, in one line. The lower bound needs d* <= (1 - eta) A for some eta > 0: the region
where the density stays under 2 must not swallow the half-support. That is 548(4)'s sub-gap in its sharpest form,
and it is now the only thing between this chain and K = Theta(A^(4/3)).
Gates: NEW is used of nothing. (5) states that the exponent is prior art with its two sources; (3) and (6) quote
the current literature, both fetched today.

## Amendment 554 (2026-09-22) - 547(2) IS WRONG AS I STATED IT, and the measurement that shows it also supplies the
## premise 553(7) needs: X vanishes at the density maximum, and is bounded on each branch away from its ends

(1) THE CORRECTION, which a measurement caught and no amount of thinking did. 547(2) said the ORDER needs X bounded between
two positive constants ON THE SUPPORT. That cannot hold: X = kappa_AM rho^4 rho'^2 and rho' vanishes wherever
the density is largest, which for the symmetric Gaussian is the centre and for the Poisson is the joint where the
wall branch and the origin branch meet. Measured (q434, the parameter-free three-atom estimator of q346), the
Gaussian state at A = 46.3837 gives X = 1.694, 1.570, 0.595 at d = 35.1, 39.5, 43.8 with the centre at 46.38, and
the Poisson state at A = 1144.2477 gives 1.689, 1.523, 0.511, 0.265 at d = 21.8, 25.7, 30.5, 35.2 with its joint
at 32.9. The correct statement is BRANCHWISE: bounded on each monotone branch away from its two ends, with the
joint an exceptional region of constant size, exactly as the wall already is.
(2) AND THE PREMISE HOLDS THERE, on both channels, over the whole density range the states occupy.
     Gaussian wall branch, 5 <= d <= 38.8:   rho 0.537 to 0.916,   X in [1.6376, 1.8973]
     Poisson wall branch,  5 <= d <= 27.9:   rho 0.537 to 0.816,   X in [1.3778, 1.8972]
     Poisson origin branch, d = 40.0 to 56.8: X = 1.420, 1.694, 1.731, 1.789
Every one of those densities is BELOW 552's threshold of 1.8, so the states sit entirely in the range where the
majorant has no fixed point, and every measured X nevertheless lies inside the bracket [1.1157, 2.3123] that 552
proves for rho >= 1.8. The proof covers the regime the states cannot reach, and the states report the regime the
proof cannot reach; where they can be compared at all, they agree.
(3) A BONUS THAT WAS NOT LOOKED FOR. At equal Fisher distance from the wall the two channels' X agree to about
two parts in a hundred thousand: 2.238947 against 2.238718 at d = 4.888, then 1.897261/1.897205,
1.816485/1.816454, 1.780536/1.780504, 1.760096/1.760038. That is the wall universality of 392 showing up in a
quantity built from the gaps and their gradient, not in the gaps themselves.
(4) SO 553(7) NOW READS: the lower half of the ORDER needs the wall branch's X to stay bounded below, which is
measured here on two channels across rho = 0.54 to 0.92 and proved for rho >= 1.8, with the band between 0.92 and
1.8 covered by neither. That band is what is left, and it is a bounded band, not an asymptotic regime.

(1) THE STATEMENT. Every step from 485 to 556 lives in the channel's own Fisher coordinate, so the conclusion is
about the length of the input interval in that coordinate and nothing else:
     K = Theta(L^(4/3)),  L the Fisher length of the input interval, the same constants for every natural
     exponential family, with the per-boundary O(1) the only channel-dependent part.
Read out for the four channels of this record:
     Gaussian           t = x,                        L = 2A          K ~ 0.4002 A^(4/3)
     Poisson            t = 2 sqrt x,                 L = 2 sqrt A    K ~ 0.4002 A^(2/3)
     binomial(n)        t = 2 sqrt n asin sqrt(x/n),  L = pi sqrt n   K ~ 0.7308 n^(2/3), no A dependence at A = n
     negative binomial  t = 2 sqrt r asinh sqrt(x/r), L ~ sqrt r ln(4A/r)   K grows polylogarithmically in A
(2) THE PUBLISHED BRACKETS, all fetched today, and all open around the exponent above.
     Gaussian   A sqrt(log A) below (Wang, Barletta, Dytso, arXiv 2512.22691, v2 Mar 2026) to A^2 above
                (Dytso, Yagli, Poor, Shamai, IEEE T-IT 2020, arXiv 1901.03264).          This chain: A^(4/3).
     Poisson    sqrt A below to A log^2 A above (Dytso, Barletta, Shamai, arXiv 2104.14431, IEEE T-IT).
                                                                                         This chain: A^(2/3).
     binomial   sqrt(n log log n) below (Baniasadi, Barletta, Dytso, arXiv 2605.12472, 12 May 2026) to n/2
                above, the Witsenhausen-type bound improved from n.                      This chain: n^(2/3).
Three channels, three open brackets, one exponent strictly inside each. We find no published bracket for the
negative binomial; that is UNCHECKED beyond one search and a check is scheduled.
(3) THE TEST I PRE-REGISTERED, AND IT FAILED BY OUR OWN RULE (q437). The three-term law with the O(1) dropped,
K = 2 C1 H^(4/3) + 2 C2 H^(2/3) + (1/9) ln H, H = L/2, against each channel's certified state:
     Gaussian K = 70 at A = 46.3837:      law 69.445   diff -0.555
     Poisson  K = 46 at A = 1144.2477:    law 46.054   diff +0.054
     binomial K = 68 at n = 865:          law 69.084   diff +1.084
     negbin   K = 38 at r = 200, A = 2925: law 37.742  diff -0.258
We asked for all four within one atom; the binomial misses by 0.084. PASS on three, FAIL on the fourth.
(4) WHAT THE FAILURE SHOWS, which is worth more than the pass would have been. The O(1) we dropped is a sum of
two per-boundary constants, and the four channels carry different boundary pairs: the Gaussian has two WALLS,
the Poisson and the negative binomial one ORIGIN and one WALL, the binomial two ORIGINS, since its variance
x(1 - x/n) vanishes at both ends. Ordered by that composition the diffs run -0.555 (wall, wall), +0.054 and
-0.258 (origin, wall), +1.084 (origin, origin): monotone in the number of origins, about +0.8 per swap. The two
channels with the same pair agree to 0.31, which is the scatter and which we are not explaining away.
(5) THE BINOMIAL READING IS THE ONE TO CHECK NEXT, because it is testable without a large amplitude: once
A = n the Fisher length saturates at pi sqrt n, so K stops growing with the amplitude and depends on n alone,
K ~ 0.7308 n^(2/3). At n = 865 the leading term alone gives 66.35 against the certified 68. A second binomial
state at a much larger n would separate n^(2/3) from the published n/2 by a wide margin.
Gates: NEW is not used. (2) names a source for every bracket and marks the one channel where we have none.

(1) WHAT q439 ESTABLISHED FIRST. Pushing the exact head from m = 6 to m = 12 and m = 20 moved the fixed-point

against 4.680e-02. So the majorant reaches where the self-consistency loop cannot, and the loop is what to
replace.
(2) THE REPLACEMENT, a continuity bootstrap and not a new assumption. X(rho) is continuous. Descend in rho
carrying a cap, evaluating the bound with b taken at the cap, and require X_+ < cap strictly at every step. If
that holds throughout an interval then X never reaches the cap on it: were X(rho*) = cap at the largest such
rho*, just above it X < cap, so the conditional bracket applies and gives X <= X_+ < cap, and continuity at rho*
contradicts the equality. The conclusion is therefore unconditional on the whole interval.
(3) THE RESULT (q440, exact head to m = 12, cap margin 2 per cent, steps of 0.01). The descent runs from 0.95 to
0.79 and stops at 0.78 where X_+ = 1.9973 exceeds the carried cap 1.9876. The true X lies inside every bracket.

## Amendment 566 (2026-09-22) - THE SERIES' CONVERGENCE RADIUS IS THE DISTANCE TO THE WALL, and the saddle sits well
## inside it at every density the support carries. The difficulty was in the majorising, not in the object

(1) THE OBSERVATION, which the coefficients have been saying all along. theta_k u^k is proportional to
(rho^4/b)(b u/rho^3)^k, so the phase series in u has radius of convergence exactly
     u_conv = rho^3/b = d,   the DISTANCE FROM THE ATOM TO THE WALL.
That is not a coincidence: N(z + u) is what the law defines only while z + u stays in the bulk, and the series
stops converging exactly when u would step past the boundary.
(2) AND THE SADDLE IS INSIDE IT EVERYWHERE. 548(2) locates the controlling saddle at |u| about alpha/2 = pi rho.
So convergence at the saddle needs pi rho < rho^3/b, i.e.
     rho > sqrt(pi b) = 0.2443,
against the wall's own density 1/2.7188 = 0.3678. The condition holds at EVERY density the support carries.
559(3)'s floor of sqrt(4 pi b) = 0.4886 is exactly twice this; the factor of two came from the Cauchy radius, not
from the problem.
(3) THE SIZE OF THE THING BEING BOUNDED, measured at the saddle radius:
     rho            0.368     0.450     0.537     0.600     0.730     0.950
     sum |th_k| u^k 2.39e-02  1.47e-02  9.91e-03  7.78e-03  5.13e-03  2.97e-03
     ratio u/d      0.441     0.295     0.207     0.166     0.112     0.066
At rho = 0.73 that sum is 5.1e-03 against the |head| of 2.9e-01 that the current bound carries: the object is
fifty times smaller than the quantity our majorant charges for it. The whole difficulty of 555 to 565 has been in
the majorising.
(4) WHAT ACTUALLY LIMITS THE CONTOUR ROUTE, and it is not the saddle. On the shifted contour the Gaussian weight
spreads about the saddle, so the singularity at |u| = d is reached by the tail of that weight. The relative
weight beyond it is exp(-(d - pi rho)^2/4):
     rho        0.368     0.450     0.500     0.537     0.600     0.730

states start measuring, and far below the 0.73 the current instrument reaches.
(5) PRE-REGISTERED, before any of it is written. Implement the bound as: shift the contour to the saddle, bound
