## Amendment 656 (2026-09-24 02:56) - AF not reached; the obstruction is local branch freedom (rho^2 rho' = (2k+1)/(16 pi^2)); three LFP transitions
(1) THE AF ATTEMPT (AF_ATTEMPT.md; report read in full). AF is not proved for any gamma < 2. What was proved:
  - Prop N [PROVED]. For every competitor nu the objective splits exactly: I(nu) = C - int V dnu - D(m_nu || m_pi) for
    capacity (the exact form of WBD Lemma 2), and l(nu) = l(pi) - int V dnu - B(nu) with B >= 0 for the NPMLE. The
    second-order part is never negative, so no local perturbation improves the objective however flat V is. Deriving
    AF from "flat V gives an improving perturbation" is therefore impossible.
  - Prop T [PROVED]. It transfers lower bounds on V from any comparison measure nu with duality gap delta_nu. AF would
    follow from comparison families with delta <~ 0.55 c* e^{-2 kappa A^gamma}. The gap is first order in nu's error
    while D and B are second order, so nu must reproduce the optimiser, edge layer included, to about c* e^{-5.7
    A^(2/3)}: roughly 250 digits at A = 1000.
  - Prop H [PROVED, a reformulation]. V'' = E_x Var(X|Y) - 1 (Hatsell-Nolte), with sum_j w_j V''(theta_j) = mmse - 1. AF
    would follow from a lower bound on the curvature at the atoms, which nothing controls.
  We checked the statements of N, T and H against the report's identities. Its numerical checks report residuals of
  1.9e-15 (N) and 5.5e-14 (H), and every inequality holding with margin. We did not re-run them.
(2) THE OBSTRUCTION [HEURISTIC, numerically supported]. The local KKT structure allows higher branches rho^2 rho' =
(2k + 1)/(16 pi^2). In chirped test combs with phase targets pi, 3 pi and 5 pi, every atom is a local maximum of T
(12/12, 15/15, 18/18); the even controls 2 pi and 4 pi give 0/14 and 0/16. Every k < pi rho^2 - 9/16 is locally
allowed. So no window-local argument can bound K below A^2. A proof must be non-local: it must show that the branch
index is k = 0 through the bulk, fixed near the edge and carried inward. This is WALL ANATOMY for the upper bound: the
real-axis route is closed by Prop O (655), and the local route by branch freedom.

## Amendment 657 (2026-09-24 03:23) - a Poisson-channel claim K >= c A^(2/3) (asymptotic, A0 not computed; NOT yet reviewed); the K = 21 certificate file was stale and is regenerated (PASS)
(1) THE POISSON CLAIM (POISLB_ATTEMPT.md, 897 lines; report read in full). For the amplitude-constrained
Poisson channel with dark current 0: for every c < 0.0117 there is A0(c) with K(A) >= c A^(2/3) for A >= A0. In the
Fisher coordinate a = sqrt(A) this is c a^(4/3). The known bound is order sqrt(A) (papers/dytso_2401.05045.txt 10-24,
309-341). The route:
  - Reference output r(y) = e^{-(C+1)} exp(y psi(y+1) - y)/y!, whose divergence from every Poisson law is C + delta0(x)
    with delta0 = e^{-x} - x E1(x). The weighted identity is exact, with the multiplier of the sign of m - r. Jeffreys
    misses by 1/(24y), which the weight makes fatal.
  - Two-sided bounds 0.0636 r <= m <= 8.19 r. The lower bound uses a floating-point chord scan up to y = 3000 and an
    analytic chord bound beyond it.
  - Gamma-type weights chi = (x/A)^(2 sigma) e^{t(A - x)} commute exactly with the Poisson kernel. The position-dependent
    Fourier damping (gap G1) is removed with Weber's integral:
      sum_k p(k|x) p(k|x') = e^{-(x+x')} I0(2 sqrt(x x')) = 2 int e^{-s^2} J0(2s sqrt x) J0(2s sqrt x') s ds,
    which is a Hankel transform with position-independent damping. We checked this identity against Watson's form of
    Weber's second exponential integral (p = 1, a = 2 sqrt x, b = 2 sqrt x'), and numerically at (x, x') = (0.7, 1.3), (5, 9) and
    (20, 24): the series and the integral agree to 15 digits.
  - Absorption gives Lambda0 ~ A^(1/3) = (sqrt A)^(2/3).
  - A direct Lemma C analogue with windows w(x) = P(s1 <= Poisson(tx) <= s2), deconvolved exactly by binomial thinning.
  At the stored A (<= 4000) the chain does not close: delta' is 10 to 260. The report says it wrote the proof once

  - Beta weights commuting exactly with the kernel;

## Amendment 663 (2026-09-24 07:36) - the centre of the NPMLE over event cycles: a sliding comb (numerical); the event-rate route carries the same information as the centre density
(1) THE TEST (q499_centre_collapse.py, ours; reads results_q496_npmle_uniform.json and results_q498_npmle_mpcont.json,
writes nothing). Question from the ideas queue: across event cycles (birth-centre -> split-centre -> birth-centre), does
the centre configuration, in units of the local bulk spacing s (mean gap of atoms 4-8 from the centre), collapse onto one
curve of the cycle phase Phi (0 to 1 with an atom at the centre, 1 to 2 without)? 59 centre events, a = 1.73 to 44.54.
(2) RESULTS (floating point).
  - Half-cycle length x 2 rho_law(a): 0.959 at a ~ 9, 0.975 at 17, 0.985 at 34, 0.986 at 44 (BRANCH 4.3 had
    0.972-0.988).
  - Fraction of a full cycle spent with an atom at the centre: 0.5066 at a ~ 9, 0.5026 at 20, 0.5011 at 40. Births and
    splits become equally spaced.
  - Velocities dx/da of atoms indexed from the edge, rows 0.25 apart: 1.0000 to four digits for every atom except the
    innermost three or four on each side. Those move at 0.87-0.95 (a in [40, 45]). This restates the freezing in depth of
    BRANCH 4.4 in the lab frame.
  - Collapse, x1/s (innermost atom off the centre) by phase bin, cycles in a in [10,22) / [22,34) / [34,45]:
    Phi in [0.75,1): 0.767 / 0.903 / 0.951; Phi in [1.75,2): 0.386 / 0.448 / 0.479. The spread within a bin at
    a >= 34 is 0.005-0.07.
  VERDICT: no collapse at finite a. The centre configuration drifts toward the perfect comb (x1/s -> 1 just before a
  split, -> 1/2 just before a birth). Its deficit decays by about e^(-0.29 a^(2/3)) or a^(-1.7); three bins cannot tell
  these apart. The limit object is a comb whose two halves slide outward at unit speed, with a centre defect that shrinks
  in units of s.
(3) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE UPPER BOUND (the wall, sourced). The event rate is 2 v_c/s_c: the outflow speed at the centre
over the centre spacing. The speed is 1 up to a centre factor 0.87-0.95, so a bound on the event rate is a bound on
s_c from below, i.e. on the atom density at depth A. That is the density bound at the flattest point, which BRANCH 7(2)
and UPPER 4.3 (remark: AF(2/3) is essentially equivalent to rho(d) <~ d^(1/3)) already identify as AF at depth A. The
event-rate reduction (Corollary C') is correct but moves no information. The three candidate readings (normal form,
velocity, cycle symmetry) are closed as routes; they remain as numerical facts about the centre.

## Amendment 664 (2026-09-24 07:38) - PRE-REGISTRATION: the finite-sample NPMLE with uniform data; a resolved-depth law against three alternatives
(1) QUESTION. The population NPMLE for Uniform[-a, a] data has K_pop(a) atoms (0.4002 a^(4/3) law; stored states
results_q496_npmle_uniform.json: K_pop = 4, 10, 23, 31 at a = 5, 10, 20, 25). With n samples, the empirical KKT function
fluctuates by about sqrt(a/(sqrt(pi) n)) (Var of phi(X - t)/m(X) under f0, m ~ f0). The population gap maxima at depth d
are exp(-(2.787 d^(2/3) - 0.88)) (UPPER_ATTEMPT.md 4.4, NPMLE a = 33.5 fit). Structure deeper than the depth d_n where the
two are equal is invisible to the sample. Polyanskiy-Wu prove |supp| <= C0 (xmax - xmin)^2 deterministically and
O(log n) for subgaussian-mixture data (papers/polyanskiy_wu_2008.08244.txt lines 146-156); uniform data are not of that
form, so only the first bound applies.
(2) MODELS (frozen in q500_finite_npmle_predict.py, sha256 be07940324d93c82bc418bd86f488b1e2892617ac7d420d24bd0adc51aeb0b01):
  - M0: K_n = K_pop(a) (no finite-sample effect; no parameter).
  - M1 (resolved depth): d_n from 2.787 d^(2/3) - 0.88 = (1/2) log(sqrt(pi) n/a) - log kappa. If d_n >= a, K_n = K_pop(a);
    otherwise K_n = min(K_pop(a), 2 * 0.2001 d_n^(4/3) + 2 (a - d_n) rho_law(d_n)), rho_law(d) = (3 d/(16 pi^2))^(1/3):
    the edge layers to depth d_n follow the law, and the centre keeps the density of the resolved depth. One parameter
    kappa. Heuristic consequence: for Gaussian-tailed data, a ~ sqrt(2 log n) gives K_n ~ log n, the Polyanskiy-Wu order.
  - M2: K_n = c log n (the Polyanskiy-Wu form). One parameter.
  - M3: K_n = c a sqrt(log n). One parameter.
  With kappa = 1, M1 gives 13.7 / 16.0 / 17.9 / 19.6 at a = 25 and n = 1e3 / 1e4 / 1e5 / 1e6, against K_pop = 31.
(3) PROTOCOL.
  - Cells: a in {5, 10, 20, 25}, n in {1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6}; 5 replicates (3 at n = 1e6); seed = 1000 a + 10 log10(n) + r.
  - Solver: the exact empirical NPMLE, accepted only with max_t D_n(t) - 1 <= 1e-9 and |D_n(theta_j) - 1| <= 1e-9 at every
    atom. Binning of the data at width <= 1e-4 is allowed. K_n counts atoms of weight > 1e-10 after merging atoms closer
    than 1e-6.
  - Calibration: kappa (M1) and c (M2, M3) by least squares on the median K_n of the four a = 10 cells only, then frozen.
  - Score: rms of (median K_n - prediction)/K_pop(a) over the 12 cells with a in {5, 20, 25}. The smallest rms is PREFERRED.
    M1 HOLDS if it is preferred and its rms is <= 0.10. If M0 is preferred, the finite-sample effect is absent at these n
    and the heuristic of (1) is refuted.
  - Mechanism check (not scored): in the centre region (depth > d_n), the mean atom spacing against 1/rho_law(d_n).
(4) Written before any finite-sample NPMLE has been computed in this project. The run is made separately, and it
must import q500 unchanged and must not see any result before calibration is frozen.

## Amendment 676 (2026-09-24 11:27) - LFP: a centre-anchored Volterra identity ties the envelope (level) deviation to the KKT gap integrated from the centre; numerically it accounts for the level deviation to a factor 1.7-3 (our own derivation and check)
(1) THE IDENTITY (ours; elementary, exact). For the LFP, u = sqrt(f*) satisfies 4 u''/u = V exactly (V = 4u''/u,
CAPLB_ATTEMPT.md 318-323). Put 4k^2 := 1 - r* and q := -(V - (r* - 1))/4. Then
    u'' + (k^2 + q) u = 0,   and   phi * q = (r* - R)/4 >= 0 on [-m, m]    (R - 1 = phi * V; KKT).
By symmetry u'(0) = 0. With A := u(0) and delta := u - A cos(ky), variation of constants gives, for 0 <= y,
    delta(y) = -(1/k) int_0^y sin(k(y - s)) q(s) u(s) ds.
So the level deviation at y is fixed by the forcing on the CENTRAL interval [0, y] only, and the Gaussian smoothing of the
forcing is exactly the nonnegative KKT gap. Where the kernel sin(k(y - s)) u(s) varies slowly on the unit scale, replacing q
by phi * q changes the integral little, and then delta(y) <= 0 with |delta(y)| <~ (1/k) int_0^y ((r* - R)/4) u.
(2) THE CHECK (our code; stored 192-bit state at m = 35.8, K = 59, converted to double; lf0_common loaders only). Level
deviation measured as the Gaussian smoothing (sigma = 1.5) of f*/(A^2 cos^2(ky)) minus its value at 0, against the
prediction 2 delta_pred/(A cos(ky)) with the gap r* - R computed on the grid:
    depth 17: -9.6e-10 vs -3.9e-10;  15: -2.8e-9 vs -1.7e-9;  12: -3.4e-8 vs -1.5e-8;  10: -2.3e-7 vs -7.9e-8;  8: -1.3e-6 vs -4.5e-7.
Same sign (u lies below A cos(ky), as q >= 0 on average predicts) and the same depth dependence; the measured deviation is
1.7-3 times the prediction. Beyond depth 20 both are below the double-precision floor of the measurement (~1e-11). Two
earlier measurements were contaminated and are discarded: taking A = u(0) with its ripple gave a constant offset 7.5e-9, and
sigma = 3 leaked the edge-layer deviation (1e-3) into depths 10-20.
(3) WHY IT MATTERS. LFP43_ATTEMPT.md 0.3 names the missing step (G-low): the smooth part of f* equals A cos^2(ky) up to
e^(-c Lambda0) in the weighted sense, which no weighted identity supplies (the negative directions of Q_chi). The identity of
(1) supplies it from a different source: the level at y is controlled by the weighted L^1 norm of the gap on [0, y], and a
weighted L^1 bound on the gap is already available from the weighted identity, since int chi (r* - R) d(A nu) <= Eterm +
Xchi + TC (LFP43_ATTEMPT.md 107-108). Xchi itself contains the level deviation, so the two close as a bootstrap:
level <= C (Eterm + TC + Xchi)/chi(y), Xchi <= EH/2 + C (Lambda0/m)^2 int chi v^2 (w - 1)^2, and the level part of the last
term is quadratic in the bound. SKETCHED, not proved. The steps to write: (a) the passage from q to phi * q in the Volterra
integral with explicit error (kernel smoothness; the endpoint; the rectified ripple product); (b) the deconvolution tails
against the weight; (c) the bootstrap constants with Lambda0 = c0 m^(2/3); then the two steps LFP43 lists as sketched (the
high-band commutator in H^1 form; Lemma C with the reference A nu).

## Amendment 684 (2026-09-24 15:00) - (L-a): the Gaussian smoothing is the right low-pass; a band-limited filter leaks the edge layer into the bulk; the linear endpoint ripple is controlled by EH in the norm the bootstrap uses
(1) THE LINEAR TERM. In psi * delta = gap term + E, E contains the psi-smoothed ripple of u at the endpoint y, linear in
the ripple amplitude and damped only by e^(-sigma^2 omega^2/2). If it were counted as level, (L-c) would pick up
(Lambda0/m)^2 x (length m) x EH = Lambda0^2 EH/m ~ c0^2 m^(1/3) EH, which is not small.
(2) BAND-LIMITED FILTER TESTED AND REJECTED (our test; m = 30.0 and 35.8; FFT low-pass with cutoff tapered over 0.8-1.2): the
filtered deviation at depths 8-15 is 2e-6 to 2e-5, three orders above the Gaussian-smoothed values (1e-9 to 1e-7). The
cause is the filter's non-locality (and FFT periodicity): the edge-layer deviations (1e-3 to 1) leak into the bulk. Such
a filter is also incompatible with the exponential weight chi.
(3) RESOLUTION (our reasoning). Keep the Gaussian psi and split w - 1 = psi * (w - 1) + (1 - psi *)(w - 1). Since
|1 - e^(-sigma^2 xi^2/2)|^2 <= sigma^2 xi^2/2 for every real xi, ||(1 - psi *) g||^2 <= (sigma^2/2) ||g'||^2 without any
band gap, so the high part, including the endpoint ripple, is controlled by EH (up to commutators with chi). The low part
is the gap term plus the rectified quadratic term (<= Rip2, measured |E|/Rip2 <= 0.24). The linear endpoint term enters
(L-c) only through its chi-weighted L^2 norm, which is at most C EH e^(-sigma^2 omega_min^2)/omega_min^2: no square root.
LFP_VOLTERRA_NOTE.md (L-a) is updated accordingly.
(4) q492: locating the 60 -> 61 appear point (a pal landing at 36.49137975, 14:59, is part of the search); not yet printed.

error is itself bounded by the centre ripple, so both sides scale as e^Lambda r(0)^2 and nothing closes. A signed weight with

## Amendment 724 (2026-09-25 06:59) - the LFP and capacity edge laws have two-line proofs; the LFP factor (1 - r*) is the Bayes-risk identity, now derived; at every gap cut the edge value is an oscillator energy minus currents of the SURE ripple; eight LFP cuts hold to 6e-33 and six capacity cuts at the KKT residual (1.4e-14, 1.1e-10); 723's ratio at m = 39.1 corrected (label B)
(1) DERIVATION (ours, by hand, written into pred_edge_currents.txt at 06:49:43 before any run; EDGE_1E_NOTE.md 9b).
- The potential. For d = y + s, s = f'/f, Stein's identity gives R(theta) = 1 + int phi(y - theta) V(y) dy with
  V := 2 s' + s^2 = 2 f''/f - (f'/f)^2 = 4 u''/u, u := f^(1/2). Integrating against pi gives int f V = r* - 1 =: Vbar, the Bayes
  risk 1 - I(f) of the LFP. Both are standard one-line identities; attribution is not checked, so no source is named.
- The edge term. R'(theta_j) = 0 at interior atoms, and d/dtheta phi(y - theta) = (y - theta) phi(y - theta). Summing w_j R'(theta_j)
  over the atoms right of a gap cut x* leaves w_m R'(m) = -int f_R' V.
- The fold. f' V = (f'^2/f)' and f' Vbar = (Vbar f)'. Hence, exactly, at every gap cut:
      w_m R'(m) = 4E(x*) - f_R(x*) <V - Vbar>_{mu_R} - f_L(x*) <V - Vbar>_{mu_L},
      4E := (1 - r*) f + f'^2/f = 4 (u'^2 + k^2 u^2),   4 k^2 := 1 - r*,
  with mu_R := f_R' dy/f_R(x*) on (-inf, x*] and mu_L := -f_L' dy/f_L(x*) on [x*, inf), both probability measures.
- Capacity, the same steps with U = log p and p' log p = (p log p - p)', then one integration by parts:
      w_A J'(A) = -p(x*) + int_{-inf}^{x*} p_R (log p)' - int_{x*}^{inf} p_L (log p)'.
- Control. The continuum reference f = A cos^2(k y) has u'' = -k^2 u, so V = Vbar = -4k^2 and the currents vanish. Then
  4E = 4 k^2 A = (1 - r*) f(0) at every cut. The inline continuum values of 06:42 (ratio 1.0 at k = 0.04 and 0.02) follow.

## Amendment 758 (2026-09-29 21:51) - bridge 3 opened: model selection is the capacity functional itself (Mattingly's five atoms at L = 10 reproduced), the bridges' existence is partly prior art (Mattingly et al. already point to rational inattention, rate-distortion and an immune model), and the immune-repertoire functional of Mayer et al. is in the class; its first test run was void (label B), the continuation run is under way with an exact analytic control

(1) MODEL SELECTION (q507_mattingly_gauss.py). Mattingly, Transtrum, Abbott, Machta (PNAS 2018), Fig. 2 caption in the text we extracted
(papers/mattingly_1705.01166.txt): the one-parameter Gaussian model with L = 10 "clearly converges to the same five delta functions".
Their objective is the mutual information between parameter and data, i.e. the capacity functional with half-length A = L/2 = 5. An
independent double-precision solver finds exactly five atoms (-5, -2.2653, 0, 2.2653, 5; weights 0.2503, 0.1708, 0.1580), residual
1.1e-11, KKT margin -3.0e-06. PASS as pre-registered. This is a consistency check of the same functional, not an independent bridge.
(2) PRIOR ART ON THE BRIDGES THEMSELVES, from the same extracted text: Mattingly et al. write that "In statistics, this problem is more often
discussed as an equivalent minimax problem", that "Discreteness has been useful ... in the idea of rational inattention in economics",
that "Rate-distortion theory has also been useful in several areas of biology", and that "discreteness emerges in a recent theoretical
model of the immune system". So the existence of these connections is in the literature, qualitatively. What 757 added is quantitative:
the record's count law and transition sequence, passed across the connections as parameter-free predictions. The roadmap is
worded accordingly.
(3) IMMUNOLOGY (Mayer, Balasubramanian, Mora, Walczak, PNAS 2015; arXiv 1407.6888, text extracted to papers/mayer_2015_immune.txt).
Their expected cost <F> = sum_a Q_a Fbar_a(Ptilde_a), Ptilde = f * P with Gaussian cross-reactivity f(r - a) = exp(-(r - a)^2/2 sigma^2),
is convex in P (their App. B); for F(m) = m, Fbar = 1/Ptilde (their B1). That is the record's class (a convex functional of the
Gaussian-smoothed measure), so the common lemma predicts the same leading phase law. They report from numerics that "the peaks are spaced
evenly, at roughly the cross-reactivity scale sigma". Pre-registered test in q508_immune_bridge.py (uniform Q on [-a, a], sigma = 1,

under squared error (Gaussian reproduction), AWGN capacity under a power constraint (Gaussian input), and the immune functional on a
circle with uniform Q (the uniform repertoire gives g = C at every point, and the optimum is unique because 1/Pt is strictly convex
and Gaussian convolution is injective on the circle, its Fourier coefficients being exp(-k^2 sigma^2/2) > 0). So discreteness needs a
BOUNDED continuum, a hard edge, or more generally a target the smoothing cannot reproduce. Every bridge in the record has a bounded
continuum and the count law is written in its length L, so the target keeps its breadth; its sentence now says "bounded continuum"
(ROADMAP_2026-09-29.md updated).

ask; it will be pre-registered before it runs.

(5) WHY THE 2D DEPTHS MATCH (derivation). Uniform Q on a half-plane is invariant along the edge. A measure
spread uniformly along a line, convolved with the 2D Gaussian, is a 1D Gaussian in the normal direction, and every functional in the
class depends on P only through that convolution; so the half-plane problem restricted to edge-invariant P is exactly the 1D edge
problem (label M). If the half-plane optimum (per unit length of edge) is unique it is edge-invariant, hence lines parallel to the edge
at the 1D atom depths; that uniqueness step is not proved for the infinite domain (UNCHECKED). The depth
match in q510 (and in q513 if it passes) is this limit near each side, a consistency check. What the half-plane cannot give is why the
layers break into POINTS and how they are spaced. q514_along_layer.py pre-registers H_corner (the corners act as the edges of a 1D
problem along each side, so the along-layer spacing is smallest in the middle of a side) against H_flat (uniform spacing), scored on the
q513 polished states, written before any along-layer spacing was looked at.

typically purely discrete beyond the critical distortion threshold (below which the Shannon lower bound is tight), except for the Gaussian

the only possible degenerate support point and the only possible inactive contact point (their Theorem 2), that every nonzero support
point persists and moves continuously, and that locally the support size is unchanged or larger by one with any increase at the
origin: births and deaths of the origin atom, or its splitting into a symmetric pair or merging back. The proof counts zeros with
multiplicity: by Karlin's oscillation theorem the KKT function has at most 2K of them; the support uses 2K - 2, which leaves room for
one degenerate point (their (64)-(66), (73)-(81)). So for capacity the birth rule of the target is prior art, as recorded before.

transform of Q/Pt^2, and Pt^2 is a combination of Gaussians centred at the pairwise midpoints of the atoms, so the same count does not
obviously give 2K; whether a bound of that kind holds for F(m) = m is UNCHECKED. The record's 1D immune data are so far strictly
one at a time at the centre (8 -> 24), with competing crossings that shrink with K (763 (5)) and a nearly degenerate centre from the
K = 24 -> 25 birth on (767); that is where the rule's reach beyond log-type functionals would show.

## Amendment 770 (2026-09-30 05:51) - the zero count of arXiv 2609.10039 carries to the whole class with uniform Q (derivation checked numerically, BIRTH_RULE_NOTE.md), which corrects 769 (2): births and splits come one at a time and only at the origin for the immune functional and the NPMLE too, modulo the continuity steps of that paper; the count test's first seed was far from optimal and is re-seeded

(1) THE COUNT (BIRTH_RULE_NOTE.md). For a functional int Q F(Pt) with F' monotone and uniform Q on [-a, a], the normalised KKT function
is G = f * h with h = Q |F'(Pt)|/lambda - 1/sqrt(2 pi). Inside [-a, a] h changes sign exactly where Pt crosses one level; Pt, a
positive combination of K equal-width Gaussians, has at most K modes (Carreira-Perpinan and Williams, Theorem 2.3, "In 1D, any Gaussian
mixture with M components has at most M modes", text in papers/carreira_williams_gmmodes.txt line 288), so it crosses a level at most
2K times; the jumps of Q at +-a add at most two. So S(h) <= 2K + 2, and by Karlin's oscillation theorem (the step 2609.10039 uses) G has
at most 2K + 2 zeros counted with multiplicity. The K interior atoms use 2K, leaving room for one inactive contact point or one
degenerate atom, not both and never a symmetric pair; by symmetry it sits at the origin. 769 (2) said the count was not obviously
available for 1/Pt^2 because Pt^2 has pairwise-midpoint centres; that was wrong, since Q/Pt^2 - c and Pt - c' change sign together.
(2) NUMERICAL CHECK (q525_zero_count.py, KKT-verified states): immune a = 18, K = 21, S(h) = 42 (bound 44, atoms 42); immune a = 12,
K = 13, S(h) = 26 (bound 28, atoms 26); NPMLE L = 18, K = 20, S(h) = 42 (bound 42, atoms 40). The bound holds each time.
(3) WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE RECORD. The record's 1D immune continuation was strictly one change at a time at the centre (K = 8 to 24),

## Amendment 789 (2026-09-30 13:20) - literature gate on the piece rule: count additivity over support pieces, shape-independence of the NPMLE count, and a count change by periodic modulation were not found in 32 sources read and grepped; the closest results constrain atom locations or treat only tight, far-apart clusters

(1) GATE (report lit_gate_piece_rule.md, texts in papers/litgate_piece_rule/, 30 sources downloaded and extracted plus OCR
of the two scanned Lindsay 1983 papers; 30 logged searches). Key quotes re-verified with grep in the extracted files:
Aragam et al. 2410.22248 ("K well-separated modes", arxiv_2410.22248.txt), Polyanskiy and Sellke 2503.20193 (one atom per cluster,
arxiv_2503.20193_raw.txt:3120-3121), Mayer et al. 2015 ("the peaks are spaced evenly", mayer_2015_immune_raw.txt), Abbott and Machta
1710.09351 ("in some sense universal"), Lindsay 1983 II Thm 4.1(b) ("real zeroes of the mixture", lindsay_thm41_ocr.txt), Barletta and
Dytso 2609.10039 ("all local changes in support cardinality are confined").
(2) VERDICT as the report words it, which we accept after the checks above:
 (a) additivity over pieces: PARTIAL. Lindsay's Theorem 4.1(b) excludes atoms from the central part of a data gap wider than 2 noise
     units (unit variance) and says nothing about counts; Polyanskiy and Sellke, App. C, prove one atom per tight cluster when clusters
     are C log(k+1) apart with C large. Additivity for extended pieces, or for gaps below 2 noise units: not found in the 32 sources.
 (b) shape-independence and the L^(4/3) count: PARTIAL. K ~ L^(4/3) through the Fisher length is stated for capacity (Mattingly et al.
     2018; Abbott and Machta 2019); Mayer et al. 2015 report evenly spaced peaks for the immune functional. No source states that the
     count for a data density is independent of its shape, and none gives a constant for the NPMLE.
 (c) periodic modulation changing the count and locking atoms: not found (0 relevant hits in two targeted searches); Aragam et al.
     observe atoms near well-separated modes, without proof.
(3) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD. The piece rule, the shape-independence of the count at slow modulation, and the count change with
locking in the window may be described as "not found in the 32 sources checked (lit_gate_piece_rule.md)". No stronger word is used.
Referee risk noted by the gate: Barletta and Dytso (2604.14915) read numerically observed exponents as solver-tolerance effects; every

## Amendment 822 (2026-09-30 19:35) - CORRECTION to 821 (3): the transition-location law has a precedent in this record (the LFP, 631 (6) and 634), and the a^(2/3) term has a derived analogue there

statements ignore our own record. 631 (2) derived the LFP local law to O(rho^-2), rho^2 rho'/s0 = 1 + 5/(8 pi^2 rho^2) + 2 rho |g'/g|
(capacity: 1 + 1/(8 pi^2 rho^2)), and from it K(m) = 0.4002442 m^(4/3) + 1.539821 m^(2/3) + O(m^(1/3)), which overcounts by 1.6-3.1 atoms
at m <= 18 (631 (4)). 631 (6) froze a transition-location predictor for the LFP (the count threshold T fitted on 8 <= m_t <= 18.68);
634 and later amendments scored it forward to m = 40 with maximum error 0.046 in m (19 of 20 transitions in (30, 40]). What 821 adds is
the uniform immune case: the transitions fall on one smooth phase to 1e-4 with no birth/split staggering, and a fit on a <= 19.77
places the two 200-bit events to 0.0004-0.0009. The immune local law to O(rho^-2), which would give the a^(2/3) coefficient to compare
with the fitted 0.113, is not derived. For a correction b/rho^2 in rho^2 rho'/s0, the same integration gives an a^(2/3) coefficient
(b/s0)(3 s0)^(2/3) = 0.0712 b/s0 over both halves (our algebra, label M, not checked against 631's derivation); the capacity value
b = 1/(8 pi^2) gives 0.142. The pre-registered windows of 821 (4) are unchanged.

## Amendment 827 (2026-09-30 19:59) - a sketch of why the classes split (pointwise G versus a G with derivatives), label M and not a derivation; NPMLE 24 -> 25 passes (5 of 5)

(1) SKETCH. Each KKT function in the first class is a Gaussian smoothing of a pointwise function of the output density:
k(y) = (phi * [Q G(Ptilde)])(y), with G = -log f (capacity), G = 1/f (NPMLE, rate-distortion), G = 1/f^2 (immune). For a slowly varying
comb, Ptilde = S (1 + eps) with eps the ripple at the lattice frequency (amplitude ~ exp(-2 pi^2 rho^2), about 1e-4 in the bulk here). To
first order in eps, Q G(Ptilde) = Q G(S) + Q G'(S) S eps. With uniform Q the weight conditions keep S constant in the bulk up to O(eps),
so Q G'(S) S is a constant factor there (-1, -Q/S, -2Q/S^2) and the ripple term is that constant times phi * eps. The positional
condition, and with it the local law including its O(rho^-2) chirp correction, is therefore the same for every pointwise G. The LFP's
G = -dI(f)/df contains derivatives of f; its first-order response carries powers of the lattice wavenumber, which is where 631 (2)'s
5/(8 pi^2 rho^2) and the tilt term come from. Consequences to test: (a) any pointwise G with uniform Q gives c2 near 0.1424 in the
transition fit of 826; (b) a slowly varying Q makes Q G'(S) S vary and can add a tilt term of order rho |Q'/Q|, which fits the small
e2 of 824 (bump +0.031, dip -0.022) and would vanish as the bump's scale grows with a. Not checked against the LFP_DERIVATION algebra;
label M.
(2) q590: 24 -> 25 (birth) at 20.786199, predicted 20.786140, error +5.9e-5: PASS (5 of 5; own-fit error -2.5e-4).
Gates: no gate word used.

Report LITGATE_BIRTHS_2026-09-30.md (40 web searches, 49 arXiv queries, 3 Semantic Scholar calls, all logged; sources in
papers/litgate_births/). Verdicts: Q1 (a formula or fit for the sequence of critical amplitudes) PARTLY; Q2 (a second-order term of K(A)
or a corrected density law) NOT FOUND; Q3 (shared transition sequences across problems) PARTLY; Q4 (BA residue near births) PARTLY.
Passages we re-extracted ourselves with pdftotext before recording:
- Barletta-Dytso, arXiv 2609.10039v1 (9 Sep 2026), abstract: for the peak-constrained AWGN channel "the structure of its support
  transitions has remained largely unresolved". Their results are local (the origin is the only degenerate support point; the
  cardinality near a given amplitude is unchanged or larger); no law for the sequence.
- Nakagawa, Takei, Hara, arXiv 2009.08780 (IEEE T-IT 2021), Theorem 4: the eigenvalues of the Arimoto-Blahut Jacobian at inactive inputs
  are e^{D_i - C} (D_i < C). This is the mechanism 831 (1) used for the binomial centre dots (mass at a point with deficit delta decays
  by e^{-delta} per iteration); 831's reading stands, with this citation. The x = 1/2 artefact before a binomial birth is not reported.
- Abbott-Machta, arXiv 1710.09351: the Euler-Lagrange equation of their field theory (p. 8) gives, by the report's arithmetic, K = 0.368
  a^(4/3); 481 (1) already showed that their constant corresponds to X = 1 where the full harmonic sum gives X_inf = pi^2/6, which raises
  the prefactor by (pi^2/6)^(1/6) = 1.086 to 0.4002. The authors print no prefactor.
UNCHECKED: Zhang's 1994 thesis and the full text of Gourdin-Jaumard-MacGibbon 1994 (not obtained).

## Amendment 848 (2026-09-30 21:26) - the centre constant is 1/3 at leading order: a continuum derivation (a separate run, CENTRE_CONSTANT_DERIVATION.md) with the parts we verified ourselves; the finite-rho transitions sit slightly below, at 0.32-0.33

(1) THE DERIVATION (labels as in its report). Where the two chirped halves meet, the phase condition has one admissible centre
solution in the continuum limit v = 4 pi rho -> infinity: M(x) = K/2 + rho_c x - eta(x/v)/2 with eta'(xi) = 2 xi coth(pi xi), so eta(xi)
= xi|xi| + (1/6) sgn(xi) + O(xi e^{-2 pi |xi|}) (DERIVED). Matching it to the edge law gives 2 N(a) = K + 1/6 on that solution, and the
atoms near the centre sit off the edge-fitted counting function by r(x) = int_{x/v}^inf t (coth(pi t) - 1) dt (1/12 at the centre). The
solution describes the chain just before a transition, hence c_centre = 1/2 - 1/6 = 1/3 at leading order, for every functional of the
class (only the leading chirp law enters). The birth condition reduces to Ghat(0) = 0 (DERIVED); that the split condition does too is a
CONJECTURE of the report. At finite rho the centre keeps a reduced barrier, Ghat_sharp(0)/|Ghat_bulk| -> 1/(2 rho^2) (DERIVED, with Gaussian
quadrature 0.686, 0.549, 0.403, 0.280, 0.203 at rho = 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.25, 1.5), so the transition comes a little after the sharp point:
the report measures c_trans = 0.327-0.328 at a ~ 25 and states c_trans -> 1/3 from below as a CONJECTURE.
(2) WHAT I VERIFIED OURSELVES.
  - The constant: int_0^inf 2t (coth(pi t) - 1) dt = 4 sum_n 1/(2 n pi)^2 = (1/pi^2) zeta(2) = 1/6 (by hand; quadrature gives
    r(0) = 0.083333333 = 1/12).

    (a = 24.3017, 24.9336, 25.5581) the inner residuals follow r(x) in shape at 85-92 % of its size (innermost 0.0599 against 0.0650,

    (a = 25.0) the profile does not hold (innermost -0.164), as the report says (it describes the chain before a transition).
  - Window independence: with r(x) built into the fit, d >= 3 and d >= 4 give the same 2 N(a) - K to 1e-4 (fit rms 8e-4 to 1.7e-3); at
    the three pre-transition rows 2 N(a) - K = 0.156, 0.160, 0.162, rising toward 1/6 as the transition approaches. Our extrapolation to

transition sequence of a pointwise-G functional is then fixed by the bulk law (derived to O(rho^-4)), two edge numbers per functional,

barrier (saddle estimate mu = sqrt 2; quadrature 1.4216 at rho 0.8, 1.4249 at 1.25) and moves the far-field offset by exactly zero. What

Basis (LFP_DERIVATION 2.6-2.8, 631): s/s0 = 1 + 5/(8 pi^2 rho^2) + 2 rho |g'/g| with s = rho^2 rho', s0 = 1/(16 pi^2); the mass density
g ~ cos^2(pi theta/(2(m + delta))) (Bickel's form, measured at finite m with delta ~ 3.34); 1 - r = pi^2/(m + delta)^2. Near the wall
(theta = m - d) this gives |g'/g| = 2/(d + delta) - (1 - r)(d + delta)/6 + O((1 - r)^2), so the level enters the local law only through
the second term, which lowers rho^2 rho' when r falls and pushes the atoms deeper.

## Amendment 940 (2026-10-01 06:11) - literature gate for the bulk law, the centre and the class (LITGATE_BULKLAW_2026-10-01.md): all three claims PARTIAL; every quantitative part NOT FOUND in about 73 logged searches

(1) Verdicts (40 web searches, 20 arXiv queries, 12 OpenAlex calls, one citation list; texts in papers/litgate_bulklaw/):
C1 bulk law and count: PARTIAL. Published: the exponent 4/3 and a leading density of order d^(1/3) (Abbott and Machta 2019, a field argument
with no constant; their equation gives the prefactor 0.3684 and no correction, as recorded in 481). NOT FOUND: s0 = 1/(16 pi^2), the
prefactor 0.4002, k/rho^2 or any higher term, the A^(2/3) coefficient, any atom-density law for the LFP or the NPMLE. The growth law is
treated as open by the information-theory group: Wang, Barletta and Dytso (IEEE T-IT 2026) list A sqrt(log A), A log A, A^(4/3), A^2 as
candidates and call the scaling open (not re-read).
C2 centre births: PARTIAL. Published: births happen at the centre (Barletta-Dytso arXiv 2609.10039, locally, for capacity; Casella-
Strawderman 1981 for the first LFP transitions). Rose (1994) listed the location of birth-type transitions in rate-distortion as open,
and no later solution was found. NOT FOUND: 2 N_half = K + 1/6 + delta, N_half, 1/6 = zeta(2)/pi^2 from the coth centre equation, a delta
shared across problems.
C3 class: PARTIAL, qualitative only (Abbott-Machta "in some sense universal"; Mattingly et al.; NPMLE = rate-distortion). Mayer et al.
used periodic domains without edges. NOT FOUND: any shared law or quantitative comparison.
(2) Our spot check of quotes against the extracted texts: arXiv 2609.10039 "the global monotonicity of K(A) remains open" is verbatim.
Bickel 1981 lines 24-25 read "the number of points increases, their location and the masses assigned to them vary in an as yet unknown
fashion": the phrase is verbatim, but the gate file attributes the unknown variation to the number as well; a correction note is appended
to the file.
(3) Not accessible here (paywalled): Gourdin, Jaumard and MacGibbon, SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 1994 (numerical LFPs, HTTP 403 behind the
SIAM paywall) and Zhang's 1994 thesis (ProQuest). Either may hold LFP support counts to set against the record; neither blocks the work.
(4) Wording rule stands: "not found in about 73 searches" is the strongest statement; no novelty word is used.
Gates: literature gate run for C1-C3.

## Amendment 957 (2026-10-01 07:19) - bridge reading: the NPMLE births law gives the critical temperatures of deterministic annealing (rate-distortion) for a uniform source, T_K / Var = 6 / a_t(K)^2; a table of 32 values from converged transitions

(1) Identity (M, our algebra on the record's NPMLE = rate-distortion bridge): rate-distortion for a source uniform on [-L, L] with squared
error at inverse temperature beta has the KKT of the NPMLE with the kernel exp(-beta (x - y)^2), i.e. noise variance sigma^2 = 1/(2 beta),
data uniform on a half-width a = L/sigma = L sqrt(2 beta). The deterministic-annealing transitions in beta at fixed L are therefore the
NPMLE transitions in a: T_K = 1/beta_K = 2 L^2/a_t(K)^2, and with Var = L^2/3, T_K/Var = 6/a_t(K)^2. Check: the first split of the NPMLE is
at a = sqrt(3) (data variance = noise variance), which gives T = 2 Var, the known first critical temperature.
(2) Table (q644_da_temperatures.json; 32 NPMLE transitions K -> K + 1 located with every state converged, K = 10-52): e.g. K = 10:

6.34440e-3; K = 52: 37.5740838506, 4.24986e-3.

## Amendment 973 (2026-10-01 10:32) - PRE-REGISTERED (Tier C): the 2D bulk law with a derived curvature term; no 2D ring position beyond A = 12 has been read

1. Derivation (ours, saddle level). For capacity on the disc |x| <= A the bulk input is uniform per unit area, so the rings form a comb on
   a flat areal density, and the first-harmonic argument of 1D (BULK_C6_DERIVATION 1.1) carries over with
   I2(r) = int int psi(a) psi(b) exp(2 pi i [N(|(r + a, b)|) - N(r)]) da db, psi = N(0, 2); positional condition arg I2 = pi at each
   ring. To leading order in b, |(r + a, b)| = r + a + b^2/(2(r + a)), and the b integral is (1 + 4 pi i rho/(r + a))^(-1/2). The a
   integral sits at the complex saddle a = -i q, q = 4 pi rho (the depth saddle u = 2 i alpha of the 1D case), where the factor is
   ((r - i q)/r)^(1/2), of argument -(1/2) arctan(q/r). The 1D law PHI - arg G = pi becomes PHI - arg G + (1/2) arctan(4 pi rho/r) = pi,
   that is
       rho^2 rho' / s0 = f1(rho) - c (1/(2 pi)) arctan(4 pi rho/r),   c = 1,   r = A - d,
   with f1 the derived 1D law (933). Neglected: the variation of the b factor across the saddle's width (relative order 2/(r^2 + q^2)),
   the b^4 terms, and any change of the areal density near the wall and the centre. The sign means sparser rings than in 1D, which is
   the direction seen at A = 7-12 (970's states; a first-order estimate on those states, 0.028/0.077/0.136/0.203 against
   0.051/0.093/0.137/0.182 extra depth at A = 12, was computed before this amendment and is disclosed here).
2. Instrument q653_bulk2d_fit.py: integrates the law with two free constants (N and rho at the first fitted ring), c fixed at 0 (M0, the
   1D law), at 1 (M1, derived) or free; rings with depth >= 6 and radius >= 6. Controls run before this amendment:
   (a) the 1D capacity half-line under a fake radius A = 20, 25, 30 (true c = 0): rms M0 1.4e-6, 1.2e-6, 1.3e-6; c_fit -0.0003, 0.0000,
       0.0001; M1 is worse (4e-3 to 1.4e-2), so the curvature term is far above the instrument's floor;
   (b) data made by M1 itself (true c = 1): c_fit 1.0000 at all three.
3. Data: q650_rings2d_far.json from the continuation now running to A = 30 (q650_rings2d_far.py, a copy of q649 with its own output and
   a repaired birth step after a stop at the birth near A 17.90). States at A = 20, 25, 30; if the run stops early, the largest integer
   A >= 18 it reaches, declared before reading.
4. PREDICTIONS. P1: |c_fit - 1| <= 0.2 at each A read. P2: rms(M1) <= rms(M0)/3 at each A. P3: the arctan form beats the linear
   alternative 2 rho/r (FORM=lin): |c_fit(arctan) - 1| < |c_fit(lin) - 1| at each A. PASS needs P1 and P2 at every A read; P3 and the
   trend of c_fit with A are read and reported. FAIL otherwise; the null c = 0 fails P1 by construction.

## Amendment 977 (2026-10-01 10:41) - second instrument for the 2D and 3D solvers: the first births equal Dytso-Poor-Shamai's single-shell thresholds to ten digits

Source: Dytso, Poor, Shamai, "On the Capacity of the Peak Power Constrained Vector Gaussian Channel: An Estimation Theoretic
Perspective", arXiv 1804.08524v1 (downloaded to temporal_within/papers/, text extracted with pypdf). Their Theorem 3: the single
sphere of radius R is optimal iff R <= Rbar_n, Rbar_n the positive zero of E[(W1/|W|) h_{n/2}(R |W|)] = 1/2, W1 with density
(Q(w - R) - Q(w))/R, W2..Wn iid N(0, 1), h_v = I_v/I_{v-1} (their eq. 6). The paper prints Rbar_1 = 1.665925641 (Fig. 6 caption) and
shows Rbar_n for n up to 20 only as a plot (Fig. 2).
Our evaluation of their equation (Gauss-Legendre, 400 nodes per axis, brentq): Rbar_1 = 1.665925641 (their printed value), Rbar_2 =
2.453389958, Rbar_3 = 3.065107732. Our KKT solvers: 2D first birth 2.453389958 (967, d50_lib), 3D first birth 3.065107732 (976,
d70_lib3d). The two routes share no code (theirs is an estimation-theoretic identity, ours the KKT equality i(0) = i(A)).
Gates: no gate word used.

before a lift-off it is the comb of J_{nu+1} plus an origin mass (nu + 1 = d/2). The McMahon pole of the core contributes
-(4 nu^2 - 1)/v^2 to 2 N(A) - K at the event (1007, phase checked on exact Bessel combs for d = 2), so
  c_birth - c_liftoff = [(4 (d/2)^2 - 1) - (4 (d/2 - 1)^2 - 1)]/v^2 = 4 (d - 1)/v^2,
which is 4/v^2 at d = 2 (1007) and 0 at d = 1 (no 1D split). The common level is not predicted.
Data (seen as e values, gaps not computed): q661 centre values with c = d - 1, K_eff from event states: d = 3 q661_d3.txt, d = 4
q661_d4.txt, d = 5 q661_d5.txt; d = 2 as 1008.
TEST: at rho_c = 0.70, 0.72, 0.74 (and wherever both event types are measured), the measured gap e_birth - e_liftoff (interpolated in
rho_c) over 4 (d - 1)/v^2 lies in 0.85-1.25 for d = 3, 4, 5 (the d = 2 ratio was 1.08-1.16). PASS if every ratio is in band; read the
trend with d. The alternatives "gap independent of d" and "gap growing like (d - 1)^2" fail the band at d = 4 and 5.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1027 (2026-10-01 15:24) - PRE-REGISTERED: the births constant at an asymmetric meeting point (annulus), with sealed outcomes

Question. Every births test so far had a symmetric centre: the 1D interval centre, or the origin of the d-ball. An annulus
a <= |x| <= a + W has no symmetric point; its rings are born where the branch from the inner wall meets the branch from the outer
wall. Does the births law hold there, and with which constant?
Derivation (CENTRE_CONSTANT_DERIVATION 3.1-3.6 with the transverse phase of the d-dimensional bulk law). The phase condition becomes
-pi D + phi_T = pi (mod 2 pi), phi_T = ((d - 1)/2) atan(v/r), the same for both branches because the saddle always sits at +iv in the
radial direction. The far-field values of D are phi_T/pi + 1 (inner side) and phi_T/pi - 1 (outer side), and the only admissible jump
at the meeting point is still -2. The solution is eta = eta_sym - (phi_T/pi) xi^2: the extra term changes only the far-field slopes
(the inner branch obeys rho^2 rho_z/s0 = f1 + ((d - 1)/(2 pi)) atan(4 pi rho/r), the outer branch the same with a minus sign), and
it leaves the +-1/12 offsets of eta_sym unchanged. Matching gives N_in(x0 - a) + N_out(a + W - x0) = K + 1/6 at the sharp point,
x0 where the two branch densities are equal. Prediction: annulus births carry the 1D constant 1/6 + delta(rho_c), with no Gouy term
(the ball's (d - 1)/2 comes from the focus at the origin, which the annulus does not have).
Instruments. q686_annulus_births.py (d85 library; continuation in W from 2 to 36 at fixed a, births bisected to 1e-7, outcomes
written only to q686_annulus_a{a}_d2_SEALED.json; runs a = 20 and a = 10 started 15:22). q687_annulus_centre.py: two-branch
readout (each branch fitted with its signed law, two constants, atoms with depth >= 6 and >= 6 from the midpoint; e = N_in + N_out - K
at rho_in = rho_out). Control: on the 13 certified 1D states c60_small_K26-38 it returns q661's e to every printed digit
(0.16003 ... 0.16262). Matched comparator: the same readout on the d = 1 chain (q684 DIM 1, run extended to half-width 19), which

same count K before the event. FAIL otherwise; the number of events in and out of the band is reported. Reported for contrast, no

## Amendment 1040 (2026-10-01 16:41) - PRE-REGISTERED (p_c runs unread): the whole-curve wall is special to the circle; every superellipse with p > 2 has a broken wall

Reasoning (heuristic, label: not derived). On the wall the KKT function has a non-zero outward derivative (the wall is a hard
constraint; about +0.3 at A = 3 from the shell states, 1026). If the boundary moves outward by eps(theta), D on the wall changes by
d_n D eps(theta), a term that keeps every angular mode of the shape. The only terms that can cancel it come from changing the masses,
and they pass through the Gaussian kernel twice (p = phi * mu, D = -phi * log p), so their angular modes decay like exp(-c m^2).
A superellipse's boundary has Fourier coefficients that decay polynomially (non-even p: |x|^p is not analytic at the edge midpoints)
or exponentially (even p, an algebraic curve), so its high modes cannot be cancelled and D cannot be constant along the whole
curve. If this holds, the circle's continuous wall is a consequence of its symmetry, the break point is p_c = 2, and the first
gaps sit where the boundary is least smooth (the edge midpoints for non-even p).
Predictions on the runs q698_p{2.1,2.2,2.3,2.4}_A3 (from uniform, stopping at a bracket of 2e-5; started 16:35, outputs unread):
(1) every one of them has a broken wall: some wall point with D below its maximum by more than 5 brackets and wall density below
1e-3 of its peak; (2) the deepest wall gap of each run includes the edge midpoint (bin 0). Falsifier: a run at p = 2.1 or 2.2 whose
wall D stays within 1 bracket of its maximum all around the curve.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1052 (2026-10-01 17:40) - sealed runs resumed with q686i to W = 44; a derived reason for the wall break at non-analytic points

(1) q686i validated on the unsealed a = 12: birth 3.3173869, split 5.797929, birth 8.0106515, split 10.081221, identical to q686f,
in 170 s against 255 s. The three q686f sealed runs were stopped at 17:39:31, their files copied unread (*_beforeresume.json), and
resumed with q686i from their own last saved states (RESUME=1, read by the script only) at 17:39:33, WMAX 44 as registered in 1050.
(2) WALL_ANALYTICITY_NOTE.md. D is real-analytic on the plane (a Gaussian convolution of log p, entire). On a supported wall arc
D = C, and where the outward slope is non-zero (0.448 for the disk at A = 3; positive by continuity on the nearby shapes) the
implicit function theorem makes {D = C} a real-analytic curve containing that arc. So a supported wall arc with non-zero slope is
real-analytic, and a boundary point where the boundary is not real-analytic (the superellipse's edge midpoints for non-even p,
however close p is to 2) cannot lie inside a supported arc. This accounts for 1040/1047 (gaps at the midpoints from p = 2.1) and is
silent on analytic shapes, which keep the whole wall when close to the circle (1041, 1045); even p = 4 breaks by a separate mechanism
(positivity of the wall density). Counting unknowns explains why a free interior ring survives (position and density for D = C and
zero slope) while the fixed wall does not. Checks it predicts: p = 2.05 and 2.02 have the midpoint outside the interior of the
supported wall; supported wall points have positive outward slope on every broken superellipse.

## Amendment 1054 (2026-10-01 17:45) - literature gate for the 2D wall findings: a published theorem on ellipses; the "whole wall" readings of 1044 and 1048 are qualified

Searches (four, logged with this entry): support topology of capacity-achieving inputs on non-circular 2D sets; rate-distortion
of a uniform source on a square or polygon; deterministic annealing on 2D uniform sources; support on analytic curves for arbitrary
compact sets. Read in extracted text: Dytso, Barletta, Kramer, arXiv 2401.17084 (papers/bridge_cap2d3d/extract/arxiv_2401.17084v1_c.txt
and papers/litgate_2dwall/), and Fahs, Abou-Faycal 1602.00878 (downloaded, papers/litgate_2dwall/, not yet read in full).
Found. 2401.17084 studies exactly the ellipse (the 2 x 2 MIMO channel with a peak constraint reduces to an input inside an ellipse with
axes rp >= rm). Their Theorem 3 (lines 325-329): for 0 <= rm <= rp < sqrt(2), "supp(PX*) is a finite set for rm != rp", and the input is
uniform on the circle for rm = rp. Their proof: an infinite support on the ellipse would, by the identity theorem, make the KKT relation
hold on the whole ellipse; continued to the imaginary axis it contradicts a growth bound. They state as open (lines 611-615) "the rate
at which the cardinality of the set supp(PX*) approaches infinity as rm -> rp".
Consequences for the record. (1) For small ellipses the wall support of a non-circular ellipse is finite, a set of isolated points.
Our ellipse runs (A = 3, 1041/1044; A = 4, 1048) are outside their size range, but a near-circular ellipse has a finite support whose
cardinality grows as rm -> rp, so the "whole wall" read there (density 0.96-1.00 of its peak, D within 1.8 brackets) can be a dense
finite set whose gaps are below the bracket. 1044 is qualified: no gap is visible at a bracket of 2e-5; whether the wall is whole is
not established. The same holds for the rose (1045 (1), passed as registered; its "whole wall" reading is qualified). (2) The superellipse
gaps at the non-analytic midpoints (1040, 1047) are deep (tens of brackets) and stand; WALL_ANALYTICITY_NOTE Step 3 stands, and its line
"analytic shapes carry no such obstruction" must read "carry no obstruction from Step 3"; 2401.17084 gives a different obstruction for
small ellipses. (3) Novelty words: none. The topology change on superellipses and the non-analytic-point mechanism were not found in
the sources read; the discreteness of the ellipse wall at small size is published (2401.17084).
Gates: "not found" used with its source list; no novelty word.

of the input, entire (Lemma 5). An infinite support on the ellipse makes this identity hold on all of (-rp, rp) (identity theorem),
then at x1 = iu, where Lemma 6 bounds the K-term by rp^2/2 + rm^2/2 + rm^2 sqrt(1 + u^2/rp^2) + 2 pi, against the term -u^2 (1 -

the size bound rp < sqrt(2) enters Theorem 3 only through Theorem 2 (all support on the ellipse); the finiteness argument itself
applies to the support points on the ellipse at any size, which would make the wall support of every non-circular ellipse finite.

other half or x2 as parameter would be needed), and step (a) of Appendix E, which bounds |log z| by log|z| + 2 pi where |log |z|| +

## Amendment 1068 (2026-10-01 19:08) - the ripple of a regular K-gon on the circle in closed form, checked; the 12-atom structures violate KKT near the circle at 80 nodes

(1) DERIVED (first order in the mode amplitude). For K equal atoms at radius r and angles theta0 + 2 pi j/K, the Jacobi-Anger
expansion keeps only angular modes that are multiples of K: p(y) = phi(s) e^(-r^2/2) [I_0(rs) + 2 I_K(rs) cos(K(psi - theta0)) + ...] at
y = s(cos psi, sin psi). Then on the circle D(alpha) = D_0 - 2 R_K cos(K(alpha - theta0)) + ..., with
    R_K(r) = 2 int_0^inf s exp(-(s^2 + r^2)/2) I_K(rs)^2 / I_0(rs) ds,
so the K-gon violates KKT midway between atoms by 2 R_K. At r = 1.3 (mpmath, 40 digits): 2 R_K = 1.96e-4 (K 6), 1.44e-6 (8), 6.91e-9
(10), 2.3437e-11 (12), 1.17e-16 (16), 2.38e-22 (20), 2.36e-28 (24). Checked: the measured violation of 12 equal atoms on the circle at 80
nodes is +2.344e-11 (1066), equal to 2 R_12 to the printed digits; for 16 atoms the measured +3.2e-15 is the D error floor and 2 R_16
lies below it. For large K, 2 R_K behaves like (r^2/2)^K/K! up to slowly varying factors, which is the heuristic of 1060 (c).
(2) 80 nodes, structures with the X orbit (Theorem 4): X + Y + 2G (K = 12) gives I equal to the rotated 12-atom I to 1e-13 and

## Amendment 1078 (2026-10-01 19:54) - the near-circle perturbation series for the ellipse density diverges like (m^3 eps)^(m/2); PRE-REGISTERED: its sign and order pattern in the saved 16-atom solutions

Derivation (q715_chain.py, definitions and quadrature only). Write the optimal input on the ellipse as a density f = 1 + sum a_m cos(m theta)
in the polar angle, boundary radius rho(theta) = r - eps sin^2(theta). D = C on the whole boundary, expanded in eps, gives at harmonic
m + 2 the balance -J_(m+2) a_(m+2) - (eps/4)[d2 J_m + d1 J_(m+2)] a_m + ... = 0, where -J_m(r1, r2) is the response of D at radius r2 to a
density harmonic m on radius r1 (q715 docstring), so a_(m+2)/a_m = -q_m eps with q_m = [d2 J_m + d1 J_(m+2)]/(4 J_(m+2)). At r = 1.3:
q_4 = 56.75, q_6 = 151.1, q_8 = 311.6, q_10 = 553.9, q_12 = 893.5, q_14 = 1345.6, q_16 = 1925.0; check 4 J_12 = 2.3437e-11 and 4 J_16 =
1.1694e-16 (the ripple of 1068). For large m, J_m/J_(m+2) grows like m^2 and d J_m/J_m like m/r, so q_m grows like m^3: the formal
series has a_(2n) ~ (-1)^n eps^n prod q, which shrinks while q_m eps < 1 and then grows without bound. The term turns at m*(eps) with
q_(m*) eps = 1: m* about 6 at eps = 0.01, 14 at 1e-3, about 130 at 1e-6 (q_m extrapolated as m^3), so m* grows like eps^(-1/3). This is
the mechanism behind the finite support (no positive density solves D = C) and it suggests a count of order eps^(-1/3), a power law,
against the K log K ~ log(1/eps) guess in DBK_CARDINALITY_NOTE. The rule that turns m* into a count is not derived; the terms left out
(products of harmonics, the background change at harmonic 2) are smaller by about 1/m^3 for large m and are not small at m = 2 or 4.
Status: DERIVED at leading order, heuristic for the count.

PRE-REGISTERED test on the saved K = 16 solutions (q708_rp1.3_rm1.29_X1Y1G3.json, eps = 0.01; q708_rp1.3_rm1.299_X1Y1G3.json, eps =
1e-3), whose harmonics we have not computed. Empirical a_m = 2 sum_k w_k cos(m theta_k), theta_k the polar angles of the atoms.
(a) Sign: a_2 > 0 (mass gathers toward the major vertices), a_4 < 0, a_6 > 0.
(b) Order in eps: a_4 falls by a factor in [70, 130] and a_6 by a factor in [700, 1300] from eps = 0.01 to 1e-3 (leading orders eps^2 and
eps^3; a 30 % band each for the next order).
(c) Size of the top step: a_6/a_4 = -q_4 eps within a factor 2 at both eps (-0.5675 at 0.01, -0.05675 at 1e-3); the factor 2 allows the
left-out terms at m = 4.
Falsifiers: a wrong sign in (a), a factor outside the bands in (b), or (c) off by more than 2 at either eps. Aliasing: a 16-atom near
ring folds harmonic 16 - m onto m; at m <= 6 the folded harmonic is 10 or higher, of order eps^5 or smaller, below the tested sizes.

## Amendment 1109 (2026-10-02 02:22) - correction to the reading of 1108: the optimum cannot jump

The capacity-achieving input is unique (mutual information is strictly concave in the input law for this channel), and the input set,
the ellipse, moves continuously with rm. By the maximum theorem the optimal input is then weakly continuous in rm. A new support point
must therefore enter with mass tending to zero at the event, and no existing atom can move or change mass by a finite amount there. The
"subcritical birth, then a jump" reading of 1108 cannot describe the optimum. Either the held-mass solutions on the larger-eps side
(not converged, 1e-12) are not the optimal branch, or the zero-mass entry at the 14 -> 16 event comes with a continuous change that our
trials did not seed (a pair born at 90 deg with a separation growing from zero, as at a degenerate touch). The event itself (KKT lost at
eps = 0.163205, 1103 part 1) stands. Next: held-mass solves at 160 bits with difference step 1e-14 and up to 80 Newton steps (started
02:22) to see whether the backward trend survives convergence.
Gates: no gate word used.

-2.8e-4; P 2.02, 2G (25.27, 66.11 deg), margins -9.4e-5 and -4.5e-4. On the ellipse the count goes from 6 to at least 18 over the same eps.

Reading. A superellipse with fixed P != 2 does not tend to the circle as eps -> 0; it tends to a squircle, whose optimal input at this size
is a finite D4-symmetric set (eight atoms here), so its count stays bounded. The growth of the count is a property of families that tend
to the circle, where the uniform law is the limit; the ellipse is one such family (a pure two-fold term). A proper third case is a family
r(theta) = R(1 + eps cos 4 theta) (four-fold, tending to the circle), where the flattest points are at 45 deg and births should come there.

## Amendment 1148 (2026-10-02 05:07) - 1146 PASSES; the first event of every n-fold family is set by circle data alone: depth = 2 R_n(rp)/g(rp)

(1) The n bump atoms sit on the circle r = rp for every dent depth delta, with masses 1/n by symmetry, so the n-atom state is the regular
n-gon of the circle and does not change with delta; only the points where KKT is checked move inward, by u = delta (1 - cos n t)/2.
Expanding D of the n-gon about r = rp: D - C = R_n (1 - cos n t) - g u + (higher harmonics, R_n u, u^2), so to first order
D - C = (R_n - g delta/2)(1 - cos n t). It vanishes at every t at once when delta = 2 R_n/g, where 2 R_n is the circle ripple of the
n-gon and g = dD/dr at r = rp is the radial slope of the KKT function of the uniform input on the circle.
(2) q750 (1D Rician integral for the uniform circle input): g(1.3) = 0.669971388, 1/g = 1.492601053492; g(1.2) = 0.672115137,
g(1.4) = 0.662104828.

## Amendment 1157 (2026-10-02 05:43) - BACKLOG 27: which steps of the Barletta-Dytso locality proof carry to the ellipse (ELLIPSE_LOCALITY_NOTE.md)

Read from the extracted text of arXiv 2609.10039: Lemmas 1-7, Proposition 1, Theorem 2, Corollary 1, Propositions 2-3, Theorem 3.
Carries to the ellipse boundary z(t): the KKT conditions, the entire extension in t, the local zero types (even multiplicity on a
closed curve, as their Remark 2 says these need only the KKT inequality and analyticity), weak continuity in rm, Hurwitz, and the
persistence of every nondegenerate support point (their Proposition 3 with the tangential second derivative). So on the ellipse a count
change can happen only at a degenerate support point or an inactive contact point. First failing step: Lemma 7, the global zero count
N_mul <= 2K, which rests on Karlin's oscillation theorem and the zero bound for exponential polynomials, both one-dimensional; along the
ellipse g is a 2D Gaussian transform restricted to a curve and f_Y(z(t)) is a sum of exponentials of trigonometric polynomials.
Replacement needed: a zero count 2K + s with 4 <= s < 8 (a vertex-orbit event already costs 4 units, a generic orbit 8), plus a step
excluding the major vertex. The trackers' confinement of every event to the minor vertex (four sizes, plus rp 1.0) is the empirical
side of that missing count.
Gates: no gate word used.

smallest masses (w at +-m: 0.00476 at m 18.65, 0.00059 at 40.9) and the central ones the largest (0.056 to 0.023); at fixed K the edge
mass shrinks, so S_(K-1) = 1 - (edge mass) rises. In capacity the edge carries the largest masses (the ellipse X atoms: 0.29 per atom at
rp 1.0) and they fall, which is the direction majorization needs; that matches 1155 and Barletta and Dytso's Fig. 5.
Reading for the target: majorization is a property of the capacity problem tied to where its largest masses sit, not a shared law of
the three count-law problems; the LFP's evolution between events runs the other way at its edge.

## Amendment 1187 (2026-10-02 07:26) - BACKLOG 29 closed: kappa_n derived from circle quantities; the two-stage n-fold law has no free constant

Derivation (q760). Treat the regular 2n-ring at radius r with angular density f = (1/2 pi)(1 + b_n cos n theta + ...) and output density
p = p0 (1 + h), h = sum b_m q_m(rho) cos m phi, q_m = I_m(r rho)/I_0(r rho). Along the curve s(t) = r + v(t), v = (delta/2) cos n t
(relative to the ring's radius, the ring at the mean radius):
    D = D0(s) - b_n J_n(s) cos n t + (ring ripple, 4 J_2n at the midpoints = 2 R_2n) + (1/4) b_n^2 L_n(s) cos 2n t + ...,
    J_m(s) = int rho e^{-(rho^2+s^2)/2} I_m(s rho) q_m(rho) d rho,   L_n(s) = int rho e^{-(rho^2+s^2)/2} q_n(rho)^2 I_2n(s rho) d rho.
The pairs' shift toward the bumps sets b_n = -2 sin(n alpha) so that the harmonic-n term cancels: b_n = g delta/(2 J_n). Collecting the
harmonic-2n terms of second order (the radial curvature g2 v^2/2, the cross term -b_n J_n' v cos n t, and the quadratic b_n^2 L_n/4),
the midpoint margin is 2 R_2n - kappa_n delta^2 with
    kappa_n = g J_n'/(4 J_n) - g2/8 - g^2 L_n/(8 J_n^2),
g = D0'(r), g2 = D0''(r), J_n' = dJ_n/ds at s = r; every factor is a circle integral.
Values at r = 1.3 (g 0.669971388, g2 0.6136746): kappa_n = 0.648633 (n 6), 0.911403 (8), 1.172615 (10), 1.432889 (12); measured from
the events 0.6485, 0.9118, 1.1752, 1.4334: -0.02 %... +0.02 %, -0.04 %, -0.22 %, -0.04 % (measured minus theory, relative: +0.02,
+0.04, +0.22, +0.04 %); the n = 10 value comes from a linear interpolation between ladder points 1.4e-11 and 1.6e-11. Check of the
kernel: 4 J_2n equals the q752 ripple 2 R_2n to every printed digit (2.34369e-11, 1.16939e-16, 2.38298e-22, 2.35689e-28). The leading
term g J_n'/(4 J_n) carries the factor n (J_n'/J_n = 4.39, 5.94, 7.48, 9.03), which is the near-linear law of 1184.
So for the n-fold family both stages follow from circle data with no fitted constant: delta_1 = 2 R_n/g, delta_2 = sqrt(2 R_2n/kappa_n).
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1213 (2026-10-02 08:53) - PRE-REGISTERED: the missing source term in b_2

1191 set b_2 = g eps/(2 J_2) by cancelling the shape term g (eps/2) cos 2t against the density response b_2 J_2 cos 2t, as in the n-fold
derivation (1187) where the ring sat on one circle. On the ellipse the atoms themselves sit at radius R + (eps/2) cos 2t, so the source
ring is displaced as well, and its displacement has its own harmonic-2 response H_2 (the response of D at radius s to a source ring at
radius r displaced by cos 2 theta): H_2(s) = int rho e^{-(rho^2+s^2)/2} I_2(s rho) [rho I_2'(r rho) - r I_2(r rho)]/I_0(r rho) d rho, at
s = r = R. The first-order balance becomes b_2^src = eps (g - H_2)/(2 J_2). PRE-REGISTERED (no H_2 computed yet): H_2/g lies near 0.5 at
the event radii, so that (a) K b_2^src is constant over the 22 events to 2 % at a value between 3.5 and 4.3, and (b) at the three rp 1.3
births it is within 6 % of the rings' carried modulation K beta* = 4.09, 3.78, 3.70 (1211). Fails if (a) or (b) fails.

## Amendment 1224 (2026-10-02 09:34) - a new instrument, the extremal sector of the smooth density from circle integrals; PRE-REGISTERED: its control, the large-order growth, and an event rule

Instrument (q764_extremal_series.py). Write the ellipse as z(t) = R e^{it} + eta e^{-it}, R = (rp + rm)/2, eta = eps/2, and the input
density in t as 1 + sum_k c_2k cos 2kt. Rotating the curve with t multiplies eta by e^{2i alpha}, so harmonic 2k first appears at order
eta^k, and the terms conj(eta)^k e^{2ikt} form a closed sector (set z = R e^{it}, conj(z) = R e^{-it} + eta e^{it}). In it the output
density is P_0(rho)(1 + sum Q_k w^k), w = eta e^{2i psi}, the log is a power series in w, and D along the curve has coefficients d_k
that are radial integrals of Bessel products; KKT (d_k = 0) gives a_k = d_k(a_k = 0)/J_2k(R) order by order, and c_2k = 2 a_k (eps/2)^k
at leading order. At first order this is exactly 1214: a_1 = (g - H_2)/(2 J_2) - 1/R. No 2D quadrature, no Newton, no soft modes.
Seen before this registration: a smoke run at R = 1.2184, N = 3 (a_1 1.457996, a_2 18.6636, a_3 212.734).
PRE-REGISTERED:
(C) Control: a_1 at R = 1.15675, 1.19638, 1.2184 equals 1214's beta_t/eps from its printed K beta_t (1.8194, 1.5763, 1.4591) within
0.3 % (the rounding of three printed digits); and a_30 at R = 1.2 agrees to 8 digits between 192 and 384 nodes and between RM 26 and 32.
(G) Growth: the ratios r_k = a_(k+1)/a_k for k up to at least 30 at R = 1.0, 1.2, 1.3. If r_k/k changes by less than 3 % over the last
ten computed steps, the reading is a factorial power 1 and, with the event rule below, a count K ~ const/eps; if r_k/k^(3/2) does,
power 3/2 and K ~ eps^(-2/3). Any other behaviour is reported as such.
(E) Event rule (the comb rule of 1082-1083, BACKLOG 19, in the t parametrisation): the K-ring is lost when the formal harmonic-K
coefficient falls to the comb's amplitude, |c_K(eps)| = 2 |a_(K/2)(R)| (eps/2)^(K/2) = alpha with R = rp - eps/2. Two index choices,
both scored: E_b with K = K before the event, E_a with K = K after. For each of the 26 events (rp 0.8-1.4, K after 8-18; table in
q761 plus 1193, 1216, 1219, 1222, 1223) solve the rule for eps and compare with the observed eps. E_b or E_a PASSES (shape) if
eps_obs/eps_rule is constant over the 26 events within +- 3 % with one fitted alpha; PASSES (parameter-free) if within +- 3 % of 1 at
alpha = 2. Expectation stated now: the shape test is the informative one; the extremal sector drops terms of relative order
eta conj(eta) times growth factors, which at eps 0.1-0.34 need not be small, so a level offset is likely and a trend with eps would
measure those terms.

forcing kappa_n delta^2 equals 2 J_2n c_2n, so 2 R_2n = kappa_n delta^2 is c_2n = 2 (1187). Both formulas drop terms of relative order
n delta and J_n: at n = 4 the stage-1 ratio is 1.5286 against 1/g = 1.4926 (+2.4 %, 1148), and q760 now gives kappa_4 = 0.383192, so

= sum_j (s e^{int})^j He_j(rho cos u - R)/j!, and the density coefficients a_k of harmonic nk follow order by order from radial
integrals. Comb rule: the ring of K = nk atoms is lost when 2 a_k(R) s^k = 2.

(the eight-ring at 0.18722 above the six-ring at 0.18495), so that curve needs a design that avoids the sign transitions before any
registration. Filed as BACKLOG 33.
Why it matters: on the ellipse, Theorem 4 of 2401.17084 keeps atoms at the major vertices, so a ring cannot take the anti-phase that a
negative a_k demands; on curves without that anchor the bump atom leaves exactly as the signs say (1235-1249). A near-ellipse whose
first sign change is reachable is the cheapest place to see what an anchored ring does when the rule asks for the anti-phase, which is

## Amendment 1259 (2026-10-02 11:53) - curve versus filled region; an observation about the proof of Theorem 4 of 2401.17084 (UNCHECKED against later versions)

(1) Framing. Every solve in this record constrains the input to the curve (KKT checked along it). Dytso, Barletta and Kramer's problem
(arXiv 2401.17084, text extracted to papers/bridge_cap2d3d/extract/arxiv_2401.17084v1.txt) constrains it to the filled ellipse E, with
KKT (4): D <= C on E, and (5): D = C on the support; for rp <= sqrt 2 their Theorem 3 puts the support on the boundary, so on the
ellipse the two problems have the same optimum. For other curves they need not.
(2) q782 (interior check, D by q719's rule copied as text): the polar two-fold optimum at rp 0.8, delta 0.10 (one G orbit at 30.41 deg, no
atom at (0.8, 0)) has D - C <= -2.18e-3 at all 210 interior points of a 14 x 14 polar grid of the quadrant (largest at 32.1 deg, fraction
0.995 of the boundary radius, next to the atom) and <= -4.3e-3 at 42 points on rays 0-90 deg; with (5) at its four atoms (residual
5e-33) and the curve scan of 1236, it satisfies (4)-(5) for the filled region bounded by this curve, so it is that region's optimum too
(the KKT conditions are sufficient). The farthest point of the region, (0.8, 0), carries no atom.
(3) The proof of Theorem 4 in the extracted v1 text (Section III-C) uses Lemma 7 (if Pr(X1 > t) = 0 then dD/dx1 > 0 for x1 > t, by
Tweedie's formula) and states that (53), D(x1, x2) > D(t, x2) for x1 > t, "would violate the KKT condition (4)". Lemma 7 uses nothing
specific to the ellipse, and the region of (2) is a filled, doubly symmetric region whose farthest point is unique, so the argument
as written would place (0.8, 0) in that region's support, which (2) contradicts. Where the step needs more: (53) gives D > C only at
points (x1, x2) with x1 > t whose height x2 is that of a support point with first coordinate t; those support points lie on the
boundary away from the axis, and points to their right at the same height are outside the region. Reading: the statement of
Theorem 4 for the ellipse agrees with every ellipse optimum computed in this record (the major-vertex atoms are always present), and
the step from (53) to a violation of (4) needs an ingredient specific to the ellipse that the v1 text does not state.
UNCHECKED: whether a later version or the published paper adds that ingredient; to be searched and read before this is used anywhere.
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1279 (2026-10-02 14:20) - literature gate, BACKLOG 30 and the comb rule: four more sources read from extracted text, nothing bears on it

Read from text we extracted ourselves (temporal_within/papers/litgate_comb/):
- Huleihel, Goldfeld, Koch, Madiman, Medard, ISIT 2018 (UC3M e-archivo PDF): the circle-uniform input with its phase quantized; a
  sufficient number of phase points for a small capacity backoff, and allocation of points across amplitude circles. The constraint
  region stays a disc; no curve other than the circle, no KKT ripple, no Bessel terms.
- Bernardo, Zhu, Evans, arXiv 2106.11007: phase quantization at the output; the optimum is a rotated 2^b-PSK. Output-side, not a
  perturbed input constraint.
- Favano, Ferrari, Magarini, Barletta, arXiv 2101.08643: norm-bounded MIMO; concentric spheres, a lower bound on their number and an
  iterative algorithm. Rotation-invariant region only.
- Favano et al., arXiv 2111.13179: sphere-packing upper bound for an arbitrary convex amplitude region (Minkowski sums, intrinsic
  volumes of ellipsoids). A capacity bound only; nothing about the support.
- Chan, Hranilovic, Kschischang, IEEE T-IT 51(6) 2005: the support is sparse for bounded inputs, concentric shells when the region is
  a ball. No statement about atom counts on a curve.
Not readable: Favano's PhD thesis (politesi.polimi.it) answers with a Cloudflare challenge; not bypassed. Its papers above are the
published parts we could reach.
Verdict for BACKLOG 30 and the comb rule: none of these treats a peak region that departs from the circle, the ripple of the KKT
function, or a count change of the ring. The gate stays partial (thesis unread; ISIT 2024 version of 2401.17084 behind
authentication).
Gates: no gate word used.

## Amendment 1280 (2026-10-02 14:36) - PRE-REGISTERED, blind: a bridge test of the comb rule on a second problem, the least favourable prior for a normal mean on the ellipse

Bigger fact under test. The comb rule (1224-1249) says a K-ring is lost when the formal smooth density's harmonic K reaches what the
ring itself supplies (2, the Dirac comb's amplitude). Only the coefficients a_k belong to the problem; the threshold belongs to the
comb. If that is right, the rule must hold with the same threshold for any problem whose KKT function makes a ring on the ellipse,
with that problem's own a_k. Second problem: X ~ N(theta, I_2) with theta known to lie on the ellipse (rp, rm), squared-error loss;
the least favourable prior (LFP) maximises the Bayes risk, and its KKT function is the risk of the posterior mean,
r(theta) = E|delta(theta + Z) - theta|^2 <= B on the curve, = B on the support. On the circle the uniform prior is least favourable by
rotation invariance, as uniform input is capacity-achieving there.

Instrument (validated before any LFP solve):
- q784_sector_numeric.py (sha256 d11120f6...): the extremal sector of q764 computed by direct numerical evaluation of a KKT function at
  complexified positions (z = R e^{it}, zb = R e^{-it} + eta e^{it}), with the harmonic-2k coefficient fixed to zero order by order.
  Rotation covariance makes that coefficient linear in A_k = a_k eta^k with an eta-free slope, so any small eta gives the same a_k.
  Check against the independent radial-Bessel derivation q764 at R 1.0 (capacity): equal in all 16 printed digits for k = 1-12
  (a_1 3.213278432580704 ... a_12 7.938425591861421e18). Plane quadrature 96 x 96 nodes, 256 bits; Gaussian normalisation error 5e-61.
- LFP at R 1.0: a_1 0.2969015011651190, a_2 13.75739989123640, a_3 155.9086819202327, a_4 2324.488202624800, a_5 42661.22944911021,
  a_6 974475.1771242425, a_7 26218757.32973813, a_8 846664098.5120159, ..., a_12 3.217382781906479e15, all positive; identical in every
  printed digit at eta 0.01 and 0.005 (q784/lfp_R1.0_eta*.log). They differ from the capacity values (a_4 29645, a_8 1.39e11): the
  LFP needs its harmonics less, so its rings change at larger eps.
- q786_lfp_wallchain.py (sha256 a77e5556...): copy of q719 with the Bayes risk and its score-form gradient on the separable
  Gauss-Hermite rule. Check: two-atom prior at +-0.8 on the x axis, where the posterior mean is 0.8 tanh(0.8 x): risk at (0.8, 0) equals
  the 50-digit quadrature of the closed form within 4.7e-19 (150 nodes) and 2.9e-22 (200 nodes); gradient equal at (0.8, 0) and
  (0.3, 0.5) to 12 digits. q787 (q738 with this risk), pf_sweep_lfp.py, q788 (q771 with q786/q787) are text copies for the tracking.

## Amendment 1283 (2026-10-02 14:56) - why the bridge failed: capacity rings follow the smooth density below harmonic K to six digits, least-favourable-prior rings do not

Three checks, each able to fail, run after 1282:
1. The ring side of the rule is the same for both problems. Regular K-ring on the circle R 0.93 (q719 / q786 KKT functions, 200
   nodes): KKT value at a midpoint minus at an atom, against the linear response 4 |slope_(K/2)| from q784 at R 0.93:
   capacity K 6 8.0590e-6 vs 8.0583e-6, K 8 1.8397e-8 vs 1.8397e-8, K 12 2.7571e-14 vs 2.7571e-14; LFP K 6 8.0079e-5 vs 8.0067e-5,
   K 8 2.4821e-7 vs 2.4821e-7, K 12 5.7152e-13 vs 5.7152e-13. Linear response holds for the comb in both problems.
2. The shape side is not the cause either. q790_full_numeric.py (new, sha256 b7eae924...; the full formal density on the real ellipse, all orders in
   eps, Newton on its cosine coefficients until the KKT harmonics are below 1e-40): LFP at rp 1.0, eps 0.143045: c_2 0.10256,
   c_4 0.21652, c_6 0.21451, c_8 0.28280, c_10 0.45654; c_6 agrees with the extremal value 0.2135 of 1282 within 0.5 %.
3. The premise of the rule fails for the LFP. Ring harmonics b_j = 2 sum m cos(j t) of the pre-event state against the full c_j:
   - capacity rp 1.3, K 10 at eps 0.207240: b 0.331127, 0.451148, 0.561937, 0.914573 (j 2-8) vs c 0.331126, 0.451144, 0.561959,
     0.916714; j = 10: b 1.74795, c 1.88080.
   - capacity rp 1.3, K 12 at eps 0.182742: b 0.278672, 0.330040, 0.352378, 0.491135, 0.858484 (j 2-10) vs c 0.278671, 0.330038,
     0.352374, 0.491137, 0.859105; j = 12: b 1.75566, c 1.78872.
   - LFP rp 1.0, K 6 at eps 0.143045: b_2 0.0350 vs c_2 0.1026; b_4 0.8815 vs c_4 0.2165; b_6 1.6353 vs c_6 0.2145.
   - LFP rp 1.0, K 8 at eps 0.08375 (valid ring, G 54.81 deg, masses 0.18108 / 0.11707 / 0.10093): b 2-8 -0.0151, 0.5673,
     0.9471, 1.3538 vs c 0.0438, 0.0617, 0.0328, 0.0230.
Reading. The comb rule assumes that a ring copies the smooth density at every harmonic below its own and differs only by its comb.
Capacity rings do so to five or six digits right up to the event; the rule then follows from linear response (check 1), which is
why it held within 2 % there. LFP rings break that premise by factors of 3 to 10 at low harmonics: they are irregular rings whose
KKT function is shaped by low harmonics into a nonpositive function vanishing at the atoms, far from the uniform state. Their count
grows much more slowly (K 8 from eps 0.143 to at least 0.064 at rp 1.0; the registered rule with the LFP a_k gives K 16 already at 0.127).
Consequence for the HIGHEST TARGET: on near-circular curves the count law is not shared by capacity and the LFP, unlike the 1D
count law. The comb rule's domain is now stated by a measurable test (b_j = c_j for j < K), not by the problem's name.

## Amendment 1285 (2026-10-02 15:01) - PRE-REGISTERED, blind: the comb rule on a third problem, the NPMLE / rate-distortion dual with centres on the ellipse, at the source width where its a_k alternate

Problem: the population N(0, s^2 I) with s = 0.5 is fitted by a mixture of unit-variance Gaussians whose centres lie on the ellipse
(rp 1.0, rm = 1 - eps); maximise int log f_G dP (the NPMLE; by Yang 2310.18908 and Rose 1994 the dual of rate-distortion). KKT:
E_Y[phi(Y - theta)/p(Y)] <= 1 on the curve, = 1 on the support. On the circle the uniform mixing measure is optimal by symmetry.
Why this case. Its extremal a_k (q784, eta-free) alternate in sign at R 1.0: -76.23, 10230.9, -2327844, 7.567e8, -3.336e11, 1.793e14,
-1.132e17, 7.674e19, ... (s 0.5; q784/rd_R1.0_sscan.txt), so (-1)^k a_k > 0 for every k computed: the smooth density's harmonics all
peak at the MINOR vertex. The rule then says the minor-vertex atom is anchored and every count change happens at the MAJOR vertex,
the opposite of the capacity and LFP ellipses; with K = 2 mod 4 there is no major-vertex atom (X birth there), with K = 0 mod 4 there
is one (X split there). The magnitudes are 24 (k 1) to 25 000 (k 4) times the capacity values at the same R: strong shape forcing. Whether
strong forcing goes with the copying regime of 1283 is open; this case tests it. A pass supports 'the rule holds wherever rings copy
the smooth density, whatever the problem'; a fail of place would mean the sign rule itself does not carry.
Seen before registering (states above every scored event, recorded so): at eps 0.05 the X + Y guess gave a negative X mass, and the
two-atom Y structure is KKT-valid (scan maximum 0 at the atom, rd05/s0, s1).
Registered predictions (q785 from q784 rd at 256 bits, SRC_S 0.5, rule 2 |a_(K/2)| (eps/2)^(K/2) = 2 with R = rp - eps/2):
| K before | eps | R | a_(K/2) | kind and place (rotated sign rule) |
| 6 | 0.014783744 | 0.992608 | -2475920.3 | X birth at the major vertex (reported, not scored: smallest ring) |

| 16 | 0.0064769416 | 0.996762 | 8.2657094e19 | X split at the major vertex |
(q785 prints 'Y birth / Y split at the minor vertex if a_k > 0'; with (-1)^k a_k > 0 the roles of the vertices swap, as stated.)

## Amendment 1310 (2026-10-02 17:36) - copying rings satisfy the KKT equations to 1e-11 before any solve; why Newton then stalls; the K 12 kind of s 2 left unresolved so far

Diagnostic solves (q786 / q789 at 110 bits, NGH 200) started from q796 copying rings:
- LFP rp 1.0, twelve-ring at eps 0.160: KKT residual at iteration 0 (no Newton step yet) 7.6e-12.
- NPMLE s 2, fourteen-ring at eps 0.284: residual at iteration 0 3.0e-11.
The same rings at 160 bits behave alike. So the ring built only from the smooth density's harmonics 2..K-2 already satisfies D = C at
every orbit and zero tangential derivative at every G atom to about 1e-11, away from any event as well as at events (1289-1308):
the copying premise holds along the whole branch, at intermediate eps as at the event.
Newton then stalls (residual flat near those values for 20-30 iterations): what is left lies in the direction that changes the
ring's own harmonic K, which costs only the response at harmonic K (slope of order 1e-13 here), so the Jacobian is nearly singular
there and the damped step cannot use it. Continuation from converged neighbours does not have this problem; the trackers resume that
