Results quoted from the readings. The block B131 passes with 8 of 8 events, with a largest deviation of 0.6399e-9 and no violation, after the event K_b 136 arrived from the chain 135c at 12:14:35. The registered predictions for K_b 136 hold: the frozen pair misses by -2.160e-12, the cell (14, 14) by +8.527e-14 and the Aitken extrapolation by +0.000e+00. K_b 140 and 142 came from the GPU walk and K_b 141 from a chain, and all their registered bars hold. The GPU and chain events agree to 3.0e-18 at K_b 141, to 1.0e-18 at K_b 138 and to 8.073e-15 at K_b 139. With the bulk law through c28 the self-consistent pair of the exact N = 90 block differs from the births pair by 6.345e-11 in nu0 on the window 30..60, and the pair is the same at N = 120 to 1.1e-13. Through c30 the difference is 3.222e-11. The one-order ratio of the pair steps is 0.4043 and then 0.4360. All 22 lower births K_b 61 to 82 are re-measured with the arb walker. The shifts are below 5.0e-13 except K_b 73, whose shift is +1.112e-11, and with the corrected amplitudes the model difference is a smooth monotone sequence from -10.6e-12 to -0.6e-12 whose logarithm is linear in v^2 with the slope -0.1287. The deviation of the inner atoms from the c28 law falls with the ratio 0.70 per atom from k = 12 to 30.

ERRATA. (1) Reading 164 and the status paragraph of 11:53 give the window 45..75 differences of the N = 90 run as +9.2e-12 and -8.5e-12. They were subtracted by hand from the pair printed to 12 decimals. The stored result file gives +9.601e-12 and -8.804e-12, and reading 167 carries the correction. (2) Reading 171 compared the arb amplitude of K_b 73 with the older file tower_K74_As.json of 7 Oct, because the docstring of q1710 and q1711 named it, and reported +4.497e-12. The births model of q1671 uses the repaired file tower_K74_As2.json of 8 Oct, and against it the shift is +1.112e-11. With the arb value the model difference at K_b 73 is -2.3e-12, on the trend of its neighbours. By the registered letter the outcome (c) of q1711 stands, because its reference was the older file. Against the file that the model uses, the shift lies within 3e-13 of the 11.4e-12 that the outcome (b) names, but that reference was not the registered one. Reading 174 carries the correction. A status paragraph of 12:24 and a final report repeated the wrong numbers, and a correcting paragraph was written at 12:30. (3) The readings 163 and 169 quote the predictions for K_b 139 to 141 from the pair fitted before K_b 136 was included. Reading 172 gives the values after the refit, which differ by up to five float64 steps. Both sets hold their bars.

Control failures and repairs. The first run of q1710 ended VOID, because its control used the default Newton tolerance of 1e-30 and stopped at a residual of 4.70e-47, while the registered bar was 4.5e-55. The repair q1711 solves with the tolerance 1e-54 and keeps the bars. The root finder of q1715 crashed in its first version and returned spurious roots near zero in the second. It was repaired in the root finder only, and the predictions and bars did not change. The predictions S1 and C2 of q1698 and the prediction P3 of the registration text of Q90 were revised before any output existed, as reading 161 and amendment 2224 state.

Bars not met by the letter, taken from the label lines of the scripts. q1709: P1, P2, P3; q1712: P1, P2; q1713: P3; q1714: P1; q1715: P2.

Results quoted from the readings. (1) GPU. The walk stopped at the birth K_b 142 because the Newton iteration of the odd start stagnates near 1e-19, far above the acceptance level 1e-30. With the new switch Q1411_BIRTH_TOL = 1e-17 the run 7 passed that birth and delivered K_b 143 and K_b 144. It made 843 Newton calls with 0 failed calls, a maximum arb residual of 4.5e-55 and a maximum GPU temperature of 51.0 C. K_b 144 entered under rule R1, and the blocks B115, B123 and B131 pass with largest deviations of 0.0338e-9, 0.1517e-9 and 0.6399e-9. The registered readouts hold at K_b 143 and 144: the cell (14, 14) gives +8.527e-14 at both, the full series gives -2.842e-13 and -3.126e-13, and the Aitken model gives +5.684e-14 and +4.263e-14. The run 7 ended at the birth K_b 144. Three odd starts passed the residual test with D''(0) = +2.393e-18, +1.586e-18 and +9.576e-19, while the starts at K_b 138, 140 and 142 had -2.633e-23, -1.792e-23 and -1.222e-23. The walker returns an odd start only for a negative D''(0). The run 8 was registered at 13:10:52 (gpu_run8_prereg_2026-10-10.txt, sha256 7e6f0f22138a9ffb) with the new default-off switch Q1411_BIRTH_POLISH and started at 13:11. At 13:17 the log showed a first odd start of D''(0) = -8.352e-24 after the birth K_b 144. The formal labels follow with the script q1743 when the run ends, and no label of run 8 is given here. At 13:42 the folder fw_gpu_cap2 holds the event file K_b 145, which is not transferred under rule R1 until its verify record exists and the run has ended.
(2) Aitken extrapolation over the bulk order. With the 22 lower births re-measured, the model agrees with every amplitude from K_b 61 to 138 to within 0.21e-12. The wall pair of the middle range is the better one, since adding the lower births shifts it by 3.5e-11. The extrapolation holds for the triple c24 to c28 and overshoots by up to 1.6e-12 for the triple c26 to c30, and the fixed ratio beats the ratio of each K.
(3) Inner deviation and pair sequences. The deviation of the exact atoms from the c28 law is the truncation of the bulk series and the compensation of the pair fit, and it needs no separate exponential sector. The steps of the ladder pair equal the negative window fit of the added bulk term to 0.2 percent, and those of the births pair to 1 percent and 6 percent. The limit wall pair from the bulk series alone is (-0.0937736508471, +0.0011599160174) with the ratio model A and (-0.0937736508483, +0.0011599160185) with the model B, and it meets the births limit to the level of 1e-11. The bulk coefficients grow like j! / 32.3^j, and the rate is within 2 percent of the Stokes rate 32.96.
(4) Fit-free amplitudes. With the wall pair of the exact block, the bulk series and no fitted amplitude, K_b 83 to 130 are predicted with an rms of 8e-14 to 1e-13 and K_b 131 to 142 within 1e-13. With the law through NG = 17, K_b 76 and 82 are predicted to 1.4e-14 and 7e-15. With the stored centre series to order 20 and NG = 18, K_b 61 to 82 are predicted within 2.49e-13, K_b 83 to 130 with an rms of 4.78e-14 and K_b 131 to 143 within 1.14e-13. The best NG rises with the centre order. The later events cannot separate NG 17 to 22, and the best NG by the later events is 16, 17 and 19 for the centre orders 16, 18 and 20. With two guessed centre terms the best NG at K_b 61 is 18, 19 and 19 to 20 for the orders 20, 21 and 22, and the overshoot at NG 22 shrinks by a factor near 0.63 per term. In the ratio model the smallest bulk term sits at n = 29 for k = 30 and at n = 41 for k = 60, so NG near 18 is not the point of optimal truncation. The tail beyond n = 18 is 2.30 times the term n = 18 at k = 30. The residual of the exact atoms is below the Stokes level 16 pi^2 t_min(k) at k = 30 to 34, with the ratio 0.2 to 0.34. It is above that level from k = 36, with the ratio 27.1 at k = 45 and 7.67e3 at k = 60.
(5) Centre series. The increments of the ratios e_n / e_(n-1) do not follow a 1/n expansion on n = 14 to 20, and the hypothesis of the same singularity as the bulk series is undecided. A logarithm in the large-order law is not supported on n = 10 to 17. The e_n are polynomials in pi^2 with all even powers from 0 to 2n-2. The top coefficient changes sign at n = 8 and has no rational ratio law, and the ratios of the constant coefficients are smooth near 5.6.

Results quoted from the readings. (1) The e_n and the bulk coefficients. The coefficients at the distances 0, 1 and 2 from the top power of pi in the exact e_n have no rational ratio law of degree (2, 2). They are not lambda^n times a polynomial for lambda = 8, 1/8, 16, 4, 2 and 1. The ratios of the m = 1 sequence settle near 12.8 at n = 8 and 9. The bulk coefficients F_j are polynomials in u = 1/pi^2. Their top coefficient is exactly (1/8)^j for j = 2 to 15. The coefficient of u^(j-1) times 8^j is -j (j-1) (6 j^3 + j^2 - 19 j + 16) / 90, found on j = 2 to 10 and confirmed exactly on j = 11 to 15, which were not used. The coefficient of u^(j-2) times 8^j is j (j-1) (j-2) (j-3) R(j) / 340200 with R of degree 6, with five independent checks once the absent powers at j = 0 to 3 are imposed. The bottom coefficients at the lowest power are negative for j = 2 to 15. They have no ratio law of degree (1, 1), no single rational function of degree (2, 2), no linear parity model, and no per-parity polynomial or (2, 1) rational ratio law. Their numerators carry 17 prime factors above 31 and their denominators none.
(2) The logarithm of the generating function. In x = u t / 8 the logarithm has the coefficient 1/(n 8^n) at u^n for n = 1 to 15. Its next level is -(n-1) n (n+1) (3 n^2 - 8 n + 6) / (9 n 8^n), a polynomial of degree 5 with 8 checks. The reciprocal series has levels of degree 3 and 8. The first levels are rational functions. The log level 1 is N(x) / (1-x)^5 with N = (2/3) x^2 (1+x) (x^2 - 6 x - 1). In w = 1/(1-x) it is the polynomial -8 w^5 + 76 w^4 / 3 - 28 w^3 + 34 w^2 / 3 - 2/3. The log level 2 was predicted from the F level 2 by F = exp(L) and confirmed on n = 11 to 15 as a polynomial of degree 10 with five checks. In y = x/(1-x) the level k spans the powers y^(2k) to y^(5k), and the diagonal coefficients d_k from the bottom series are -2/3, -14/9, -1856/81, -270652/405, -4285088/135, -24054628096/10935 and -50598400000/243 for k = 1 to 7. The coefficients d_1 and d_2 equal the lowest coefficients of L_1 and L_2, which checks the code and adds no data. The levels 0 to 2 reproduce ln of the exact partial sum of the bulk law at rho = 1 with the relative error 1.129e-5, which is 1.3e-7 in absolute terms.
(3) The prospective tests. The ratio d_1(11)/d_1(10) of the exact e_11 was registered at 13:47:41 to lie in the band 12.72222 to 12.96222 (centre_scripts/q1754_prereg_d1_ratio.txt, evaluator q1755). The exact f32 = F_16 was registered at 14:00:02: the coefficient of pi^-32 is 1/8^16, that of pi^-30 times 8^16 is -196352/3, that of pi^-28 times 8^16 is 1845151984/15, and the lowest power is pi^-16 (small_gap_q206/q1765_prereg_f32.txt, evaluator q1766). The exact run for f32 was started at about 14:00:30 (py q1557_f12_symbolic.py 32, below normal priority, guard f32_memwatch.ps1) after the symbol f32 was added to q1557_f12_symbolic.py with a backup. The run for e_11 and the GPU run 8 are still going, and no label of any of the three exists at the time of writing.

The scripts print maxima only for K_b 61 to 82 (0.21e-12) and K_b 131 to 138 (0.085e-12), and for the 48 births K_b 83 to 130 they print an rms of 3.1e-14. Labels of the scripts. Script q1785 did not hold its prediction P2 in the first run and is a defective test (see the slips). Script q1786 holds P1, P2 and P3. Script q1787 is VOID by its registered control C1. Script q1788 is VOID by its controls in the first run. Script q1789 holds P2a, P2b, P2c and P2d. Script q1790 never finished. Script q1791 holds P1, P2, P3 and P4. Script q1792 is VOID by its control C1. Unless a reading says otherwise, these scripts were written after earlier outputs had been read and are not blind. Their predictions are in their docstrings.

Results quoted from the readings. (1) The quadrature lemma of the ring certificate. A complete written proof now exists. It reproduces the constants 4 (1 + eta), 1.6, 0.7979 and 0.484 of the printed statement, and it adds two hypotheses that the sketch left unstated: the atoms lie within the radius r_p, and the sum of the weights is at least 1/4. The sanity script q1786 finds no violation of the strip bound in 20000 instances, none of the quadrature bound in 300 instances, and none of the Gaussian-sum inequalities. Of the 300 instances, 241 had a bound above the floor 2e-13, with a worst ratio of observed error to bound of 8.743e-03, and 59 had a bound below the floor, with a largest observed error of 1.667e-16.
(2) The first draft check. A reader with no project context read the proof of the quadrature lemma and reported 0 FATAL, 0 GAP, 3 MINOR and 7 COSMETIC findings. We verified all ten and repaired the text.
(3) The deformation identity of the planar NPMLE. Steps 1 to 3 are now a proposition with a complete argument, valid for a bounded open set with C^1 boundary and a deformation x + eps V. The numerical test q1787 with the grid solver is VOID, because the disc control has a relative difference of 1.463e-02, above the registered 1e-02. The ellipse deformations differ by 2.196e-03 and 1.133e-02.
(4) The strong-G2 corollary. The corollary was audited internally twice before. Its chain with explicit constants holds on 54 certified states (q1789), with E2/c* up to 0.2426, a worst chain ratio of 3.303e-04 and a worst ratio of eta e^(Lambda/3) to the explicit constant of 0.0596. The first output q1788 was VOID because the centre atom of odd-K states was dropped and two controls were badly conceived.
(5) The second draft check. A reader read the deformation identity and the strong-G2 note and reported 0 FATAL, 2 GAP, 6 MINOR and 9 COSMETIC findings. We verified all 17. The gaps were a citation of Danskin's theorem whose cited form does not match, now replaced by a complete proof, and the step from the curvature expansion to the local law, which needs a remainder whose shape derivative is small. One constant (C1 at most 2.58) was false at the top of its range and now reads 2.59.
(6) The lower-bound constants. In interval arithmetic (q1791) the bootstrap check holds at 4000 points with a smallest margin of 0.00122480, J(1.1648) is negative, and the liminf constants are 0.1660754212 for the capacity and 0.07596985678 for the NPMLE. The numbers 0.1661 and 0.0760 that earlier notes carried are roundings up, so they are not valid lower bounds. The valid decimal statements are 0.1660 and 0.0759. In the printed text of paper 1 the numbers occur only in a comment line. The tail p >= 1e7 of the bootstrap and the derivations of the lemmas were not rechecked.
(7) The one-minimum lemma. A complete written proof now exists, based on a zero-count lemma for exponential polynomials proved by Rolle induction, the variation-diminishing property of the Gaussian kernel (quoted), and two literature hypotheses. The re-read of the stored counts in q1792 shows no mismatch in 25 lines of q1363 and 48 lines of q1366. The script is VOID by its control C1, with no violation found among 500 step functions, 226 of which reach equality.

Parking and its partial lift. The research was parked at about 15:00 and the background jobs were left to run to completion without being read. At about 15:10 the parking was lifted for the nearly finished proofs only. The jobs for the exact f32, the exact e_11 and the GPU run 8 still run unread, and the registrations of amendments 2227 to 2229 stay in force. The file with the exact f32 has grown during this period and was not opened.

The merge order. At about 16:05 the author ordered paper 1 and paper 3 merged into one paper once the finished items are finished. The order asks for a new abstract, a new title where needed and the next plan. After that come two draft readers and the repository with all its gates. The plan is UNIFIED_PAPER_PLAN_2026-10-10.md. This reverses our advice of 14:20 and 15:12, and the decision is the author's.

Slips. (1) The first run of q1785 flagged 29 of 300 quadrature instances as violations, with observed over bound up to 2.650e+26. The bounds were near 1e-40, below the rounding noise of a double-precision grid sum. The first output is kept and the repair q1786 adds a floor. (2) The first run of q1788 was VOID: the centre atom of the odd-K state was dropped, the control C2 reached a ratio of 18 against the bar of 100, and the control C3 was conceived the wrong way round. ## Amendment 2240 (2026-10-11 03:12) - LITERATURE CHECK of Smith (1971) and of the introduction, two sentences of the appendices replaced, and a rerun of the pipeline; executed record

Scope. This entry covers readings 255 and 256, three text replacements in app_lower.tex and app_min.tex, and one more run of the pipeline. Each reading is a script or a table with no verdict word. The registered predictions of the two readings are in the task and in the docstring of q1808.

Reading 255, text of Smith (1971). A reader without the project files fetched the text of Smith (1971) and of Wang (2025) and wrote the table paper_unified/referee/r4_literature.md, with 11 rows STATED, 3 NOT STATED and 2 UNCHECKED. The text of Smith came from a web archive snapshot of an open copy, because the live pages answered with a bot check, which the reader did not pass. The table lists existence, uniqueness, finite support and the Kuhn-Tucker condition in both directions as STATED, and symmetry of the optimal input as NOT STATED. A grep of the OCR text of Smith for symmetry and extreme points printed two lines: line 543, about the pair of mass points at the extremes for small A, and line 700, a footnote about zero mean. The text of Wang prints in Theorem 1 that K_A divided by A tends to infinity and gives no exponent. The Smith thesis of 1969 is UNCHECKED.

Prediction that failed by the letter. The queue prediction of reading 255, that the texts support the sentences of Appendix A and of the introduction, held for uniqueness, finiteness, the Kuhn-Tucker pair, the sentence on discreteness in the introduction and the sentence on Wang. It failed for two sentences: app_lower.tex wrote that Smith gives symmetry, and app_min.tex wrote that Smith gives symmetry and the atoms at plus and minus A.

Repairs. The script paper_unified/apply_lit_repairs.py made 3 replacements, one in app_lower.tex and two in app_min.tex. Both sentences now cite Smith for uniqueness and finiteness. Symmetry follows in the text from the invariance of the channel and the constraint under x to minus x and from uniqueness. In app_min.tex the Preliminaries add that the posterior mean is below the largest atom a, so D' of x exceeds x minus a, which is not negative for x at least a, and that a below A would make D exceed C just above a. So A is an atom, and by symmetry so is minus A. No number of the paper changed. The new sentences are draft proof text.

Reading 256 (q1808), five statements of the introduction. The script prints lines of local texts. The docstring registered P1 to P5 before the first run, and P5 was marked as seen by a grep a few minutes earlier. P1, P4 and P5 held. P2 and P3 failed with the registered patterns, because the text file of the paper by Barletta and Dytso on near-optimal inputs drops the square-root glyph and the Mattingly file is a single line. The variants S2b and S3b, added after that run, matched. S2b prints from page 1 of the PDF that K_epsilon(A) is of order A sqrt(log A) for polynomially decaying epsilon. S3b prints the scaling law MI of order 3/4 log K from the Mattingly text. The step from that law to K of order A to the power 4/3 needs capacity of order log A, which the printed line does not contain. The line 21 of the Abbott and Machta text prints its exponent flattened, and the script does not resolve how it reads in the typeset original.

## Amendment 2241 (2026-10-11 03:37) - executed record

Scope. Amendment 2240 covers readings 255 and 256 and the three replacements in app_lower.tex and app_min.tex. This entry covers six further readings, q1809 to q1814. Reading 257 (q1809). Page 1 of the PDF of Abbott and Machta (arXiv:1710.09351v2) was extracted with PyMuPDF and rendered. The extracted text carries the exponent of the abstract as the plain characters 4/3, in one span of size 6.97, the smallest size on the page. The rendered page shows the abstract sentence as log K of order I to the power 4/3. The body prints I of order 3/4 log K as equation (1) and K of order L to the power D over zeta, with zeta equal to 3/4, as equation (20). The abstract and equation (1) differ in form, and the reading does not decide which one the authors intend.

Reading 258 (q1811). Sympy prints the Fisher information of the Gaussian location family as 1 and the Fisher length of [-A, A] as 2A. The numerical half of the check integrates the constant 1 and checks only the interval length.

Reading 259 (q1810). The script lists 47 bibliography keys of unified.tex and supplement.tex against 98 local text files. With a match rule on file names and title words, 20 keys have a local text and 27 have none. The registered prediction that at most 10 keys without an arXiv number have a local text did not hold: 13 did. A look at the first lines of the matched files, made by eye, found that nine of the matches by title words were wrong, among them Smith1971 and DYPS2020, and that IHT2011 has no local text. The OCR text of Smith (1971) from reading 255 was copied into papers/.

Reading 260 (q1812). Theorem 1 of Dytso, Yagli, Poor and Shamai (arXiv:1901.03264v4) prints, on page 3, that the optimal input is a symmetric discrete distribution. It prints a lower bound equal to the square root of 1 plus 2A squared over pi e and an upper bound a2 A squared plus a1 A plus a0. The square root over the whole expression was confirmed on a rendered clip of the page, because the extracted text drops the radical.

Reading 261 (q1813). A Blahut-Arimoto run of 20000 iterations on 2001 input points gives, for A = 1.5, 3.0 and 5.0, the capacities 0.5267772455, 0.8813532127 and 1.2188199676 nats. The end masses are 0.499931, 0.352966 and 0.250160. The largest value of D minus I on the grid is 6.104e-08, 2.664e-05 and 2.431e-05. The largest symmetry defect is 1.8e-13. D minus I at the points A plus 0.05 k, k = 1 to 10, is positive and increasing for each A. The optima have 2, 4 and 5 atoms. The symmetric output is built into the program, so the symmetry defect checks the arithmetic only.

Reading 262 (q1814). Page 3 of arXiv:1005.3889v2 (Ikeda, Hayashi and Tanaka), downloaded into papers_dl/arxiv_1005_3889, prints pSNR equal to Emax over sigma squared, and equation (1) on page 2 prints the noise as sigma over root 2 times two standard normal components. From these definitions the radius root Emax in units of the per-dimension noise standard deviation is root of 2 pSNR for the circular constraint. The grid points of Fig. 5(a) read in the Notes were not checked.

Predictions that failed by the letter. In reading 259 the prediction P2 failed, as stated. In reading 262 the prediction P2, that the caption names pSNR in dB, failed, because the pattern searched Fig. 5 and the caption starts with Figure. In reading 260 and in reading 261 the first predictions held with a weakness stated in the reading: the radical test found the glyph in a2, and the symmetry is built into the program.

Failures on the way. Two time stamps of readings 257 and 258 were first written from a guess and were corrected after the clock showed 03:25. The first run of q1810 matched titles too loosely, and a second variant was not enough. A print line of q1810 was broken when the script was patched through a heredoc, and the repaired script was rerun. A command python with no input was started once and ended at once without output.

## Amendment 2244 (2026-10-13 19:39) - recomputed numbers, a readability gate with general writing rules, a reading of the whole paper, repairs of wording, and the closed form of the gap to the Abbott-Machta constant; executed record

Scope. All are readings with no verdict word on the paper, and each registers its predictions or its rules before its first run on the paper. The text of the paper changed in wording only; no number of the paper changed.

Reading 277 (q1829). An independent recomputation gives rho = 2.90902789532 and the constant of Theorem 1 as 0.166075421166. It also gives the sign change of J of Lemma g2(c) between 1.1647 and 1.1648, the total mass of the 32-atom ring, the edge numbers e_2 to e_4 and the two count constants. In the stored certified state with K = 40 at A = 29.85, the spacing of the atoms grows from 1.181 at the center to 2.719 next to the wall. This contradicts a sentence of Section 4.1, which said that the atoms crowd near the two ends.

Section 6 of writing/PAPER_RULES_ITSOC.md now records general writing rules with their sources: Knuth, Larrabee and Roberts (1987), Halmos (1970), Mermin (1989), Jaffe and Quinn (1993) and the ethical guidelines of the AMS. These are sentences that start with a formula, formulas separated only by a comma, logic symbols, incomplete text before a theorem, displays without punctuation, undefined abbreviations and words such as obviously. On its first full run the gate listed 92 hard findings (K1 9, K2 71, M1 1, A1 3 in the paper; K2 5, M1 1, A1 2 in the Notes). The paper and the Notes were then read in full and every proof in the paper was followed step by step. The findings are listed in writing/REVIEW_WITH_CONTEXT_2026-10-13.md: one error of fact, five claims whose wording says more than the evidence, several letters with more than one meaning, and the gate items.

Repairs. The script apply_review_repairs.py made byte-equal backups and replaced each target exactly once. It repaired the sentence on the spacing of the atoms, the nine sentences that started with a formula and the display without punctuation in the paper. It also spelled out FLINT and paraphrased the quotation that used KKT. The first paragraph of the Notes now defines LFP and NPMLE.

Not applied. The 76 pairs of formulas separated only by a comma are listed with a proposed word in writing/k2_proposals.txt, by a dry run that changed no file of the paper. These choices are made and applied in the next steps. The five claims are handled by first raising their evidence: an enclosure of the exact states, an out-of-sample test, and a closed form. Their wording is narrowed only where the evidence is still missing at release.

Reading 279 (q1830). The paper writes log 56 times and ln 10 times; ln occurs only in line 414 and in lines 1061 to 1063 of unified_flat.tex, all for the natural logarithm.

Reading 280 (q1831). Of the six numbered labels that the gate reports as never referenced, eq:curve is referenced in a caption and in a table note, which the gate does not read; 5 have no reference in the paper or the Notes.

Reading 281 (q1832). The ratio of the Abbott-Machta count constant to the constant of the paper is (6/pi^2)^(1/6) = 0.92039711952907552433 at 50 digits. A factor 2 in the length would change the constant by 2^(4/3), so the full length against the half-length cannot account for the 8 percent; the gap sits in the prefactor of the density law. The review document had suggested the length convention, and that suggestion was withdrawn in it.

Limits. The reading of the whole paper was made by the same process that wrote much of its text, so it is not an independent review. The literature items marked UNCHECKED in amendment 2243 stay UNCHECKED.

## Amendment 2245 (2026-10-13 21:10) - stronger evidence for five claims, the title, readability rules, a citation gate; executed record

Scope. Claims whose wording said more than their evidence are handled first by raising the evidence.

Widening the grid from A plus or minus 9 to A plus or minus 40 moves the stored state by at most 7.916e-19, and halving the step changes nothing above 1e-141; the initial minors of X stay positive (q1833). On the strip of half-width 0.5 the output density has no zero, with a smallest margin of 0.37614 (q1834). The trapezoid and truncation errors of the residual and of the Jacobian are at most 8.3610e-132 and 4.1226e-134 (q1835). A Krawczyk test on the system with these errors shows that a box of radius 1e-110 holds exactly one solution, within 3.439e-123 of the computed state, and all 380 initial minors of X are certainly positive over that box (q1836).

Readings 286 and 287. Over a state widened by 1e-17 the error bounds still hold, and the bound for D, D' and D'' at any point of [0, A] is 5.023e-134. The scan for D below C on [0, A] in q1837 was stopped by its timeout of 3000 s before any box was reported, so its optimality part is void. A profile with floating midpoints (q1838) gives D''(0) = 1.396303e-10 > 0 and, off the atom zones, a largest D - C of -1.847411e-13 at x = 0.540; the registered prediction that this maximum lies next to the origin failed by the letter. A certificate with windowed sums and a capped bisection is running (q1839) and will be recorded in a later amendment.

Claims (apply_claims_strengthen.py and _b.py). The abstract now says that all twenty-four ring losses predicted in advance fell inside their registered bands. It says that the settings of the series law were fitted to twenty known capacity events, and that three later blocks were predicted before computation. Section IV-A gives the count law for the capacity with L = A + beta/2 and its range over 2666 stored states. It gives the closed form (6/pi^2)^(1/6) of the ratio to the Abbott-Machta constant. Four numbers are bound to amendment 2243 (bind_claims_cl1.py), and amendments 2243 and 2244 are now read as computation records by the number gate. The title spells out nonparametric maximum likelihood (apply_title_decision.py; repository README likewise).

Readability.

Citations. The registry writing/citation_registry.json has 62 entries: QUOTE 32, ATTRIBUTED 24, POINTER 5, COUNT 1. Two sentences changed on the way. Appendix C now says what Barletta and Dytso illustrate about D'(0+) < 0 for even K, where it had said that this case occurs only shortly before a birth. Section II now derives B(pi) = d - I(p_pi) from Tweedie's formula, Stein's identity and an integration by parts, and cites Robbins and Brown only for the Tweedie form of the Bayes estimator. Texts of Fomin and Zelevinsky (arXiv math/9912128) and of two papers on Neville elimination were fetched from arXiv into papers/cit. The publisher sites of Smith (1971) and Brown (1971) refused automated access, and these works are cited through local texts that state their results.

Pipeline. The build after these changes ended with exit 0 and check_all R1 to R6, R8 and R9 at 0, R7 at 4.

## Amendment 2246 (2026-10-13 22:22) - the exact stationary state of K = 40, A = 29.85 is certified to be the capacity-achieving input, so the total positivity of X holds at that optimum; notation of the merged paper; the reader version of the public repository and its gate; executed record

Scope.

Readings 288 and 289. The first optimality certificate q1839 bounded D - C over boxes of [0, A] at 128 bits around the Krawczyk box of reading 285. Run 1 stopped at its cap of 200000 boxes: all failed boxes lie inside the zone of one atom, where the test D'' < 0 cannot pass because D'' changes sign there; P1 failed by the letter, and P2 and P3 held. Run 2 failed 82 boxes of width about 1.5e-6 that contain an atom and was stopped by its process number. The reading q1840 shows why. As a point value, D'' at the 19 positive atoms is certainly negative, from -1.4606e-10 at the innermost atom to -0.021840 at the outermost. A ball evaluation of D'' over a box of width 1.5e-6 has a radius of about 9.76e-6 whatever the width, because the sum cancels terms as large as |log Q|. Its P1 held and its P2 failed by the letter.

Reading 290. The certificate q1841 uses D(x) - C = G(A) - G(x) with G(x) the integral of phi(y - x) log Q(y), whose derivatives are integrals of Hermite polynomials times phi(y - x) log Q(y). Point values carry the accuracy and a box enters only through a remainder of order six. Every derivative is widened by an error bound of 1.131e-31 (window tail of the order-six terms; the strip part is 3.27e-129). All 19 atom zones pass (0 failed, smallest half-width 9.766e-05), the wall zone passes with half-width 0.05, and 1203 boxes are used in all, with no gap box failed and none left. The largest upper bound of D - C over the gap boxes is -3.5600e-19, error bound included. P1 and P3 held. P2 failed by the letter: the registered bar for the error bound was 1e-100, and the bound is 1.131e-31. With reading 285, the initial minors of X are certainly positive at the exact capacity-achieving input of this state. The other 93 states of Section VIII and the proof text in the paper are open.

Reading 291 (claim B3, the strip constant). The scalar case of the dual upper bound printed by Dytso, Goldenbaum, Poor and Shamai and the entropy-power inequality with a uniform input give sqrt(4A^2 + 2 pi e) <= e^(C+h_1) <= 2A + sqrt(2 pi e) for every A > 0. So a limit beta of e^(C+h_1) - 2A lies in [0, sqrt(2 pi e)] if it exists. The reading q1842 found the three stored states inside this sandwich, the measured beta = 3.98160794709 inside [0, 4.13273135412], and e^(C+h_1) - 2A - beta between -4.247e-9 and 6.204e-13 for A from 20.374 to 51.513; its P1 to P3 held. Section III-A now states this two-sided bound after the strip law, with the upper bound cited as equation (12) of Thangaraj, Kramer and Boecherer and the lower bound from the entropy-power inequality; a registry entry quotes their text (apply_strip_sandwich.py, backup gates/unified_before_sandwich.tex).

Reading 293 (claim B3, a lower bound from the uniform input). For X uniform on [-A, A] the output density is F/(2A) with F(y) = Phi(y + A) - Phi(y - A). So h(X + Z) = log 2A - (1/(2A)) int F log F exactly, and e^(C+h_1) is at least 2A exp(-(1/(2A)) int F log F) for every A. The reading q1845 found this equal to 2A e^(kappa/A) within 2.4e-32 at A = 10, 20 and 30, with kappa = -int Phi log Phi = 0.90319728556862535363. Hence the limit inferior of e^(C+h_1) - 2A is at least 2 kappa = 1.80639; its P1 and P2 held, and P3, which predicted more than half of the measured beta, failed by the letter (2 kappa is 0.454 beta).

Reading 292 and a batch run (claim B2 at the exact states of Section VIII). The reading q1843 rebuilt the list of 94 distinct states from the five recorded state lists (95 files, one duplicate). Of these, 91 carry the verdict OPTIMAL, and 3 are stationary states beyond the end of their family, at K = 40, 70 and 80. Its run 1 ended VOID on a number stored as the string np.float64(...), and run 2 held P1 to P3. The driver q1844 runs the same chain unchanged on each of these states, in a fresh process per state: the zero-free strip, the error bounds, the Krawczyk box with the minors of X over it, and the Taylor-model certificate. Its predictions were registered in its docstring before the start, and its result will be recorded in a later amendment.

The NPMLE edge defect is written D_N, so that D keeps one meaning. The shift of the mass-scaling law is written a_w, and the text says that it equals beta/2 of Table I to the digits shown. The masses of that sentence are written w_j, as in Section VIII. The half-widths of the first LFP and NPMLE events are written m and R, as in Section II. Public repository. The trigger list of the public material has a new class for wording about how the work was organised: instructions, audit lines, task names of the work list, helper programs, readings of drafts, and the first person singular. The class feeds both the gate of the public log (G2) and the scan of every other file of the repository; in Python files it is checked on comments and docstrings only. ## Amendment 2247 (2026-10-13 22:51) - a lower bound of the strip constant from three atoms at each end, certified in ball arithmetic; executed record

Scope.

Reading 294. For an input made of Lebesgue measure on [-A+g, A-g] and atoms of masses nu_k at plus or minus (A + s_k), normalised, the output entropy is log M - (1/M) int G_A log G_A exactly, with M = 2A + 2(sum nu_k - g). The limit of e^(h(X+Z)) - 2A is B = 2(sum nu_k - g - E) with E = int G log G, G(t) = Phi(-g - t) + sum nu_k phi(t - s_k), so the limit inferior of e^(C+h_1) - 2A is at least B. The optimiser q1846 ended VOID in run 1 on an overflow of exp; the audit found a drift along a flat direction (gap to zero) with B finite, and the clip at plus or minus 40 binds only there. Run 2 held P1 to P3 and gave B = 3.9320969183, 3.9767131096 and 3.9796646221 for one, two and three edge atoms; four atoms gave no more. The gate q1847, written before these numbers were read, ended FAIL by the letter: it compared the unrounded optimiser value with the value of the printed configuration (difference 4.8e-12, bar 1e-12). The gate q1848 evaluates the printed configuration only and printed PASS.

Edge configuration of the bound: g = 4.361045; atoms (s, nu) = (0, 3.49413), (-2.68983, 2.25076), (-4.36104, 0.62400); ball of B = [3.979664622053985264996123 +- 4e-46]; measured beta minus B = 0.00194332503601474.

Reading 295. The certificate q1849 integrates G log G on [-40, 40] with the certified integrator of python-flint at 160 bits and bounds the two tails in closed form (together below 1.7e-175). Its first selftest ended VOID on the positive control, which asked the ball of 2 kappa to contain a 20-digit decimal that is coarser than the ball. The control was changed to a distance below 1e-19; the other criteria were not changed, and the change is in the docstring. The run printed the ball of B above (radius 3.99e-46) and VERDICT q1849: PASS. The limit inferior of e^(C+h_1) - 2A therefore exceeds 3.97966, and the measured beta lies less than 0.002 above it.

Three gaps in the earlier chain. The earlier exact-state chain (q1855, q1856, q1836, q1857) had certified the optimal states of Section VIII. None of the omitted terms is larger than 1e-300 and the margins are far larger, but each is a gap in a proof.

What happened. The control state of 2255 ran first (small_gap_q206/q1891_control_K61.txt). E1, E2, P and the in-run negative control held. Its verdict line reads PASS, with dw_0/dA = 0.240950135296 +- 3.92e-13 and du_1/dA = 5.67387312489 +- 7.02e-13. The selftest of 2255 then printed VOID and SELFTEST: FAIL (small_gap_q206/q1891_selftest.txt).

Why the VOID is real. The selftest replaced the whole forcing b by -b. The system is linear in b, so every du_i/dA changes sign too. The positive control then reads a certainly negative du_i/dA and returns VOID before the FAIL branch is reached. The selftest as registered could never read FAIL, so it fails by the letter. The defect is in the control, not in the solve.
